review_text:
Not located in Manhattan, but in Queens, a few blocks from the Aqueduct race track, but very much worth the trip. About seven years ago a friend of mine kept talking about this 'Italian place' in queens like it was some mythical place, like Xanadu. One day we skipped work early (WTC 1) and went off to queens. I couldn't believe how good it was. If you like big chunks of roasted garlic, like me, this is THE place. Roasted peppers, big cutlets of sausage, roasted chicken covered in olive oil and vinegar, served 'family style'.
The restaurant itself is about as warm and inviting as a 7 Eleven, but the food makes up for any lapse in lousy decor'...

If you and a few friends have an afternoon to kill, hop into the car and make a trip out here. It will become a favorite of yours too...

So, you walk in the door, make sure you bring cash because these wise-guys don't bother with credit cards. You walk past the table with the guys with the pinkie rings and shiny suits and sit down and try not to make eye-contact with them.  You leave them alone, they'll leave you alone.......Anyway, Baked Clams, Scapparella, Chicken Parm, garlic bread, Zuppa De Clams or mussels, Osso Buco......This is my favorite Italian restaurant on the planet and if you are ever in Brooklyn near JFK, you have to go.  Bring cash and leave your gun at home.  
Dishes are posted on a black-board and everything is served family style on big oval plates to share. 
The Scapparella is bone-in chicken pieces tossed with onions, bell peppers, garlic chunks and potatoes and all roasted in the oven and slip on to the plate...amazing
Imagine chicken parmesan pounded thin then pan-fried until the breading is tender and crispy with only a wisp of sauce brushed on top and sprinkled with grated Parmegiano Reggiano., no mozzarella which is a great thing.   
Baked Clams the way they were intended, Garlicky baked breading drizzled with olive oil mixes with the juice of the clam, oh yes.  
Go.....enjoy.

This place will make your head explode!  I guarantee it.  Forget that the restaurant is next to JFK, it is well worth the commute.  Just remember that this is a cash-only, no BS establishment, so walk in, be respectful, take a look at the menu on the big board, order and enjoy.  I can't say enough about this place.  I've noticed people being more lax in dress there lately, but I would recommend not coming in shorts and a t-shirt - lots of special occassions being celebrated there, so don't stand out!

This is the original family style Italian restaurant and it gives credence to the family style.  It is one of the best, if not the best, Italian restaurant in queens and even though it's right by JFK, it is so worth the trip.  The baked clams here are amazing and the best I've ever had.  Their broccoli rabe is not too bitter and is very tasty while their salad is great.  But enough of the light stuff; let's get right down to the nitty gritty.  The veal parmesean and chicken parmeasan here are amazing while the eggplant is also delicious.  The pastas are great, especially the linguine with clams and the shrimp luciano.  Both outstanding dishes packed with flavor.  And you will be full by the end of this meal.  Guaranteed.  The Chicken Chinese is also great.  For dessert, they go with cannollis, tiramisu, sorbet and biscotti, which are all so good.  Of course, this is if you have any room left.  Enjoy this and don't head over to olive garden when you could have a real family-style italian dinner.

Come here with a group of hungry people as the portions are huge! The staff are very knowledgeable so when in doubt, take their advice. The baked clams are the best i've had anywhere, and i really love the way they do their veal parm. The decor is not that great, more for famiies, friends, business than a romantic date place. Just remember, cash only.

came here on a recent NYC trip, based upon yelp and location. Friends were driving to meet from Long Island. We were staying near JFK. 

Agree decor is secondary, Sat. night was jammed, we were seated after a 20 minute wait, thre's no bar, and hardly a spot to sit and wait. 

Service was excellent, I don't remember a menu at the table, we studied a far wall, got recommendations from a thick accented local. Dishes were family style, plenty of food for party of 6. 

All in all food and house wine were excellent, only complaint was the seafood marinara, lots of calamari and squid, no shrimp or scallops. 

Also, seems overpriced,  $300 for food for 6, 2 bottles of wine plus tip. 

One other thing, after we spoke favorably about Obama 2 of our party noticed the waiter did not serve the rest of our meal, it was serve yourself from then on, hmmmmmm.

Don Pepe's is what Italian food dreams are made of. The downside is the cash only part of the business, but the homemade wine, delightful bread and scrumptious baked clams.... these folks are NOT afraid of garlic and I love them for that. :) :) :) Seriously, we consider it a big night out when we can get to Don Pepe's... who cares about Canal street and little italy's over-rated italian joints? We'll skip those anyday and head to Don's. The staff is always attentive, witty and sarcastic - thank you Don Pepe's for keeping it real.

had: baked clams and Linginlie w/ clams... lots of garlic... yummy... soaked in oil... did i mention yummy??? al dente... reminded me of italian food when i was in italy... Family style... go w/ a few ppl so u can try diff food... best baked clams EVER... yummy.... Cash only... long wait... don't bother to go if you are watching your weight :)

Overall a pretty bad experience. 

Decided to go here for dinner with four people. Pull up to the restaurant and needed to find parking. You must park on the street and it is usually a pain to find parking anywhere in the area. Walked in and had to wait which was no big deal. We were told half an hour but it was actually about 15 minutes. I guess that is this places only saving grace. Unfortunately the waiting area is just a glass room facing the street where everyone stands. 

While waiting it was brought to my attention that it is cash only. No problem, they must have an ATM then. Wrong. The ATM is next door at a supermarket. So I run over to the ATM to take out some money. Of course the ATM in the supermarket is broke. So I have to resort to buying a pack of gum and getting cash back from the supermarket cash register. Obviously the supermarket limits you to $50 cash back. Good thing I had some cash on me or I would have had to end the night there. 

So we finally go in and sit down. There are no menus. The menu is posted on the wall as far away as possible from the table we were sitting at. Also they post the menu at just the right height so people walking by, and sitting in front of it block anyone else from reading it. 

Decided on something simple. Mozzarella and tomatoes for an appetizer and spaghetti and meat sauce for the meal. How can you screw that up? The menu is fairly small and is just typical Italian food like pasta, chicken parmesan, etc... Nothing special. The appetizer was great but $21 ($14 times 1.5. More on that later)  for some cheese and tomatoes is pretty expensive. The pasta came out and was al dente. Too hard for my taste. After we ate we decided on some dessert. They were out of almost everything so we just got whatever they had left. 

Another concern is the family style pricing. We were four people so they just "adjust" the portions. They said well give you 1.5 servings (or in other words well just charge you 1.5x the price).

Best place ever!  Don't expect white glove service or fancy decor.  DO expect the best baked clams ever.  Follow with linguini (always cooked perfectly) with shrimp Luciano and finish with Veal Don Peppe (pounded veal chop, fried with chopped onions and tomatoes).  One of the best meals on the planet!  The Broccoli Rabe and chopped salad get honorable mention.

Not  fancy...but good

BEST BAKED CLAMS EVER...ive been eating them since i was 2

no menus, its on the wall...so be prepared for a casual dining experience

im a fan

This place was awesome. When I first got there I felt like I was in an episode of the Sopranos but once I got passed that I really enjoyed my meal. There are no menus except a board on the wall. I started with their red house wine that for $18 a bottle was a great deal. Had the baked clams as an appetizer and let me just say they were delicious. then I had spaghetti and the chicken Don Peppe which was a chicken cutlet topped with tomatos and onions. Make sure you bring cash since they don't take credit cards. I can't wait to go back

My 2 Favorite Italian places to eat will always be the Parkside in Corona and Don Peppe in south Ozone Park queens......Don Peppe is a real relaxed setting and not very fancy shamsy BUT the food there is pretty much the Best around anywhere in NYC's 5 Boroughs..... Ive been going there for years now and the quality is still as top notch as my first visit years ago....All the waiters are friendly and helpful but my favorite is Marco .  He makes ya feel right at home and loves a good joke too....As for the food....Momma Mia......You must start your meal with a dozen Baked clams that melt in your mouth....For my money the best pasta in the place is the Linguine with white clam sauce  OR the Shrimp Luciano over linguine.....Whatever you choose will be a HIT.....My favorite main course is the Veal Don Peppe which is tender fried veal cutlet with chopped tomatoes and onions on top.....Enjoy a bottle of house red Wine and a espresso afterwards and you have a meal you wont soon forget........SEE YA THERE......PHIL

Everything here is served family style. I went here sort of knowing this. I took my 2 year old and my father in law and went 8 months pregnant in the pouring rain. My husband got called into work last minute, but I was dying to go here. I ordered the Lobster Fra Diavlo. The lobster was more than 5lbs and the sauce wasn't spicy at all, tasted gross actually. The service is rude and the place is loud and simply stinks

So one day I was at JFK after a long flight, started talking to some fellow passengers while I was waiting for my luggage and they asked where they should go for dinner for their first night in the NY. 
What did I tell them? 
 UMM HELLO DON PEPPE!  HAnds DOWN.  This is my all time favorite restaurant in the world.  If I could have my rehearsal wedding party here I would. (my wedding is in another state!)   I salivate thinking of a dinner there. I go here for all of my birthdays, and make up excuses to go to Queens to go there!  Here is what you should order: (not in any order) 

(oh bring at least 3 other people with you) 
1. Start with the house salad 
2. Chicken Don Peppe
3.  Any pasta
get dessert! YUM YUM YUM! 
oh and wine-- red or white! both are great! 
4.  if you can handle dessert , try them! yum!

don't ask for plain coffee, they will send you across the street! hahah!
Get the cappachino!  if you can eat/drink any more!)

Don Peppe is the best New York Style ( and maybe Soprano style) Italian restaurant in my opinion. I usually avoid non-authentic Italian places, but this one, I am addicted to. My recommendations are the white clam sauce linguine and the Veal Don Pepe. These will "wow" ya!
Remember to bring lots of cash with you since it is a cash only restaurant.

http://bit.ly/9msGwD
Finally made it to Queens to take pics of my 5 favorites at Don Peppe.
Link will bring you to my blog post.
In short: There's no better old-line Italian around.

Best South Italian this side of Dominicks in the Bronx. Maybe a little higher in price, and in quality of the food, but you won't go broke here. And there is actually a menu with prices posted on the far wall, and table cloths on the individual tables.  

Three of us shared the stuffed artichoke appetizer (gigantic), the calamari in marinara sauce (very tender) and the chicken scarpariello (plenty of garlic, olive oil, and red peppers). Very delicious, and priced just right - less than $60 total.

Things to watch out for - unless you tell the waiter to serve you otherwise, the seemingly house-made red wine (no tax stickers on the unmarked bottles) is good, but served cold (!). No olive oil to dip your bread in , even upon request. Drinks, the espresso (no regular coffee), and desserts can quickly  double the bill. Go to your local Friendly's after the main courses.

Another caution - hats are not permitted, per the sign at the entrance! When I asked the 'bouncer' seated just inside about this, he replied cryptically 'This is a restaurant.' It's exchanges like that that make  restaurants such as this a lot more interesting to visit than any plain old 5 Star establishment.  

No credit cards, but the attentive service and delicious food will make you ready to return. Good choice if you're flying in or out of JFK, and well worth the trip in any event.

Delicious!  A must go!  We had a stuffed artichoke and baked clams that are as good as any we've ever had (three could share), caprese (mozzarella on a tomato with balsamic) with a slice of roasted pepper on top (really, really great and unique!), and the Shrimp Luciano is the star of the show!!!!  It is incredible shrimp over linguini with an amazing creamy sauce!  A must have!  We even had the veal don peppe which is like a breaded veal cutlet with a bruschetta topping.  Yummmmmm!  

It's cash only, street parking, no reservations, no website, no printed menu so know the items on the wall are what they call a half order (for two people) so for a foursome they will double the cost, a line to get in (on a Saturday night), full of hustle bustle in the one big room, and it's no hats (for you Kangol lovers).   

The food and the service are well worth it.  A very New York-style place.

Saw an older italian gentleman go right up to a table as they were nursing their 2nd cup of coffee and told them that it was time to leave as he needed the table. They jumped out of their seat, didn't say a word and were out the door before you could say "put em' in the bathroom" (random bronx tale reference). 

Gold standard for authentic Italian food in NYC.

Family style menu is on the wall. My favorite is the Shrimp Luciano (Shrimp sauteed with linguine and chopped onions in a vodka sauce with a little kick to it).

No Hats.

Credit....fugheddaabouittt...Crisp, Clean $100 Bills

Parking....after 7 the meters expire on the street, you'll be ok.

The portions here are family style.....4 servings per plate on average.

Try not to stare in one direction too long...when it doubt, look straight down.

don peppe is the best family style italian rest. in the nyc and surrounding areas, hands down!  the decor inside may be dated, they dont accept credit cards, and its location isnt the best, but if you want good italian food this is the place.  i challenge anyone who disputes this places food.  they wont kiss your ass when you come in but if you're a friendly, courteous diner(unlike many NYer's) the staff will treat you with great respect and help you decide what you might like.  if you are going out to lunch or dinner with the intention of eating great food and being a fatso like me, then go here.  you wont be disappointed!

now this place is by far on its own level no other place in new york can compete with don peppes baked clams , roasted red pepps with garlic n oil, and oman the shrimp luciano if the dish was made out of bread id fold it up and eat that as well . you will not find one dish made bad in don peppe as i said its on its own level .

When it comes to Italian food I am a little hard to please.  I tend to compare the sauce to my grandma's and there is no comparison.  So I guess I am a little biased even before i taste the food.  Growing up I enjoyed eating a lot of home cooked Italian meals, almost to a fault since now I try to avoid Italian food when going out.  Its not that I dislike Italian food in fact  it is a comfort food for me and i make home cooked Italian food at least once a week.  So when i go out to eat i want something different.  After saying that Don Pepe's is most likely my favorite place to eat Italian in NYC.  The place is very modest looking, (kind of reminds me of my grandpas basement) the menu is on the wall, (very weird) the stereotypes are ubiquitous here, its right out of a Scorsese film.  Now to get to the essence of the place, the food, it takes a while for the chef to cook (this means it fresh), and its a little expensive, but the portions are big (family style).  The pasta we had was amazing and perfectly al dente, the sauce, a very light  garlic, olive oil & tomato, was mouth watering.  The shrimp Luchiano was another big hit, but the braciola was average, it lacked a flavorful stuffing.  All in all a great experience and worth the money.  This is my go to spot when i get that rare craving for Italian food out.

Truly amazing food. Im still salivating over the baked clams.

The linguine in clam sauce was recently featured on the Food Network, and rightly so. It has all of the old world dining charm without any of the airs. Its bare bones, amazing food done perfectly right.

I eat here quit often.... EVERYTHING on the menu is delish!  Aside from the cash only the only downside to this place would be the decor.  It's defin. a casual dining experience as the decor has not changed from the early 80's.. i recommend to anybody that know what true good ital food is!!  Mangia!!!!

Family style, amazing clam sauce the red and white together out of this world. Menu is on the wall, broke my neck trying to read it. Beware, the waiters and owners think they mafia. lol really, quite disturbing. But, they must slice the garlic so thin, it liquefies. Parking is ok. I would go there on a date

After a long day of travel from L.A., my cousin picked us up from JFK and I had a serious hunger that needed satisfying. My dad suggested this spot, once favored by the Teflon Don himself, John Gotti. It's not in the greatest of neighborhoods, but consider it a gem among the rough. We arrived and found the place mostly empty. An Italian gentlemen took us to our seats and we began the feast. 

The menu is printed on the wall, and it's huge. Everything here is served family style, so don't let the high prices scare you off too much since the portions are made out for at least 2 people or more. We started off with the baked clams. Our waiter, a very nice, exceedingly attentive gentleman from Italy, scooped a few onto each of our plates. Each clam was cooked with bread crumbs and butter - the combination of crunch with the soft flesh of the clam was fantastic. I could have eaten them all night. Up next was a plate of (huge) stuffed mushrooms. Again, they were outstanding. Our pasta dish was the linguine aioli, but this wasn't the same olive oil and garlic crap you get at the Olive Garden. This was the REAL DEAL authentic Italian style, with just the right amount of bite and mammoth chunks of cooked garlic strewn throughout. It was honestly some of the best pasta I've ever eaten at a restaurant - ever. The closest I can recall to eating something this good was made by my relatives - you just can't find good food like this anywhere. At this point, my stomach was crying for mercy, but we still had one last entree to go: Chicken Scarapello aka Chicken Scrap. I desperately wanted to devour all the fowl in front of me, but I only managed to get down a couple pieces before my body warned me that proceeding further might be hazardous. Oh, was it good, though. Succulent chicken chunks baked and seasoned with some Italian spices - at least I was able to package it up for eating later. 

Come hungry, that's all I can say. The food is outstanding, some of the best I've eaten. Even somewhere like Maggiano's, which is comparable in terms of portion size and comes close to crafting authentic Italian cuisine, can't hold a candle to this spot. Be warned, they are a CASH ONLY joint, so come ready. Your bill can easily soar to over $100, make sure you're loaded before walking in the door.
This is my favorite family style restaurant.. food is excellent.. i love the house red wine!!

I've been coming here with my family for the past 10 years, and it hasn't changed. 

They have the BEST baked clams in the world. My favorite dishes here are: 
Veal (or you can get chicken) Don Peppe
Baked Clams
Linguini with White Clam Sauce

TO DO FOR! This place is still great as it was 10 years ago.... the service is great, but it's cash only. My mouth waters everytime I think of this place. Sooo good. You gotta like garlic to come here. Yummmmy!

if you're looking for the best linguine in clam sauce - featured in "the best thing i ever ate".... this place is legit. 
if you're also looking for a place where bus boys have sparking clean white shirts (which is impossible to do with marinara sauce flying everywhere)...  buttoned to the very least possible with their wife beaters showing, you'll find it here.
if you're looking to be the only non-italian and to be seated after all of the italian "friends" and/or "cousins"... also here.

in summary: the food is amazing. the service... not so much.

here's what we ordered: (6 people)
2 - linguine in clam sauce (olive oil and butter galore, delicious and not creamy)
1 - baked ziti (average... i could pass)
1 - don peppe salad (fresh tasting and already dressed)
1 dozen - baked clams (topped with lots of bread crumbs and butter, Yum)
1 - stuffed mushrooms (stuffed with pureed vegetables, bread crumbs and marinara sauce)
1 - chicken don peppe (best surprise of the meal, awesomely breaded, topped with refreshing tomatoes, red onions and basil)
1 - veal parm (eh.. i'm not that big of a fan of veal, too mushy)
1 - tiramisu (better at other places)
1 - tartufu (good but not my thing)
1 - cannoli (good but better at other places)
1 - lemon sorbet (awesome! it's lemon sorbet served in a giant costco size frozen lemon... so good)
2 - table red wine - pretty good

everything was cheap (CASH ONLY) and we'll definitely come back. BUT... either before 6 pm or after 10pm. It's packed and there is definitely a long wait.

next time we'll definitely try the chicken chinese :)

We just got back from a wonderful dinner with very good friends (we were there about 20 years ago and decided to try it again).  None of us were dissapointed!  Everything is soooo wonderful and all served family style.  They make their own red wine (great).  We started with the "BEST" baked clams, then thanks to other reviews, had the linguine in clam sauce (OMG), then as we've had in the past, the chicken parmagania and the veal chops -- to die for!!
GREAT food, good service, reasonable prices, and good company.  You can't ask for anything more!!!

Reasons why I love Don Peppe:
1. Grilled portobello mushrooms in a saucy balsamic vinaigrette? (this dish is not on the menu but ask for it, and they will know exactly what it is you want. it's amazing - taste, texture, everything!)
2. Baked clams
3. Linguine in white clam sauce
4. Veal Don Peppe
6. Lemon sorbet (smooth and creamy sorbet served out of a lemon)
5. Feeling welcome

I love unpretentious restaurants that serve amazing food for reasonable prices. I love family style. I love that we don't usually have to wait too long to be seated here - so I'm selfishly hoping that Don Peppe will remain a little-known neighborhood gem.

After hearing rave reviews about Don Pepe's from a friend, my other half and I decided to give it a try this past Friday.  We were surprised at how close it was at only an 8min drive.  We were disappointed to find there was only street parking but did snag a spot after circling for about 5min. 

 We arrived about 8pm and were surprised to see the dining room only a quarter of the way full, mostly with families.  I may be wrong but most of the patrons seemed Italian, which to me was a good sign.   We were seated immediately at a table of our choice.  

Our friendly waiter, Karl, came right over and explained how our dining experience would go.  The menu is located on the back wall and all dishes are served family style.   The menu didn't have a huge variety, but it covered the necessary bases!  We did get a bottle of the house wine (red) which was ok, not the best but decent.  We ordered the Linguine w/ Prosciutto, Lemon Chicken and the Veal Don Pepe. The food arrived very quickly and was GREAT!!! everything was delicious and well prepared.  I found the staff very friendly and the entire dining experience enjoyable.  We've made plans already to return!  This was definitely a good find.  

Oh I must say the one downfall (which is no fault of Don Pepe) was the Coked-out man sitting at the next table (not right next to us but a few empty tables down)   He was a mess! fidgety, no shoes on, talking loud and doing the coke sniff all night.  He was entertaining at first then a tad annoying.  Luckily his party soon after our food arrived!

I never liked veal or baked clams before coming here but after trying the Veal Don Pepe, it's changed me because I LOVE it and I'm eating clams, which I've never done before. This place is my second favorite Italian restaurant (#1 authentic). My friends and I always order the same things every time we come (baked clams, portobello mushrooms, linguini with clam sauce, veal don pepe) that when I went just this Saturday night (probably my 6th time), the waiter said "I know, I know, the Chinese menu" jokingly since I guess he recognizes us by now. Hehe.

Compared to the rest of these "family style" italian joints, this is hands down the best.  The pounded out veal with bruchetta (Veal Don Pepe) and linguine with white clam sauce are tops.   Dont forget the baked clams and the italian cheescake.

If you have never been and someone wants to go, take them up on the offer!

CASH ONLY!


There are only two other places in the tri-state that you can kind of compare (fyi - non are on arthur ave!). 
1) Matteos
2) La Parma

Best Italian joint around.

Must try:

Veal Don Peppe
Baked Clams
Mussels
Linguini w/ clam sauce or garlic and oil

It doesn't get any better than the legendary Don Peppe's. The best Italian restaurant I've had the pleasure of dining in, worldwide. So simple yet so perfect. Better than the high end Italian spots in the city and absolutely worth the trip out to Lefferts Boulevard. First meal I had after living abroad for 5 months, if you want the best go to Don Peppes.

What you need to have:

-Bottle of House Red
-Bottle of House White
-Don Peppe House Salad
-Two dozen baked clams
-Stuffed mushrooms
-Shrimp Luciano over Linguini
-Veal Don Peppe


Get about three loaves of bread and dip into the sauces that accompany the baked clams and shrimp luciana. The sauces are worth the trip alone. Laid back dress code in this classic NY Italian staple, one of the last remaining. 

No reservations, Cash Only, my favorite restaurant on this massive planet
Really enjoyed the food...great fra diavlo, awesome Marsala, and the garlic bread was perfect...nothing fancy, just awesome home cooked family style food...a definite must!!!

First if you want to eat at this restaurant call the place first because it gets pack in there.
Cash only, no baby strollers allowed inside.
Street parking near the residences. The waiters are all men. The menu is written on the wall. When my husband & I went there for the first time we asked the waiter who took care of us which he would recommend. We ordered what he just said: mussels and some tomato sauce(i dont know the name of it on the list) and spaghetti with white clam sauce. Yum! slurp!
The waiter brings the food one at a time not all together and then they serve the food for you as in they will put the food on your plate.
Dessert we had cannoli and cappuccino. My husband and I enjoyed it!

Cant wait to go back there!
Very good italian food.  Can't complain except for the location and the decor.  I really don't care about the latter if the food is well made and taste good.
Family style Italian....Almost as good as Moms.  Worth the trip from Jersey.  We make it a point to stop here when we fly out of JFK.   Veal Don Pepe ..enough for 4!   Autentico Italiano!

I honestly didn't expect much from this restaurant even after getting recommendations from a friend; however, after the linguine and white clam sauce and some of Don Peppe's famous baked clams, I have to say I am a big fan. I highly recommend this place for some awesome Italian food and look forward to making a return trip.

Best Italian food in Queens.
Must try: 
Don Peppe salad
Baked Clams
Roasted pepper
Veal Don Peppe
Shrimp with pasta
Stuffed artichokes
Chinese chicken and of course House wine

Hands down, the best Italian food EVER!!!!

Roasted peppers!!!!OMG
Soooo good!!!

I absolutely love this place.... great and authentic Italian food. I love the waiters here because they are all so old school and sarcastic it's just great! Now lets talk food ....absolutely everything is delicious here! My favorites include: 
baked clams ------- the best I ever had! 
mussels- always fresh and tasty 
the don peppe salad- lettuce so crunchy, roasted peppers, olives, tomatoes, onions- perfect 
eggplant rollotini- eggplant baked with ricotta --- Love love love 
veal done peppe - veal breaded with tomatoes and onions on top - BEST thing here! 
chicken with garlic simply amazing! 
shrimp with garlic and pink sauce - yum yum yum 
pasta- the portions are huge and the pasta o so authentic 
Remember the portions here are huge and family style! 
So take the family and friends and enjoy a meal you will not forget!

The servce was great. We had the chicken breast w eggplant, chicken don peppe, n broccolli. Yum. The glass for soda was small n the soda was flat. The ac was on blast. There was no music. The bathroom could smell btr n the dollar store cutlery needs to be upgraded. i expected it to be nicer based on their prices.... Nevertheless, the food tasted great

I've been here twice with a group of friends.  Both times was a Saturday evening and there was a 45 minute wait.  The place was jam packed with tables and quite loud.

Decor:  Nothing to write home about, but who cares?
Service:  Hit or miss.  Last time we got a crotchety older guy.  Meh.
But the food is really, really good...

Baked Clams - great

Stuffed Mushrooms - great

Shrimp Oreganata - EXCELLENT

Linguine w/white clam sauce - EXCELLENT

Steak Pizzaiole - this is a HUGE steak, covered in tomato sauce, but EXPENSIVE, for me not worth the $60-$70 pricetag

"Chinese" Chicken - tasty...bone-in chicken pieces in tomato sauce - if you want it, you have to be order it as soon as you walk in

Escarole - not bad, but needed salt, which is strange since all the other dishes are quite salty

their desserts are from a frozen chain, so decent, but not fantastic.

Worst Italian food I ever ate!  Baked clams were the size of a nickel in
a water sauce  (we had ordered two dozen, a real rip off)...linguini and clam sauce had tons of chunks of garlic but no clams that were noticeable...shrimp luciano was boiled shrimp in
pink water....and veal parmigiano was tough and tasteless..
tables were one on top of another and we kept getting bumped,
restaurant was very noisy to boot!
Would never recommend, would never go back...think they are just
busy living off the past  or else diners don't get out much..

Love, love, love how delicious the food is here and how they do it family style and in family portions! I wouldn't suggest going here with any less than 4 people.. I've been here 3 times (will be back for many more) and have left with a satisfied belly every time. My favorite of their dishes are the baked clams, linguini in clam sauce, portabello mushrooms, the veal don peppe.. and even the don peppe salad was good. From beginning to end, every experience at Don Peppe was one that tops the last!!
you can not write A review of Don Peppe. just go and see for yourself. its the Best Restaurant Around...

Had a fantastic meal here with family. There is a real neighborhood vibe to this place, with virtually no atmosphere. There is one menu, and it is on the wall. When we asked for wine, we got a chilled bottle of red without a label and we drank several.

We don't do a lot of heavy eating so the family style portions-generous portions- worked perfectly for our table. We had a salad, fried peppers, pasta in meat sauce, chicken in lemon and butter, and the veal don peppe.plenty of food for 7 people. 

Not much to say about service-it was gruff, but pleasant.

Over an hour wait! on a Sunday...Waiter was great.. Very Noo Yawk!.. We started with the baked clams.. waiter suggested 2 orders, which we did.. very tasty.. and very small clams.... had better.... D Peppes Chicken, very good.. a little too much chopped tomatoes...the baked ziti.. was pasta with some sauce and a little melted cheese.. would not order...Bread was ehh.. not hot.. and would have been nice to have some olive oil to dip...went there, as we heard it on Entorouge. but .. once is enuf..  big hype since the mention on Entorouge..... try.. Parkside in Corona.. nicer place for dinner...

Excellent food, considering I had to wait 2hrs to be seated. The inside didn't look anything special, but being that I was starving at that point, it really wasnt an issue. I was disappointed when I found out it was family style because there were six of us, but when we realized how much food we actually got,i was stuffed once I finished my appetizer. You definately get your moneys worth, and the food does taste like authentic Italian food. At the end,i was satisfied, but next time I'll go during a weekday!

Food was blah, no flavor/spice in fra diavolo. It appeared everything was cooked in the same sauce.....baked clams needed some more baking, waiter threw dishes on the table - dirty ones at that, if the food and services were mediocre at best, the place itself is a complete dump.  This place had its day if ever it should have.  There are plenty of other places in Queens doing a fine job....My two favs are Parkside (Corona) - Flavor, portions and value...and The Olde Tyme Vincent's (Flavor) - Howard Beach.  Skip this one.

This is the best Italian restaurant ever. I have eaten at the best restaurants my whole life, thanks to my father. Let me be clear here with what you will get. This is a no frills or pretentious place.

What you will get is real home cooked Italian food. I was raised in Philly and we have great restaurants too, but nothing like this. I eat at IL Mulino in manhattan, I eat at Martorano cafe in ft lauderdale and I eat really really good. 

I promise you, there is no better place to eat than here. Simple choice, red or white wine? No menus either, look at the board on the wall and make a decision. Hell, throw a dart at it because whatever choice it hits will be outrageous. Actually, I don't even write reviews but I have to for this place. Me and my friends call it the GOAT: the greatest of all time.

PS: my friend that came with me who doesn't eat seafood, said the baked clams I made him eat, are now his favorite dish. Just saying, if you don't know, now you know.

Fantastic food!  Do not be fooled by the no frills, outdated decor- the food is amazing!  The fried eggplant and baked clams are must haves!  There can be a wait so try to go early and bring cash...they don't take credit cards.  It's a great place to bring people from out of town who are looking for delicious, new york, family style Italian food.  Yum!

1st off there is an incredibly long, long wait.  so come early.  we were told 30 min and 1 hr later we finally got seated.  servers are the old school guys with young guys bussing tables. 

 food is quite good.  had the calamari w/pasta - and the calamari was tender and the pasta was al dente.  also had the veal w/eggplant which was delicious.  portions are nicely sized.  they're typical of any family style restaurant we've been to like carmine's.  fortunately what they lack in decor they make up w/in food quality.   would have like the bread to be warmers and fresher but we were so hungry it didn't matter.  the entrees are good.  we watched everyone walk away w/extra food.  we ordered just right for the 3 of us.  

the wait is long - the food is good.  not good to wait longer than you'll be eating though.  plus bring lots of cash.  and be ready to hunt for parking. it's not the easiest of areas to park in.

I really don't know where to even start..... Don Pepe is an institution.. not merely a restaurant..... it is a place where you do feel that the time stands still and that any minute one of the Gambino brothers will walk in with his entourage. The food is very Neapolitan and thus expect tons of mozarella and souce dumped on every dish but that being said.... it all tastes AMAZING!!!!! Worth a visit as these places will not last for long....

I can't believe I never knew about Don pepe!! I came here with my friend and her family for her 23rd birthday.  It was such an awesome place. When i first stepped in I thought "boy what old school" but it only got better.  We got complimentary glasses of red wine and of course delicipus bread. 

I love the family style servings.  Before the ginormous entree we had delicous salad and for appetizer clams orreganato which were delicious.  My absolute favorite was the chicken francais.  It was the best I had tasted, seriously.  

I will be back to try their seafood dishes now that I am a pescetarian!

One of my FAVORITE italian places in new york.  It is a trek but well worth it.  Great for groups since it is family style.  It is cash only though so don't forget to stop by the ATM!!!

What to get:
Baked Clams - These are DELICIOUS.  Make sure you save some bread to sop up the sauce!!!
Linguini with Clam Sauce - Oh my gosh!!  This dish is AMAZING!!
Veal Don Peppe - Heavenly!!  Love it!!!  Great breading and love the fresh tomato/red onion topping!!
Tortoni - I can't believe they have this dessert here!!  Yummy almond ice cream!!!  =)

Service:
Don't expect to get the most polite waiters.  I've had my fair share of rude ones and totally awesome ones.  The food is worth it though!!  The dining area is a very big room with lots of people and noise.  Again, the food is worth it!!  Depending on where you sit, the ceiling fans have the effect of flickering the lighting.  Might be a bit annoying.

I came here with my parents after seeing this featured on Best Thing I Ever Ate...yes, a place in Queens!

A huge plus upon walking in was seeing that it was full on a weekday, and full with Italian families - that's when I knew this place was legit. You order from a menu on the wall (it's quite small to read, so get a table that's nearby if you don't want to get up!), and keep in mind all the dishes are family size.

We ordered the baked clams, linguini with clam sauce, and the veal don peppe.

The linguini with clam sauce is definitely the best I've had at a restaurant - they are extremely generous with the garlic and the clam sauce, which is a wonderful thing. The Baked clams were nice and succulent, but it definitely needed some extra salt. The veal was very tasty too - although I felt it was a bit overpriced for fried meat and some diced tomatoes and basil.

No complaints about the service, and overall this is a good choice for Italian food in queens!

The rating is strictly based on the food. It is that good. However, the decor has seemingly not been updated since it opened up years ago. The waiters also oftentimes are rude and don't really seem to respect the customers that aren't aware of how things work in the restaurant. In any event, this place sure knows how to make food! Some of my favorites are the Don Pepe garden salad, the baked clams, roasted peppers, the breaded veal with diced tomato and onion topped over it, the chicken chinese, and the unbelievably good angel hair pasta! If you come here, make sure to bring lots and lots of cash because they don't take plastic. Mamma Mia, I can't wait to come back!
Awesome grill portobellos, baked clams, linguini with white clam sauce, best ever!

Again another over hyped Italian red sauce and garlic mecca.Overpriced aaverage family style food.To top it off at these prices no CC accepted.
Room was not the cleanest staff adequate but nothing to make a trip for, better food can be found at Gino's on the nearby Crossbay blvd or Bruno s also on Crossbay.

Been going there for 15 years.  First time I went there I was amazed how good it was.  It gets better each time. Bring cash, no credit cards.  Best baked clams you will ever have.  Family style with plenty of food.  Try the stuffed artichoke and shrimp luciano{you will ask for a straw to suck up the sauce}.  Pasta with clam sauce is pure heaven.  Ask for plenty of bread to sop up the sauce. Both the house white and red wine are perfect.   
No reservations so prepare to line up on a saturday night and wait with the rest of us.  It will be worth it.

***DISCLAIMER - LIFELONG PATRON WHO ALMOST BROKE UP WITH MY GIRLFRIEND ON HER FIRST VISIT WHEN HER REACTION WASN'T PURE GASTRONOMICAL BLISS.  GOOD THING I DIDNT, SHE'S MY FIANCE AND NOW FINDS MORE EXCUSES TO GET TO QUEENS THAN ME***

If you are looking to be pampered, move on........if you don't feel like the trip to Queens is worth it for the best Italian food you've ever had, no worries because they will find plenty of loyal patrons who book flights in and out of JFK just so they can use it as excuse to stop off for dinner(yes you can judge me).  

My standard order is -
Baked Clams - Last meal of my life has this as the starter. Get some bread and dip, dip, dip.
Fried Peppers - "That's easy to make".....try it and then try to replicate the dish in your kitchen.
Linguine Red/White Clam Sauce - Apparently the white was on "Best Things I've ever ate" but I usually stick with the red with Shrimp Marinara thrown into the mix.
Veal Don Pep - Veal cutlet topped with tomato, onion, and garlic.

***Keep the bottles of the unlabeled house red wine coming....for $17 how can you go wrong.  It's not Opus One, but like I said, it's $17!!!*** 

Not a stuffed artichoke guy but hear this is delish if you're lucky enough that they haven't sold out of them for the night.

Waiters(all men) will warm up to you if you order like you've been there but they will always let you know if you're ordering too much or not enough.  Just please bring cash as Credit cards will get you directions to the nearest ATM.

If you like Linguine Red/White Clam Sauce then this is the place to go! They make it the best! Baked clams and Salad! They don't take credit cards and won't kiss your ass and the wait can be long at times, but the service is very good and you'll feel your in the middle of a Sopranos tv taping!!!

Cozy atmosphere, very friendly family type of service. Waiters seem to all be old school Italians- anywhere from 17 years of age to 85. I thought the food was good, fresh, but a bit simple. no exciting twists or turns, or amazing flavors, but definitely good hearty Italian grub..i would definitely come back, prices are moderate.
I don't care what the food taste like, they are the rudest people I have ever come across in a service industry.  They should be embarrassed. I was horrified.

Delicious
Garlic bread!!!
 best shrimp scampi on this side of the Mississippi  
pasta with garlic and olive oil A+ goods
peppas and onions very delicate

AMAZING BAKED CLAMS!

Veal don pep, string bean salad, fresh moz, EVERYTHING is great!

This place while the waiter lets you know you are not a priority doesnt quite make up for its lack of service and decor with their food. The baked clams (whole not chopped) were very good, tender and came with a ton of extra sauce to dip their delicious bread in. Then we split the family style size entree of pasta di mare with scallops, mussels, shrimp, and mushrooms. It was pretty good, the scallops were tough and the shrimp were over cooked and stringy. We were much too full for dessert, so we just had espresso and cappuccino (both excellent). When the bill came our server handed a hand written bill directly to me, no check presenter, no thank you, no take your time. He just walked over and gave it to me...oh, and make sure you bring cash. No credit cards accepted.

Just thinking about this place makes my mouth water. The food is absolutely to die for --  whatever you order will be absolutely delicious and authentic, I can guarantee it. I've tried the following dishes veal don peppe, veal parmesan, baked clams, linguine with clam sauce and many others. All the ones I mentioned are my favorites.  The pasta with garlic and olive oil is also delicious.  This place can be a little bit of a pain to get to but is WELL worth the trip for any gastronome.  

The decor inside is hilarious --the walls are chocked full of paintings of the italian countryside. It definitely makes you think that you are in a scene from the Sopranos. 

I've noticed some other reviewers have commented on the surly waiters.  While it is absolutely true that the waiters are a bit standoffish, I think their attitude adds to the charm and feel of the place. This is certainly not a place to go to if you're looking to be pampered.  It is however, the place to go if you're searching for the best italian food you've ever had.

One of my Favorite Italian Joints of all time.

A really great place to with a group. You need a group to be able to order all the great food.

Family Style Plates that are huge.

Baked Clams, Linguini with Clams, Scampi, Veal Don Pepe, Good House Vino, Fresh Salad, Garlic Bread, Broccoli Rabe, Portabella Mushrooms.......just the way a Queens Italian Place should be.

The food, atmosphere, service and patrons are exactly what you want, expect, maybe even dreamed about in a great Queens Italian Family Restaurant.  Big hair, track suits, surly waiters, checked table cloths, generous portions.......It is not a fancy city place with the finest ingredients, but Italian grandma's would be proud.

My biggest problem with Don Pepe is that I don't have enough friends to go and order and eat all my favorites.

We often book flights in/out of JFK to eat here.  You have to be hungry when you go because the portions are big.  The stuffed artichoke had nice garlic, but the excessive bread crumbs made it a little gummy.  We had spaghetti with meat sauce for the kids and it was yummy.  For an entree, we got the chicken chinese.  We made a mistake asking if it was enough. The waiter ordered us a full order, which is too huge for two people.  We got the feeling it was an up-sell to increase the check.  The chicken takes 55 minutes to cook, so decide early if you want it. 

For the kids pasta we wanted a small plate of plain noodles and a small plate with meat sauce.  He said we couldn't. We had to get a full order with meat sauce and a half order of plain.  Again the up-sell.  The pre-meal bread is a nice crusty Italian bread.  

The waiter avoided us like we were from homeland security.
Great food, great service. The baked clams are delicious.. Definitely going back soon..

I don't get what the big deal is. This is a red sauce Italian place, like many others in New York. It looks like it was redecorated in 1987, with rough sort of stucco walls that were popular back then. They kept the old oil paintings that they'd probably had since back in the day, and put them on top, which made for a really weird time period mashup that didn't work. But on to the food.

The baked clams were supposed to be otherwordly. They were not. My guess is that a lot of people have just had baked clams cooked improperly, which is a shame. These were cooked properly and decent, but nothing special. And paying over $1 per clam before tax and tip is a pretty hefty price.

The waiter also recommended the stuffed artichoke. Like the clams, it was fine, but not special. And again, expensive for what it was.

Finally, the linguini with white clam sauce was similarly ok. It was nice and garlicky, and you could taste the clams, but it somehow felt a little bit bland. Underwhelming even.

But what really got me was the service. I received a call on my cell that I didn't take when the artichoke was about halfway finished. It probably took five more minutes to polish it off, and then another 40-45 to get the linguini. They didn't make the pasta from scratch. Last I checked, it doesn't take 40 minutes for dried pasta to cook. Maybe they were catching the clams, and the boat had mechanical problems. We'll never know. Other diners that ordered after us got their food first. No apologies. No reasons given. Our water glasses hit the bottom and our bread basket was empty.

I would not go back here. If anybody asked me about it, I'd tell them not to venture all the way out for it. Let the locals and tourists think that they're getting something marvelous.

One of the best Italian restaurants I've been to except the service really sucked.  I'm not sure if it was because we were one of the only non Italians there that we got bad service but it took almost half an hour for a waiter to come by our table.  The menu is posted on the back wall of the restaurant so if you don't already know it or can't see well, you may have to run to the back to read what they are serving.  I ordered the don pepe salad which had a light vinegar dressing and it was really good.  The baked clams was amazing too and I wish we ordered another dozen.  The linguine with clam sauce was my favorite but the shrimp luciano with lingiune was also very good and it had some spice to it too.  The veal don peppe was also delicious.  The food is family style so make sure to come with a group of people.  If the service was better, I would've given this place 5 stars but the food was so good I would come back.

If you stay with the favorites you cannot go wrong!
Baked Clams.
Linguine White Clam Sauce.
Veal Don Peppe
Etc.
You are going to consume large amounts of olive oil and garlic when you go - but you only live once so start enjoying yourself!

I finally went here after years and years. I heard plenty about it over the years. Being a foodie, I had to try it. I would never go back there again! The food was average. It did not blow me away in the least bit like I hear it does by so many. Then we order a bottle of red wine, and it's put on the table ICE COLD. I said to the waiter, "Why is this bottle cold?" he said "We keep our wine in the freezer" I said "Freezer?, your supposed to store it at 63". Why am I telling this world famous restaurant this? They don't know that ice cold red taste super tannic. Then the places decor is straight from the 90's. Nah N/G man.. Not for me.. You guys want good Italian, go to Contis in Douglaston. There is no better....

this place is straight up gangsta!  must come with large group so you can try a bunch of appetizers and dishes.  they serve their meals family style.  there is quite a wait since they do not take reservations.  get their house red wine (don't know how they make it but it was good!),  don peppe salad (crispy and fresh), stuffed mushrooms, linguine with while clam and garlic! and chicken don peppe!.  need to try the veal don peppe and other pasta dishes the next time I come back.  p.s. cash only

Ok, i've been coming her for years and its easy to give this place a 5 star review.

Servers are friendly.
But food is outstanding. 

Just like everyone else on here, the Clams are always on my order list. Their house salad is off the charts good.

I love their Chicken Scarparello with sausage and peppers too.

And their Red Wine chilled is incredible. Just keep bringing the bottles.

Will recommend this place to everyone and anyone who wants top notch Italian Family style food.

It was my sisters birthday and I wanted to bring my family to a nice family style dinner. I read nothing but rave reviews so I said ..why not?

We went on Superbowl Sunday so it was fairly empty -which was good because I hear it gets crowded. We waited at the front for a few minutes wondering if we sat ourselves or if we needed to wait for someone to seat us. All the staff looked over at us and looked away. It was empty so it's not like they were too busy. So I spoke up and ASKED if we should pick a table.

One guy finally walked over and brought us over to a table in the corner. I asked for a menu an he said "It's on the wall" and walked away. The table where we were seated was at a weird angle where we couldn't see a thing on the menu. So I asked if we could be seated at the empty table closer to the wall menu. (considering almost all tables were empty - so I didn't see it being a problem)

He gave me a dirty annoyed look and said I will have to ask the owner! Who was sitting at a table with his buddies playing poker. I'm like are you kidding?! I told him I AM NOT interrupting him, and asked if he can please find out himself. We were moved and the owner whispered to him "Why do they want to sit there?" in an annoyed tone, like he didn't want us near him & his buddies.

STRIKE ONE.

We look at the menu and decided, I waved over the waiter and he walked over with a bad attitude. I told him what we wanted. If I dared ask a simple question he gave me a curt reply. He puts in our order and brings over bread and drinks. I asked if my 3 y.o. niece can get a cup, versus the wine glass placed before her. He says NO, they don't have any. Mind you this place was NOT THAT FANCY.

STRIKE TWO.

He brought over the food and starts serving us our individual plates. He splashed the spaghetti oil on me a few times and didn't apologize when I flinched. When he finished he walked away before I could ask for paper napkins. When I tried calling him over, he got so annoyed that I was interrupting his texting session and continually rolled his eyes. I was nothing but polite, so not to cause a scene in front of my family so I don't know WTF his problem was.

STRIKE THREE

Finally we're finishing up and the owner and his buddies light up their cigs and start smoking, meanwhile there are NO SMOKING signs posted up all over. An old couple had to move from their table while eating because of the secondhand smoke. Did they take this as a sign and put it out? NOPE.

Our waiter asked if we wanted dessert, I said NOPE I would like the check. The place doesn't take credit cards -such an inconvenience -but luckily I was aware of this before hand. I paid my check and walked right out to find almost the entire staff in the small lobby talking on their cells, smoking cigs. Not outside, but in the lobby.

Needless to say, I WILL NEVER return. That's a promise. The service was terrible! The food was overpriced and not that special. I'd much rather take the trip into the city for REAL family style restaurants such as Carmines and Tony DiNapoli.

This place is incredible!  Layover at JFK last night...searching for some authentic Italian cuisine.  Google search led us to Don Peppe's (South Ozone Park - Queens).  We were seated immediately -tight quarters but lots of friendly conversations going on.  Lots of Italian people dining here which is a good sign!  Menu is on the wall on a black board...many choices...all look delicious.  Our waiter came by, described the specials...and offered us beverages...house red wine is relish!  

Party of three...we started with the house salad...family style.  I could have been content with just that...fresh beyond belief...from the crisp, green lettuce to the obviously imported tomatoes that taste like they came from your grandmother's garden.   And the dressing...mwah!  It was the lightest, freshest, homemade Italian imaginable!  Olives green and black...incredible.

As one member of our party had a seafood allergy...we had to shy away from the clams...and although the veal gets total raves, we opted for spaghetti with garlic and olive oil first...delicious!  Plenty of garlic and sauce.  The pasta was not homemade...only downside of this entire meal...and not a big deal.

2nd course chicken with lemon and butter...can't say enough about this dish...wish I could make it that good at home...pounded thin...tender and moist beyond belief...vibrant lemon butter sauce - bright with a hint of fresh parsley!

Dessert we split two...tortufo and a cannoli....seriously THE BEST cannoli ever.  Filling so light and creamy...again AMAZING!

If you are in or about the JFK area...this is a MUST!
Great food especially like the linguini w/ white clam sauce.

1st time I knew Don Peppe was from company lunch but it's take out party orders.
I don't really in for Olive Garden or some other chain Italian stores style.
Don Peppe still keeps the old fashion way. 
Menu is painted on the wall, so don't ask waiter for the menu lol.
The things I LOVE are:
-House salad
-Baked Clams.
-Grilled Portabella mushroom ( by luck, sometimes they don't have it)
-Linguine White Clam Sauce.
-Veal Don Peppe
-??? forgot the dish name ( fried Eggplant)
-House Red wine 

Their portion is good for sharing. 4+ ppl to share is very convenient and you may only be able to order 3 things and you are done....too full!!!!
our avg. expense is $35-50/ea not too bad for a big meal.

With a group of friends, I came from Manhattan via public transportation (E train, then the q10 bus; another option was to take the A train, then walk about 15 minutes), and learned not to come back again until one of us had a car (because we accidentally took the q10 that skips a large part of Lefferts Blvd). It would've been less hilariously sad if we took up shuttle service from JFK to a nearby rental car lot. In the end, we walked through puddles and along some highways and made it there.

The service and atmosphere at Don Peppe is reminiscent of Peter Luger's Steakhouse, minus the steak and the Brooklyn accent. It's more casual though, So no need to dress up.

The linguine with white clam sauce was the best dish of the night. The baked clams were nicely flavored with garlic, but very oily/buttery. The red peppers fried in oil and garlic was tasty. The veal Don Peppe was not exhilarating; it was basically just veal cutlet with salsa on top. The eggplant rollotini was also very ordinary. 4 of us shared all of that and some house wine, and the total came out to about $175. I would return, but there is some equally-as-good and better Italian restaurants in Manhattan.

It's like the movies, you need to be in the right frame of mind for what you are going to see. You don't watch "Spiderman" for acting, nor Hamlet for special effects. You go to Don Peppe for  fantastic family size portions of simple Italian food. The place is out of Guys & Dolls, sometimes with the card game still going on. If you look for where the locals eat in Chinatown, this is where the Italians eat italian food. (Almost) everything starts with olive oil & huge whole cloves of garlic on a huge flame. My favorite dish bar none is the baked clams. I could eat them, one at a time like forever. Someone wrote they are oily. To me, that is for dipping bread. The clam sauce is always excellent. I also love the shrimp & mussel fra diavlo, always with good heat & rich tomato flavor. Other regular choices are the chicken parm & peppers w/onions. I have been coming here literally for 35 years, always looking forward to the meal before hand and building it up in my mind. The food has never disappointed me.

My family goes to this place whenever we have something to celebrate. We have ordered everything from Clam Sauce to Veal Don Peppe and even arthokes, and trust me, you can never go wrong! 

I've never had a problem with the waiters here. They are always very friendly and are more than willing to recommend a dish to you. The difference: when they recommend something to you, it is excellent food (unlike what I often hear when waiters recommend the worst food they have, just to sell it off).

The price is very reasonable with a small group and downright cheap with a large group. When I had my confirmation several years ago, a group of 12 went to Don Peppe and had appetizers, pastas, entrees, deserts, and drinks (including some wine) for about $350 (less than $30 per person for drink, appetizer, pasta, entree, and desert=very reasonable). This price level is amazing, especially since it's one of the best Italian restaurants in New York City.

When I'm in the restaurant, it's usually for lunch. Therefore, I can't attest to how crowded it gets. However, with this level of food quality, it is definitely worth the wait.

There are a couple of things to keep in mind before entering into Don Peppe. First, they only accept cash! They don't accept credit cards!!! Second, the menu and menu prices on the wall don't necessairly correspond to what they actually have and for the price they are offering.

I considered knocking Don Peppe down a star for its dated decor. A couple of things changed my mind on this. First, the great food at a reasonable price more than makes up for the decor. Second, I noticed a Joe Montana signed autograph on the wall, with the autograph saying that he really enjoyed the food. To me, this cool piece makes up for decor issues. If it's good enough for Joe Montana, it's definitely good enough for me!

There are a few times I recommend that someone NOT go to Don Peppe:

1. You want to impress your date with romantic ambiance in an intimate setting.
2. You want to be treated like a king/queen who has their food served 'just so'.
3. You like small portions and diet friendly fare.
4. You don't like garlic. 

However, the reason that you DO go to Don Peppe is that you are a hungry carnivore, looking for Italian that feels home cooked, at prices you don't get in Manhattan proper. 

The Don is family style, so bring your appetites and don't be surprised is they make strong recommendations on what you should order.The menu is on the wall, but the waiter will tell you, "its a given" that you get certain dishes. Take his advice; and don't miss the baked clams. 

Make sure to dip into the restrooms. Last time I was there, a circle of chairs was setup in the handicapped stall. No one bugs the bathroom! It's just THAT kind of place. Enjoy it for what it is - or fuggetaboutit!

We got baked clams ($20 for a bakers dozen) and a stuffed artichoke ($10.50). Everybody's talking about the clams here, but I didn't think they were all that... at all. The stuffed artichoke was a much better experience, and came with the same bread crumbs as the clams. 

Our linguini with clam sauce was good, and I would recommend it to anyone who comes here. But that's where I stop recommending. 

We were implored by the smug waiter to order entrees instead of more pasta, but when plate came to food, the entrees were way flat and not worth the price... at all. Our braciole was one 6 inch log, and tasted flat. Our veal marsala was also nothing special and not worth the price. 

If I could do it again (and I have no qualms about coming back, it clearly can be a decent experience), I would stick with the artichoke, and get a couple of pastas. Maybe an entree, but I would have to view it on someone else's table or iPhone first. 

Maybe this was all because the staff was scheduled to clean the floors at the end of the night and were trying to expedite us. That's fine, I understand shit has to be done, but if you are inconveniencing your guests, you can't just be smug about it. One manager was nice, but the rest had this "get out of here" attitude. They should have at least treated us with something to-go, to make up for the nudging to leave. 

I understand that the employees or management would look at this review and blow it off, but they really shouldn't .  The waiter gave us a negative impression of the restaurant, and the entrees were not nearly worth the order. I came in expecting a Baller Italian experience, but it fell way flat.
Pepe is  consistently very good. Loud ambiance. Family style. No short cuts in food prep. You can cut veal with spoon. Pasta gets an  A. . Waiters gruff. Moderately expensive but well worth it.

What can you say about Don P's that hasn't been said.  Great food, fun place...a real family restaurant.  If you want stuffed shirt waiters and fancy tablecloths, go to Le Bernardin.  If you want great Italian food and a fun night, hard to be The Don's place!

Place is run like a boot camp,what's on the wall is all they have,that's it.service is good but the food is kinda bland,People that I usually speak to say the food I'd delightful.I have had better food in a pizza shop.prices are ok but I think your better of trying it and making your own decision,I'm not busting down the door for there food any day soon!

The Best Family Style Italian I know. I have been eating here all my life and the food is always great. The Baked Clams, Stuffed Artichoke, Chicken Scarpariello, Shrimp Luciano over Linguine and the Veal Don Peppe are delicious. The cofffee and cannolis are very good as well. Great for a group so you can try lots of garlicy goodness.

My family went here to celebrate my graduation 5/31. I saw the sign on the door about no tank tops and thought that my sister would not be able to go in. Unfortunately, that was not the case. We didn't know it was family style we thought it was just a regular menu. The waiter was very polite and helpful especially since we were new to the restaurant.Though I didn't like how the main meal dishes were separated into two. After the ziti 15 mins or so later we got the chicken parm. I thought the food could be a little warmer and not separated. The bread was warm, but not hot and fresh like Cara Mia which is our favorite place. Overall the food is good and it is a place to go to if you like family style and their style of serving food.
Great baked clams..To me the BEST white clam sauce in NYC !   I really enjoy the Veal Don Pepe in the summer!

My family comes here regularly because we cannot last that long without coming back. Don Peppe has become a staple in our diets now. 

It's an old school Italian American family style restaurant. Do not come here if you're on a romantic date or on the Atkins diet. Also, I think it's safe to say that this place is not too vegetarian friendly, and if you're scared of excess fat, then hate to break it to you, but everything here is dripping with olive oil (and sometimes butter). 

The wait staff is extremely helpful on menu recommendations and to help decide the portions (everything is made to share). -side note, the menu is a giant board on the back wall that lists everything they have. They're a super friendly bunch that recognizes their customers and treats them well. 

Things you have to order:
- Baked clams- what they're famous for, they're small clams topped with a buttery crumble that you need at least a half dozen of for yourself.
- Linguini in white clam sauce- best linguini in white clam sauce I've ever had in America. It's so simple that it's unfair. Ingredients: linguini, clam, white wine, full cloves of garlic, and parsley overflowing in olive oil. Prepare to ask for seconds.  
- Veal Don Pepe- breaded veal cutlets topped with fresh seasoned raw tomatoes and red onion. It's a great combination of ingredients that gives this dish a great bite. 
- House red wine- I say house because I have no idea where it's from. If you order for two, they serve it in a 12oz glass bottle. If you order a bottle for the table, they serve it in a fifth glass bottle. Wherever it's from, it's fruity, cheap, and pairs well with the food. 

Things that are also worth ordering:
- Fish in lemon sauce
- Grilled Portobello 
- Roasted red peppers
- Cannolis 

If you're preparing for a marathon, this is the place to go the night before. It's hands down my favorite place to carbo load. GET THE LINGUINI IN WHITE CLAM SAUCE.
BEST ITALIAN FOOD IN NEW YORK!!!! A very old fashioned family style restaurant. Takes only cash.

This place is the gold standard for old school NY family style Italian food. The crowd has become a peculiar mix of traditional NY Italian families partaking in a lifelong weekly/monthly ritual and people not from the area who get a kick at being a part of this incredibly authentic scene (although increasingly rare to find these days) for the occasional meal. There really is no decor to speak of - Its just a large room full of people eating, but thats ok as the food is the star here. Almost all of it is can't miss. Their baked clams are legendary and their marinara sauce is the best in NY. Period. The service is decent - it can be slow and it's cash only, but this is the kind of place where you just deal with it. However, when the food is this good, I don't really care. You keep trying to get a reservation at Rao's - I'll be at Don Peppe eating my face off.

Visited Don Peppe's on Saturday.  The food was very good, but I have been to many restaurants, and I can get very good food anywhere.  The rest of the place is a nightmare.  Starting with the greeting and treatment from the owner I'll call him "The BOSS', at the door, stating in a gruff maner, "Sit Down, I'll have a table for you soon." while others who came after us were seated right away.  He,"The BOSS" also told us in the same gruff manor, not five minutes after we paid our check, "you have to get up now, I need this table, we have people waiting."   Never in any restaurant have we been told to leave.  He,"The BOSS" was rude, obnoxious, nasty and full of himself and his own ego.  Our waiter was no better, rushed us and tried to tell us what we wanted, placed an order for pasta we didn't ask for.  $20.00 for a bottle of lousy house wine I wouldn't cook with.  I think bums on the street drink better wine.  We ordered our coffee's, and I asked if they had biscotti for the table, and was told very nastily, "Where do you think you are, in a Manhattan restaurant?"  Just nasty talk back from start to finish. The menu is on a board at the back of the restaurant, so if you have trouble seeing you have to get up, go over in the middle of other patrons who are eating and look.  God forbid they should spend some money and print paper menus for us paying slobs. The place is a dirty mess from floor to ceiling, dust and cobwebs everywhere.    Don't know when the place had a good cleaning last. Poor air conditioning.  I think the "BOSS" turns it on and off so patrons will eat fast, hurry out, and the "BOSS" can turn another table.  I could go on, but surfice to say we will not be comming back to "Don Peppe's" ever again.  Also would like to know who he bought that "A" rating he sports in the front window from?  Cash only business!!!!  Like to know how much business he claims on his taxes!!!!    I give this place 5 stars for grunge:-(.
P.S. Anyone who thinks the food is so good it worth getting treated poorly, and eating in such a dirty place must not know what it is like to have both.

Before we begin, I'll start you off with a little background: I rarely go to an Italian restaurant because it can never compare to my Mother's authentic Italian cooking (both of my parents are from Italy) and if I do, it's usually a letdown.  Having said that, Don Peppe's gets not only mine, but my Italian family's stamp of approval.  If my father says its good - its good.  

You come here for the food - not the service and not the décor.  Hate to say it, but this place has the best Linguine with clam sauce I've ever had (Sorry, Mom).  The Veal Don Peppe is the best veal you will ever have too - it's so tender you can cut it with your mind (the sever will cut it with a spoon instead - a spoon!).  The bruschetta-like topping with the veal cutlet is a match made in culinary heaven.  I went with a Mexican friend of mine and he loved the baked clams so much, he was dipping his bread into the empty shell of the clam - a move I've never witnessed before (and hopefully, never again).


 I plan on trying a lot more here, but here is what I've gotten so far:


The Go-To's:
Don Peppe Salad
Baked Clams
Linguine with white clam sauce (a must get)
Veal Don Peppe (a must get)
House red wine
Double shot of espresso



I've also tried:
Roasted red peppers (only okay)
Shrimp in the baked clams sauce (forgot the name, but I liked it)
Eggplant Parm (not bad)
Cannoli (didn't like it)


Menu is on the wall, don't wear a tank top, bring cash, sit back and enjoy the show.

This place is the best Italian food you can get - anywhere . My father ate here 30 years ago. I now live 90 min away and try to come here anytime I'm traveling through the area 
It is a great food fix for me
Ate here Saturday night with my 2 daughters after spending the day at the Barclays tournament
We waited 1 hour,  but after tasting the first dish , we knew the wait was well worth it
The service was great ( waiter Pedro), the food quality unsurpassed 
I advise - go here whenever you can, even If out of your way

Leave the gun take the garlic.  When it comes to family style home cooked Italian food, as if there is any other way to put those words together, you either got it or you don't .  Don Peppe's got it and in a big way.  

They have been at this location for 45 years, and any night you go you will over hear someone talking about playing cards there in the 60's or being a regular for 20, 30 or 40 years.  People just was to be attached to this place in any way possible.  Much like the Menu, only written on the back wall, you want to be there not to miss anything.

Start with the clams, then get some more clams, yes they are that good.  The salad might be the only thing not to drive home a 10, but it is salad, what are ya gonna complain about a 9?  

The lemon butter chicken is so good, I am drooling now thinking about it.  The Veal Marsala, and the garlic pasta are right there too.  You need some Bill Gates brain to figure out what is better then what.  

My suggestion is to round up a group of calorie counting, stomach ailment suffering, pickiest eaters you know, head to Don Peppe's and that just means more for you.  If you go with anyone close to normal you are going to fight down to the last clove of garlic, and if you are with me it is war.

ENJOY!

If you are looking for an old Italian restaurant family style, look no further. All plates are to be shared as the portions are generous. Reasonably priced, cash only. We had the stuffed mushrooms and linguine with white clam sauce and the taste is still lingering in my mouth. Two thumbs up, there will definitely be a repeat visit.
My god eat the clam sauce and baked clams if its the last thing you do on earth!! Artichokesw are great. Homemade red wine is good stuff. Cash only. Worth every dime.

If you're looking for a classic, old school family style italian amazing meal..this is the place.  
I suggest the baked clams, white clam linguini, and the veal.

 I agree with the other reviewers to not come here for a romantic date or if you are on a diet.  

Cash only.

The service was absolutely terrible, and the food was just so-so.  For instance, we asked for oil to dip our bread into, and the waiter said no!  We must use our butter.  Wow.  AND, they do NOT serve coffee, only espresso.  Definitely never worth the trip from Long Island, and certainly not even a 5 minute walk.

Weirdness: NYC health grade is "pending", no credit cards accepted, no HATS allowed!, waiter's card game usually in progress at a central table. Foodwise, however, it is hands down THE BEST ITALIAN RESTAURANT IN NYC. The homemade Italian red wine, probably unlicensed, is incredible! The linguini and clam sauce is the best I ever ate.

Lived in Howard Beach, Ozone Park, Richmond Hill for years and have never been here before. I decided to try it out with my brother on a weeknight. 
 
Strike One: Menu on a wall. Nobody wants to read shit from 20 feet away. Invest in individual menus.

Strike Two: Doesn't take credit cards. Really? It's almost 2013. Nobody wants to sit down and shit in their pants wondering if they have enough cash in their pocket to cover the check. GET A CREDIT CARD machine!!

Strike Three: Waiter was a rude prick. We got up and walked out before the food even came out.

Forget this place!!

Hands down my favorite Italian restaurant. This is a Hidden treasure way out near JFK. Don Peppe is a family Style italian restaurant with no menus and is cash only. I always feel like I'm stepping into a scene from the sopranos. 

Linguine with white clam sauce is out of this world. This is a must have. You cannot leave here without having this. Baked clams appetizer is amazing. Veal don peppe is amazing. Shrimp Luciano. Even the spaghetti with meat sauce is amazing.

This is the best family style Italian restaurant in NYC.  It is tucked away in the southeast Queens where many Italian families use to live.  I only know about this place from a coworker who grew up in the neighborhood.  The physical restaurant looks like it belongs back in the 70s but the quality of the food is unmatched.  From the baked clams, to the linguine in white clam sauce and the delicious veal.  I never walked away hungry or unsatisfied.

Although the food was good, the service sucked! They're nowhere to be seen until you have the bill in your hand.  Bring your own grated geese if you want some or you'll be finished with your dish before you can find someone to get it for you.   Also, if you like anything other than wine or soda, skip this place.  There are no other options.  The atmosphere (if you think there is one) is loud and the decor is  outdated.   I think this place is popular with the old timers because its been around for years, but they need to move into the 21at century. To appeal to the younger crowd. It also is a bit over priced, I added pasta to my dish, and although it was a nice portion, it was $14!  Seriously?!  A whole pound of pasta is $1!  I can see $5 maybe $6, but $14 is nuts!

Italian, family style. Great restaurant of this kind. No reservation, but waiting to besotted is not terrible - not more then 30 minutes in busiest time. Food definitely worth the wait. Muscles, pasta with clam source and veal,eggplant are the best we ever ate. Not terribly expensive, great for big parties. I would not recommend for 2 people - portions are too big.

Well worth the drive from manhattan!!! The clams so great ,  the  spaghetti with shrimp sauce to die for! The house red yum yum yum!  We were so full by the veal don peppa arrived we could have stopped at pasta course.  We gorged and ate most of it!!,!  This is a definite destination restaurant!! Don't miss this place !
The Texas Girls gone to NYC !!!

My friends and I were so excited about coming here for dinner and we were not disappointed. This is the best food I have ever had!  The wine was amazing, too!  They should bottle and sell it... they'd make a fortune!!!  Our waiter, Marco, was wonderful, too, with a great personality, which only made the evening even better. It wasn't just going to a restaurant... it was a dining experience.  After reading the reviews, and as this was our first time here, we decided to try what others had suggested: the baked clams and linguine with clam sauce.  Everything was delicious, just as the other reviews had stated.  We then had the veal parmigiana.  Absolutely amazing!  One of my friends bases his opinion of restaurants by this dish and he was in veal heaven, as was my other friend and I. We can't wait to come back so we can try everything on the menu!!!  Yum!!

This place is awesome. Leaving on a plane out JFK tomorrow so searched for restaurants near the hotel. Read reviews on yelp and were pleased beyond belief with this little gem. Started with the red wine! Which was, as promised, chilled.,reminded me of a sangria without the fruit. Followed with the spaghetti with clams (white) and it was definitely as good as everyone said.
