Continued on with the veal don peppe and, again, pleased. The veal is lightly battered and fried topped with an Italian salsa of tomatoes, red onion & basil with oil and vinegar. The service was perfectly timed. Didn't try to rush us out even though the place was packed. Great people watching experience too. I would totally repeat this experience the next time I have to fly out of JFK.

Just got back from a trip and landed at JFK. This place is a must stop if you are passing through the area. Old school Italian food, but they are at the top of the field. We started with baked clams that were sooo good. Then came out the linguine and clam sauce and the veal Don pepe, wow.. the veal Don pepe. Beautiful pounded veal, breaded, fried and topped with tomatoes and red onion. All family style so try to go with at least 4 people. Don't worry about drinks just order the house wine, white or red, their both fantastic. This is a MUST stop if you like italian food, even if your not going to JFK, make a special trip. It's that good!!

Just had dinner here for first time, luiguine  with white clam sauce, lots of roasted garlic very few clams not enough white wine too much oil. Also chicken Marsala ,3 skimpy cutlets sauce tasty but watery. Food  was very good all around ,but not family style portions.Will go again and try other things but 2 family style portions barely feed 3 average appetites .Must try deserts.

The best Italian restaurant. I'm from Pa. and have been to Italy two times and this is the best state side. My friend Neil God Bless took us there and we were blown away with the whole experience. I miss Neil. My friend.
Heard nothing but good about Don Peppes have to go some day have family still lives there!!I love family style also will go ASAP!!

I've been here a bunch and while I'm sure there are places doing classic Italian American dishes better, this is my favorite.  The chilled house red wine is great.  I fear that it is really just Carlo Rossi or comes from a cardboard box but to be honest I don't care.  The host is a super nice guy and even gave me a side hug in front of my girl and made me look like a VIP.  I don't know him really but the effort was appreciated.  My favorite dish is the spaghetti with garlic and oil.  Simple, but delicious.  It's loaded with roasted garlic.  The veal Don Peppe is good, veal cutlets with a bruschetta topping essentially.  I really like the chicken with lemon and butter and a side of escarole.  I've never had the Chinese chicken here because it takes awhile to cook, but I'm looking forward to trying it.  The servers are all willing to give suggestions.  As you can tell I'm a big fan.

I live in Florida now, but I am a native Nyer and I miss Don Pepe soooooo much I could cry! I love the baked clams, linguine and white clam sauce and the veal chop! I wish DP would have a restaurant down here in FL :(

Four stars certainly on food and service.  It was everything i have been reading about and more.... Amazing stuffed artichoke.. awesome linguine with clam sauce... all perfect...service attentive and at a good pace.  What bothers me so much (thus the 4 instead of 5 stars) ...why can't a place as successful and well known as this, close up for 1 or 2 days, put a fresh coat of paint on the walls and maybe replace the 2x4 wood chair rail with something more decorative? Maybe replace a few of the spaghetti sauce covered receptacles on the walls?   Come on..you can get this done for 2-3 grand and at least look a bit more classy. sponge painting went out 22 years ago, prob when they applied it.    Also, i went home, made some clarified butter and roasted some garlic.  I am hoping it will bring some of my cooking up to par with them!..
Was there last Tuesday after a day out of town on business.  Great family style Italian restaurant. Great salad & pasta.

Ate at the famous Dom Peppe,, i agree with the few haters, dont waste your CASH or time going to this place. The decor is old, dingy and cheap, yet the CASH prices are high.  Pass on the oily baked clams and save your $20. The wait staff definitely pushes the food or should i say the higher priced food.

Got there at 6:00 to avoid the wait. After being seated one of us immediately ordered for the entire table of 6.   We had no questions about the menu and made life easy for our waiter. Had our apps, pasta and then main course. To be fair the food was good.  Our waiter wasn't outwardly rude or obnoxious (at this point) but had been very matter of fact and not so welcoming.  Again, to be fair we were all fine with that. We knew the atmosphere and realized we weren't at a 5 star romantic French restaurant.
    HOWEVER...at 7:25 the waiter came by and almost as if it were an inconvenience, asked if we wanted dessert. One of us said "yes, can you give us a second to decide." To which we were told "actually, no.  I can't. If you don't know now, I can't.  There is a line out the door"
    Are you kidding me!  We were not sitting around chatting and sipping on water.  In fact, we ate pretty quick once our main course was finally served.  Never in my life have I been rushed like that.  Usually dessert is pushed on a customer. Instead we were pushed out the door.  Needless to say we asked for the check, since there was such a rush to get rid of us.  Never, ever again will I step foot in the place.
LInguine White Clam, bad homemade wine that tastes great, stuffed artichoke, "try the veal, it's the best in the city", a total scene.  You'll love it.

Don Pepe is hands down the best in the city. eat the baked clams and you've done your piece on earth .. the liguine , the veal "best in the city" best of all you can write a book about the joint and there are some great stories in the 40 years I've gone there. Along with the great food you cant help it but come back. I was even warned that if I didnt bring Don Pepe back to Fla DONT COME HOME. My friend at the door yells out" Tell her I got yuz covered"

On a Saturday night, we arrived at 7pm and had to wait about 90 minutes for a table for two. The host was very positive though and once inside the service was pleasant and timely. My companion and I had the chicken with lemon and butter and the linguine with white clam sauce. They were both very large portions so we took some home. They go very heavy on the garlic in the linguine dish and it's really oily, but tasted good. The inside is like a plain banquet room with pretty bright lights but the ambiance wasn't as bad because everyone was having a good time. The house wine was great.

Good food and chilled red wine :) 
I liked the stuffed artichoke but my wife and son were not too thrilled with this appetizer. The mozzarella & tomatoes was a hit with the family. The chicken marsala entree was also delicious. 
The chilled red house wine definitely complemented the meal.

Overall a nice dining experience. Please note this restaurant accepts cash only.

Just tried Don Peppe for the first time and I wasn't disappointed at all. My sister took me out for my birthday. What a present. We started out with their famous bake clams, What flavor. Then  we had fried eggplant, veal chops and green beans. They serve family style so you won't leave hungry. We can't wait to go back and try their linguini in clam sauce with chunks of clam. OMG. People who live in the neighborhood are really lucky to have Don Peppe so close. Chow

Not gonna lie but the food quality has gone way down since 2 years ago..   My plate that came had food bits all over and was not even clean.   The spoon has so much black oxidation.   

Short wait, at times, but man i wish it was 2 years ago..   Things were missing off the menu too..  you figure Don would have meatballs or chicken parm..  oh well.. went home hungry, it was good but was better before

There's nothing I can say that hasn't been said before about the food. Great artichokes, linguini with clam sauce, veal with eggplant, baked clams, red wine.  This was my second time at DP. first time we were 3. This time we were 5 and the waiter, without telling us adjusted each order for our table size. So when you think you're ordering from the board with pricing ($20 for an item) he brought us 1 1/2 or double sizes. So a $21 chicken dish was $40, $20 pasta was $30, etc. So when ordering, make sure you specify the size you want. Now we know and you should to! Bill ended up much larger than expected. But the food is worth it!

We lived in the "neighborhood" for a couple of years. Can not tell you how many times my husband and I wish we could just pop in Don Peppe's for a great meal. San Francisco woudl be lucky to have such a great place. We miss the wonderful food, and of course the chilled red wine!!

As a baked clams lover, Don Peppe has knocked almost every other place off my favorite baked clams place list. Vincents is still better in my opinion but its now number 2! Its so good. The blend of crumbs melts in your mouth. Yummy! 

Linguini with clams & garlic sauce was really appetizing. It tasted better than I expected by a million. The garlic was cooked perfectly. Browned but not burnt and no rawness. I ate so much garlic... not exactly to my bfs liking. 

We also ordered the chicken don peppe. OMG the chicken was breaded lightly and extra crispy on the outside and it was soooo juicy on the inside. AND it didnt go soggy. By itself I called it a glorified large slab of chicken tenders BUT my second bite, I tasted the seasoning of the chicken or the breading and the topping the combination was amazing. SUPER WOW. The onion and tomatoes marinated in whatever it was ...YEA so coming back soon! 

The place looks old and it was dejavu for second like the chinese restaurant I visited on queens blvd. It could use renovations, but then they might add another 0 at the end of the bill. I'd still come again though LOL

What a gem! Been a loyal Frankie and johnnies pine fan for years. This place is my type of place as well. Traditional Italian with all the hooks. Warm bread, chilled homemade red wine, cash only with silent service that isn't over bearing at all. Perfect! Scarp and baked clams tonight. Outstanding!

Always a fan, but times change. So does the quantity and quality of food. So if you expect the same thing as years ago, don't go.  If you understand that things change, but can still be good, you'll be fine.  Baked clams are great, but sauce is thin.  Linguine white clam is also good, smaller platter, higher price.  Wine-vintage yesterday :) Service as sucky as always, but that's not why we go.

Anyone who says it is not as good as it was years ago is a miserable person that should not post! It is just as good as my first visit 32 years ago! Don Peppe's is like Sunday dinner made by the most talented family with Grandma supervising everything. No rectangular plates, no drizzled nonsense, no ingredients that nobody heard of until the last few years. Just amazing real food for real people. Tonight I had baked clams and chicken scapriello. Unbelievable!!!!*****

Don Peppe's is old school Italian at it's best....Go in...mind your business...order the meal...and don't rat on your friends. And if you get  pinched, tell them nothing!!!....Seriously, the baked clams, linguine white clam, shrimp Luciano over linguine and veal don peppe is what's it's all about....Forgetaboutit!!!!

When I was smaller, family style Italian restaurant was Olive Garden.  That was how tv portrayed its so what else did I know?  Well, Don Peppe's really does deliver the true meaning of family style with their awesome food being served here!  I was first told about this place from my brother who dined here in the past and raved about this place.  Since I absolutely LOVE Italian food, this was a must check out place due to my curiosity.

One of their must have dishes is the baked clams.  The seasoned bread crumbs on top of this prepared dish, cooked with butter is just phenomenal.  Also their veal don peppe is really good too.  The linguini with garlic and clam sauce is awesome without saying and get the broccoli rabe as well!  One time we also ordered the sole that was prepared in the same manner as the baked clams, broiled with butter and bread crumbs.. so good!

This place doesn't joke around and disappoint.  I really suggest coming here and be the judge yourself.  I am just salivating writing this review.

I really don't understand why this restaurant is getting good reviews. The food is mediocre, the waiter was rude at times and the place need some serious up grade. Just don't go to this place is a waist of money an time.
Excellent! Excellent food! Excellent staff! Excellent owners! Family friendly Italian style! Be back for sure (&bring friends for share huge dishes).

Good, solid Italian food in Queens. don't think i would day it was the best food ever. certainly overpriced with arrogant waiters, who couldn't believe we weren't ordering the " signature" clam dish.  We were with a group of about 15 and the waiter said they couldn't accommodate "too many pasta variations"...really b/c for the price they should accommodated whatever we wanted to order. No rush to go back.

Tried Don Peppe for the first time yesterday. The clams were good. I wouldn't say they were amazing. I've had better at a few Italian places in the city. The Veal Don Peppe is the dish that will really have me coming back. Basically it's veal cutlet with bruschetta over it. The clams and veal don Peppe is definitely enough to feed 2 people. I would say this place is expensive for the decor. Definitely needs a facelift.
The only two thing to order here which ON ONE can beat: baked clams, and white clams sauce linguini.  That's your whole meal, trust me.

Was back on Friday and actually tried two things I had yet to order on the menu. The stuffed peppers which were delicious and the eggplant parmesan which was also excellent. I'm not much of an eggplant fan but I thoroughly enjoyed the dish. Just a few more reasons why I keep coming back again and again.

True gem - need more stars!  We drive over an hour to come here - found by accident after trip home from JFK.  Right out of old New York.  Mozzarella and tomato w roasted peppers is AMAZING.  Everything we try (chicken parm, spaghetti marinara, spaghetti with garlic and oil) is superb.  It is also refreshing to not labor over a wine selection: Options are chilled red or chilled white.  Both good and serve the food well.  All-male waitstaff serves food promptly and plates it (it is served family style) upon its arrival.  And we get to bring a bit home with us for the next day.  What a great place!  Go if you are landing at JFK, go if you live anywhere around there and..if you are like us... Go Even if you don't.  CASH ONLY.
Love this place! From the appetizers to desert you can't go wrong, oh and bring Cash$$$$ No CC

So the walls are blah, it's not in the best of locations for a restaurant and you definetly feel like you are in a 1970's italian dinner movie scene .... So why the 4 stars??? The food!!! The food is unbelievable. It must be the sauce, because everything is super tasty. It's funny because I went with a group of friends and one of them inquired as to wine selection. The waiter simply responded "we have red and white"... But the wine was delicous as well. From the outside you wouldn't think much of the place, but dodge that initial perception and walk in for a great family style, italian cuisine experience.

Took off a star for the horrible service :(
A friend and I were driving back from JFK to drop off a friend and he read the reviews of this place and we decided to stop. He was craving clams and I wanted Italian. Walking in and seeing the menu painted on the wall, I really wasn't sure what to expect. From the very beginning, our waiter (the old man in the middle section, in case others want to AVOID his section) was incredibly rude and gruff. I always respond with please and thank you and he had no acknowledgement back of either. He took our order very briskly and walked away and came back with drinks. That was the ONLY time my friend was able to get a glass of water from him. We had to keep asking the bus boys. He gave me a nasty look and an audible sigh when I asked for another Coke. We wanted to add to our order and finally had to ask the bus boy because he didn't come back for 30 minutes. He appeared MUCH more attentive to his other parties, both of which he knew the people at. They even received pitchers of water. It was so bad that my friend and I had no choice but to start laughing at how obviously nasty he was to us!
However, THE FOOD WAS INCREDIBLE!!! I tried the breading to his clams and it was just amazing (I'm not a clams person). I even used the excess sauce for my bread! I had the eggplant parmesean and it was just amazing! Both the cheese and sauce were the best I"ve ever had. I was surprised to see that it doesn't come with pasta, so we when ordered spaghetti and meat sauce and that was really good too. We had planned to get dessert and coffee and wine, but the service was so bad and it took over 2 hours, that we were forced to skip it. I will try and come back because the food was so amazing, but I will NEVER sit in that guy's section again!!!

Wow....I was impressed. Coming from the Bronx, I have tasted some great Italian food in my day. THIS, has to be the best tasting Italian food I have probably ever had. The setup is simple. One large room, family style. 

The menu? On a board on the wall. The service? On point. Our waiter came by at least 20 times to make sure we were okay. 

I left wanting a bed, that's a good thing.

Was very excited to come here but kind of disappointed. Eggplant parm was 100% microwaved lacked cheese and was not so good. The spaghetti w garlic and oil were very good. Stuffed mushrooms needed extra crispiness. Not coming back

This is the place to go after the track!
It's a "who's who" of celebrities and big shots.
The salad is just like the one your Nonna used to make!
Order the baked clams and linguine and clam sauce.
Cash only ! and don't forget the camera.
Bella ciao!!

Went for dinner last week with family.  Was very disappointed with the food.  Bread was terrible, shrimp was tough, pasta was just ok.  Server tries to push extra food and owner was very rude, asked us to hurry because he needed table. Chicken was best part of meal as were the clams     I guess spending  $325 without a tip was not good enough.  Been to many better restaurants  and would not go out of my way for this place
AMAAZZIINGG! AMMAZZING! I've had dreams about their food long after coming here

The food was amazing !
We went with great friends, there were 7 of us.
The waiter helped us order just enough so we all ate our fill with nothing left over. It's a great testament to a good waiter who can guide you to the correct amount of food.
We started out with Baked Clams...OMG !! There is a reason they are rated #1 in the country.
We then had Mussels in Zupa (white broth with a hint of herb....tarragon I think)
On to the pasta dish... Linguini with white clam sauce...yummers !
Finally came the entrees...Veal Don Peppe, Shrimp Luciano and Veal Marsala.
We all ate and drank and left full but not bloated.

As we left (6:45pm) the line was out the door. Here's a big tip, plan for an early dinner and avoid the long wait !

Also...CASH ONLY, so be prepared.

Pricey and decent italian food. Do not come for the service, its horrible. We were a party of two and were rushed through the whole meal at 5PM. Let the locals believe the hype I guess, for the price you could eat anywhere you wanted in New York.

If someone gives Don Pepe's less than 4 stars, they should have all reviews removed from Yelp and should be banished from reviewing anything - even non-food related things - for life.  It is a 5 star northern Italian restaurant with food that others should envy.  I just don't get why other places can't just produce food that is half as good as Don Pepe's.  THE best Italian food I've ever had short of (because of sentimental reasons) one place where I grew up in Utica, NY.  Baked Clams, Shrimp Luciano, Linguini with White Clams, Chicken Don Pepe, Stuffed Shells.  done.

LINGUINI & CLAM SAUCE.  BAM!  The most amazing ever.  I totally ruined a shirt digging in to this amazingly tasty dish.

Also, worth noting, I kinda felt like I was in a scene out of Good Fellas (cash only), but hey, it's all good!  I walked out alive (and full).

Do it like a Don.
The best italian food in New York, bar none.The place isn't fancy, but you will be in heaven over the food. Wow, what an experience!!!

I came here on my own because I was stuck at a hotel near JFK for one night.  The food is delicious.  The service was great.  The atmosphere is incredible - in a sort of ironic amusing way.  

If the Sopranos were inspired by the this place I would not be at all surprised.  Track suits and teased hair as far as the eye could see.  Sorry did you say "her?"  "Yeah, huh, that's what I exactly said!"  If you're a shitty writer come here and transcribe, you'll win awards.

The decor is pretty off putting - bright lights and tatty grey wallpaper. I nearly turned around and walked out at first glance but be brave!  It'll pay off.  If you're from out of town it's practically an anthropological study.  And I'm not being mean, it's just a very specific world.

Once thing to note, it is all cash and all family style.  I was asked about six times if I was really eating alone.  Apparently that is very strange here.

I had the linguini white claim sauce.  Amazing.  Delicious. Yummy.  (No I did not eat it all because it's enough to serve five and that would be gross.)  Some chilled red wine.  What can go wrong there?  And a slice of house made cheese cake with orange rind.  Soooo yummy!

I highly recommend this place.  Do it.  If for not other reason than YOLO.

Ate here Wednesday night. Food is delicious. Two couples. Thought waiters a little brusque - but polite. Food is family style and place is brightly lighted. Had a tossed salad stuffed mushrooms and baked clams - all excellent. Wine is either red or white there is no wine list. We had the red probably a chianti. It was cold which surprised me a little but you kind of just go with the flow here. Also had rigatoni with sausage and chicken marsala everything was delicious.  Be patient definitely have to wait for table on weekends but food worth it and good for groups.

We decided to try this place out for our anniversary even after reading mixed reviews. We got there around 6:30 on a Saturday night and I have to say there was really no wait like people where talking about with lines out the door, we were seated right away. The place reminded me of an old basement that badly need to be updated and the bathrooms really needed a good cleaning. That would not have mattered if the service and food was good..  We knew before we even got there that we wanted the stuffed artichokes.  We ordered  for dinner Stuffed Artichokes, Baked Clams. Chicken Scarpariello,  Shrimp Luciano and broiled Steak.  After we placed our order the waiter that had no personality and was rude came back and told us that they ran out of artichokes.  While trying to decide what we wanted instead, we were rushed and told that we couldn't have a minute to decide because he had to put the order in. The waiter brought us plates which had dried food stuck to them and we had to share knives because the waiter said they were short on utensils. The appetizers were fine but not amazing as per other reviews, then the steak came , which we ordered medium and it came not only rare.....but RAW!  We asked to cook it some more which annoyed him and he brought it back to us two minutes later and it was still raw.  We were all disgusted at that point so we did not eat it and told the waiter this. Again he seemed annoyed.  We eat out a lot and have never had this bad service.  Not only did we pay $68 for a steak that nobody ate, but we had to deal with a nasty attitude from the waiter and everyone left hungry.  We were not asked throughout our whole meal how everything was and we were never offered dessert or coffee either.  The check was thrown on the table and we paid and left a tip which wasn't deserved.  Needless to say , we will not be returning.

In the past I've been burnt before by Italian restaurants that either forsake traditional methods for the sake of novel creativity, or otherwise rest on their laurels until there is no joy at all in eating their food. Those kinds of restaurants generally rely upon location and radio advertisements, meanwhile you could miss this place coming off the Belt if you don't know it's there, and they have no imprint on the net. 

Don Peppe is a stalwart of the old Italian neighborhood, with everything staying traditional to the last bite. Family-style platters of Italian-American favorites served table-side by the waiter, chilled house wine filled up into re-usable glass bottles, (points for unintentionally being green.) and of course one big menu board for the entire restaurant. 

Clams, clam sauce, braciole. I regret none of it. I want more of it. Oh, and primo people watching.
A True Gem, will be back. excellent food, price, service and location.

So good. Super warm, family friendly place. It was packed on a Sunday night  (come before 6pm) but the server was attentive. I came with 3 other people. We ordered the most famous dishes:

Linguini with white clam sauce- the olive oil in that sauce was amazing, lots of garlic too
Veal don peppe (breaded veal topped with fresh bruschetta)-banging
(Extra: Stuffed shells: great
Baked clams were allright. Get a salad and house wine to share

It is DEFINITELY worth the trip if you live outside of Queens

My fiancé and I went to Don Peppes to celebrate our 4 year anniversary. We had heard from friends that the food was delicious there. Upon entering the place we didn't expect it to be open spaced and so casual...but after we had the great baked clams ...the unbelievable liguini with clams sauce and fantastic veal don pepe we did not care about the decor !!!! The place is a must go and we are definitely going back!

I've been coming to Don Pep's since I was tiny enough to fit in a highchair and it's been a staple for my family since the 70s. I love that it's never changed -- excellent then and excellent now. And that's not just the nostalgia talking. 

MUST ORDER: 
Baked clams (EXCELLENT)
(also baked / stuffed artichoke)
Zuppa di clams or mussels
Shrimp Luciano (PHENOMENAL)
Linguine w/ clams (THE BEST)
Veal Don Pep (THE BEST)
Chicken  Scarpariello (w/ fennel sausage)
Lobster fra divolo
Beef braciole 

This is a place for serious eating. You don't come for the ambiance or the neighborhood. You don't come for overpriced cocktails or a pretentious wine list -- you won't find any of that here. You come here for the FOOD. And it's WORTH IT. You have two choices of wine: red or white, and that's all you need.

Went here for lunch with a friend on a not-so-busy Wednesday afternoon.

I'll start with this....the ambiance at Don Pepe's takes a little getting used to, but the impeccable service and fantastic food shines above all else.  Forget the cash only, poker playing in the corner mob undertones and you'll be transported to food heaven.  We were greeted by a nice old Italian guy, who told us to pick any table we'd like.  Our server then came up to us and very nicely explained how everything works at Don Pepe's (menu on the wall, cash only, the specialties).  Since we were only in a party of two, we stuck to the staples.  Baked clams to start and Linguine with Clam Sauce.  Best baked clams I've had.  Just fantastic buttery and crispy crust with a sauce that can only be described as liquid gold.  Next came the pasta.  Perfectly al dente cooked with just an incredible sauce with just the right amount of seasoning.  Not too much clam, just enough.  Watch out for the whole cloves of garlic though!  The food was simply great.

There are a few reviews that say that the service was bad, people were smoking inside, playing cards in the corner, whatever.  Yes, the owners smoke in the atrium when its cold outside, yes people play cards in the corner.  Who cares if some wise guy is getting beat up in the back room, just mind your own business eat the food.  Our service happened to be impeccable.  Our server recommended things, asked if we had been here before, came to our table many times to see if we needed anything else and was very nice.  Don Pepe's is one of those places that you need to take with a grain of salt, the food is just fantastic and shouldn't be missed.

I had been looking forward to visiting this place since learning about it over a year ago. I was aware that it was a no-frills place not known for great service. But it was still a disappointing first visit. My second visit is not likely to be anytime soon.

Greeting - We asked to be seated before the final member of our party arrived. We were told no. Perfectly understandable for a place that doesn't take reservations but the owner  was not at all friendly about it. The place was half empty but we were made to feel unwelcome. 

Ambience - All the atmosphere of a church basement.  Flourescent lights. Charmless layout and furnishings. Tacky big board on the wall displaying the menu.

Service - the waiter was pushy and more than a bit impatient. He seemed to think we had memorized the menu. How could we when this place doesn't HAVE a  printed menu? Instead the entire menu is displayed on a big board, as mentioned above. We weren't able to look at it ahead of time since we were told - rudely - to wait outside the dining area... On the positive side food was served at the table from the larger platter into individual dishes. Nice touch. 

Food - We had many of the signature dishes.
Salad - Good
Baked clams - Very good
Linguine with clam sauce - Decent. Nothing special.
Veal Don Peppe - Tender and served with fresh, diced tomatoes. But heavily breaded and not especially tasty.
Chicken with eggplant - Also quite tender but, again, not especially tasty.
Wine - Chilled red house wine. Mellow and quite good.

The food is decent but it didn't come close to living up to the raves. It was also way too pricey for a place that offers no other attractions (in fact it's quite UN-attractive) and treats patrons poorly.

Some of the best Italian food in Queens. It's right near JFK so I frequent this to and from the airport. Definitely worth a visit if you're in the area. Try the baked clams everyone raves about them! There's no reservations so make sure you have some extra time to kill.

The best Italian restaurant you never heard of, thank you Zagat. So this place is ooooooooold school, it's family style and cash only. It also doesn't help that it's in the middle of no where, it is however not far from JFK or the racetrack or Resorts World Casino. There are no menus, only a big ass board with everything they sell. Also, don't expect world class service, you go strictly for the food. I hear the Chicken Scarpariello is good and I saw some seafood boat that looked awesome. The place is family style, try to go with at least four people.

The food:

Veal Don Peppe- if you don't do veal, you have the option to go chicken. It's a cutlet with a tomato and red onion salad on top. The cutlets are so perfectly tender yet perfectly crunchy. The tomato and onion complement the cutlet perfectly. My fav thing here. http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=JS9Pp6NftdFBEi4GOzvV2Q&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Baked Clams- the best I ever had. The tops have a nice crunch and the clams are nice and tender, the garlic oil is amazing. Beware of the garlic dragon breath. They give you lemons to add a touch of acidity which is nice. http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=ZVdQjBYmjN61w42pyZDEIw&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Shrimp Luciano over linguine- This was a recommendation from a guy who just did my garage and it was a great recommendation. It's kinda like a shrimp a la vodka but with a thinned out sauce. This dish was really good and the onions are basically melt in your mouth. The pasta is an additional charge of $12, I think the dish by itself comes with rice. I thought this dish was great. http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=M5V3VOLYAOt7y3RBjgTftQ&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA 

Breast of Chicken Marsala- This is a dish that I thought I never liked, apparently, I just never had it done properly. The sauce is excellent and the chicken is so tender. The best Chicken Marsala I ever had and it's chicken breast and I normally hate chicken breast.

Linguine White Clam Sauce- It's a good dish, but didn't blow me away like everything else. I thought it was a tad greasy. Beware of the garlic dragon breath. http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=pV5Bwvv07hYMRBAwgheYBg&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA

Tiramisu- I didn't see this on the desserts menu but asked it they had it and they did. It was a solid dessert but the cake part was a tad dry. The cream makes this dish and I like the fact that there is a presence of coffee  and no strong boozey alcohol taste. http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=a_yN1YjT4SymPjCzIWz-iA&userid=Y_iTTjKvV5hLy-880SZzlA
All I can say Great Food. The homemade wine is great too. Not fancy but worth the wait.

I come here with my boyfriend and it is like a ritual that we need once in a while! I'm addicted! I'm a very picky eater when it comes to oily/greasy food but I just cannot resist Don Peppe's:

- Baked Clams (surreal clam goodness, true classic as it can get)
- Linguini with clam sauce (I cannot stop eating this thing! just p-e-r-f-e-c-t)

This place is always PACKED for dinner and especially on the weekends be prepared to wait for a table if you got a big group. If you want to avoid the wait try to come before 7-6 pm. You just know people are there for the food since the place lacks ambiance or any fancy appeal to it. When your food is excellent nothing else matters! Cash only. Waiters are always nice and remember their regulars.
Great food. Excellent service. Cool, old school setting. Fair prices, but not cheap.

I had better food the eggplant parm was burnt and not fully cooked  and chicken Marsala came with 3 pieces of chicken what the hell is that that is not no family size very packed very noisey people seating on top of you sorry I'm sicilano and I had my share of eating out to fancy restaurant and this place was no family style portions and  could have eat at home with all the noise and the waiter was not paying attention at all was looking around I should have went to another restaurant t no BIG deal believe me was not impressed at all save your money and no credit cards allowed really wTf thanks for taking care of the customers NOT oh FYI the silverware and dishes were dirty Really dirty with the the money they make they can afford some new dishes  I would not be going back there for that type of money no way never

This is Authentic Italian Food, OLD School, as they say...
You have to sort of get over the ambience of the place,, It's Not fancifully decorated. There are no Gaudy murals or Gorgeous Chandeliers,, It's just basically a group of tables in a well Lit,,spacious room. To me it's reminiscent of the old days when Italians would get together for a 'block party' and Feast,,(but indoors)  It has that kind of family feel,  The service is....well, lets say, If you're an English Aristocrat,,don't eat here. But if you know how to talk to, and move among Italians,,,You Will enjoy this restaurant. And Let me tell you,,the Food... will Definitely Please. Everything has homemade taste, Fresh,& Flavorful, ...Just fabulous, Family style, traditional home-cooked, Italian Food. Delicious.

This place is a total scene! Umm like a real scene.  Sort of part Godfather part Jersey Shore.  The veal Don Pepe and the linguini and clams were totally solid.  But lets be honest, the real reason to go here is the food and the decor/ ambiance/ people watchgin.  We went on a Sunday night it was busy, the house wine is pretty gross but overall I would go back.  Better then other family style Italian food in NYC.  Totally fairly priced for the huge portion size, you want to come wiht a big party!  Oh and PS- two day laters my breath was still stinky from all the raw red onions and garlic!!! Oh and the cash only thing really adds to the Mobster mood at this place!

the food is very good I tried the "Chicken Marsala" the big downside is the service. as I got there I had to wait a while and to get someones attention just to get a table. the place was dead because of the snow  to the storm. tbat said the waiter should have been more atentive he never came by once to see how the food was I had to actually call him to get the bill. now if you go to Ginos on Cross bay Blvd the Chicken Marsala taste just as good if not better and for $16.95 vs $24.00 of don pepe I would rather go to Ginos a 100 times. when u order Chicken Marsala from don pepe it comes by itself with no side dish ginos gives you an option on 3 different side dishes. I can't see how other people gave don pepe 5 stars I'm only giving it 2 stars only because the chicken Marsala was good.
Amazing food. Excellent service. Family style size portions. The wine list is a little short, just a house made red and house made white, but they did not disappoint either.

Wow,Wow,Wow!!!  I Love This Place! You come here to Eat! This is the best tasting Italian food I've eaten anywhere. Stuffed little neck clams, Stuffed mushrooms, fried egg battered eggplant , stuffed artichokes, whole dish of fried peppers, just to name a few of the amazing appetizers served. The butter, lemon, & garlic sauce that is prepared on the clams and mushrooms you can soak up with the warm fresh Italian bread given to you when you first sit down. Linguine with garlic & oil was the bomb, sweet roasted garlic cloves the size of a 4 karat diamond. Chicken & Veal Don Pepe(fried cutlets covered with tomato brushetta, red onions so tasty) . Only cutlets ever eaten where you use a spoon to cut them, yes a spoon they are so tender. Home made bottles of wine that are great, red or white, (didn't see Brenda & Eddie, you know the king and the queen from the prom). 
This is not a place to come if you are looking for a romantic setting, it's one big brightly lit room, reminded me of a large Chinese restaurant setting, but you do come here to eat, and eat you will. Everything is served family style and the waiter's do a great job. For dessert, the cannoli's were just freaking out of sight. This will be my go to Italian restaurant for many years to come. They have been open since 1968 and the crowds keep coming, it's a family owned business and Mike greets you at the door. They take cash only, and are closed for vacation Feb. 17,2014 - March 3, 2014 reopening March 4.  I expect to be back on that day. Maybe I'll see you there, Ciao
They do not take reservations, first come, first served!

What's left to say that hasn't been said already?
Don Pep's is the real deal!
My favorite's - chicken francese (chicken lemon & butter), spaghetti marinara, linguini w/ clam sauce, and baked clams. Some of the best you will ever have.
Yes, it's off the beaten path in the south of Queens. And yes the decor is plain and simple. But it's all about the food in this old school red sauce (gravy) joint.
Enjoy.

The baked clams here were just amazing, and I really liked there fettuccine with white clam sauce. It tastes very different here compared to a lot of other Italian restaurants, I believe they put garlic into there's, making the flavor really stand out a lot. We got 4 orders of baked clams here, and they all tasted fabulous, only problem is you might get a sore throat afterwards from all the breadcrumbs they use to make it! 

Nonetheless, the service was very friendly and they really try to understand what each customer wants/needs! I would come back here again next time I go to the airport!

Wow love this old school Italian resturant..
Family style so make sure you fasted the entire day for this dinner 
Food is amazing !

Service: Rude, disparaging, domineering

Decor: Drab, dated, dingy

Food: Sloppy, unexceptional, fabricated

If you're looking for a place that makes the same thing, unchanged since 1988, it's fine. If you're looking for a nice dinner experience, try any of the Carmine's in Manhattan or Rao's in East Harlem.

Heard about this place for many years, but being from Brooklyn I just never got around to visiting. Well, finally i made it here. Plenty of parking (come after 7 for no meter parking on the street). Nice gentleman sat us down right away. Place was almost full with many people having a great time eating.

As many other reviews have stated, this is not the place you go for fancy atmosphere.

What you do come here for is possibly the best Italian food in the city.
The food in this place is unbelievable.
My friends & I were amazed at how hot & fresh the dishes came out from the kitchen.
Large menu on the wall with a good selection of dishes.

Having been recommend to this place by a friend, and reading other yelp reviews, I came prepared on what to order, and basically ordered for the whole table.

Our waiter was very nice and attentive. The whole service team was great- bread & water refilled almost instantly. The chef (old man, I think his name is John?) came by and spent a minute with us to make sure we were satisfied (which omg we were)!

Now, down to the important stuff- The food.

We did a double order of baked clams- wow- unbelievable. 
Also stuffed mushrooms and fried peppers- I'm getting hungry just thinking about it.
Be careful- dipping the bread in the sauce of all these dishes can fill you up quick (its hard not to, the sauce/gravy of all these dishes are ridiculous).
Next we went on to Linguini with White Clam Sauce (1 1/2 order as recommended by the waiter, which he was right- perfect for 3 people). This may have been the best linguini with clam sauce i ever had, and my friends also claimed this was their favorite dish of the night.
Finally, we each had our own entree- my friends had the shrimp marinara and the seafood marinara (both right on point).
I went with the Veal Don Peppe- WOW- what a dish- this was by far my favorite dish of the night- crispy breaded veal cutlets, moist on the inside, so tender that the server cut them with a spoon!!! The veal cutlets are covered with a diced tomato/onion salad (bruschetta) that made this a dish to brag about. i am definitely going to be having this dish again.

Barely had room for espresso coffee.

What a great experience.
This is truly one of the best restaurants i have ever been to.
Just writing this review is driving me crazy with craving.
I will see you there TONIGHT!!!!

;)

my family took me out for dinner for my birthday on march 15 and suggested don peppe. we were a party of 7..we heard from others who have dined here in the past on how great their dining experience was . we also checked the reviews on  yelp and tripadvisor and zagat  and found great reviews. we however did not have such a great experience. we knew that there would be a wait but not 2 and a half hours(we should have not not been told  the wait was 30 minutes) we could have dined elsewhere but decided to stay and wait . we were getting anxious and hungry. the service was less than perfect. we knew how busy they are but we felt as if we were being rushed ,in fact the waiter told us what to order rather than us deciding. the  waiter was not very attentive and at times could not find him at all. once the food arrived we dugged into it(family style) because we were starving. the food  did not live up to the hype in our opinion. it was good but not worth waiting several hours for.
for a 550 dollar bill we did not get what we paid for. 
we tried it and i am sure it is good for most of the reviewers but not for us
sorry we wont be going back to dine there..

it was a memorable birthday but not in a good way
what a shame...really wanted to give five stars....but couldnt...

I went to this place after watching entourage. I was comig home from the airport and was in the mood for a good home cook Italian dinner. We went with a  group and the place was great! Beat all expectations - very reasonable price point for both food and wine. The waiters were all extremely helpful! If you are in town and can get it- definitely try it out!!!
Excellent quality Italian food, cash only though. I can't name a better Italian place in NY  besides my aunt Rosas house. Try the shrimp and the clams
Baked clams , Mussels marinara ,Shrimp Luciano over pasta and a bottle of house wine. Simply put the food is great... totally worth a trip..get there early or your gonna wait.

....Take the cannoli. My fiancé and I came here with his cousin for dinner and the food was excellent. It's best to come here with several people because everything is served family style and you're going to want to try several dishes. We ordered the house chilled aka cold red wine to start. It's terrible but it becomes drinkable once it hits room temperature. 

We ordered the baked clams and mussels in red sauce for appetizers and the veal Don Peppe and shrimp Luciano for our entrees and everything was amazing with the baked clams being the best dish of the night. They were perfect. 

The food is consistently good and the service is service. They bring the food. That's it. Unfortunately, we didn't have room for dessert but we've tried some in the past and they are very good. Come here with an appetite. You'll need it.

Amazing food, amazing place. Not much to look at but don't be discouraged by that this place is top notch. 

Came here with a bunch of buds for my birthday and let me tell you this place is on point! We started off with eggplant rollatini and baked clams as the appetizer, AMAZING! For entrees we had linguini with red clam sauce and rigatoni with broccoli as our pastas and then the veal don peppe and chicken sciarpatella for our meats. The veal is one of the best things I ever had, so tender and tasty. The pastas were both amazing, they don't sound like much to talk about but trust me DO NOT be fooled. The chicken left me dissatisfied but everyone else at the table loved it so they get a pass on that. 

House red wine is great. We kept it flowing all night. The service is also very great, the servers put the food on your dish for you, it's family style so they made that all work out pretty easily. 

All in all for my first time they get an A+ rating by me and I cannot wait to go back there more often. Just some advice come here with a bunch of cash (they don't accept cards) and a healthy appetite and you will not go wrong!

The next time my ManWich says to me "We gotta go to this restaurant, its really good" I'm making plans to go the following day because he knows what he's talking about.

This place alone has made up for all the terrible meals and service I've had in the past 5 years.  We were fortunate enough to get seated right away - from what I understand you may have a little bit of a wait - but let me tell you, now that I've eaten here, if I come back tomorrow and they tell me I have to wait two hours for a table, you'll find me in that cute little porch area drooling.

its family style, and they have the menu on the wall on a big chalk board.  If there's anything special, the guy will let you know, but here's what you should order:

1. baked clams.  If you're with four people total, order 12 each.  I'm serious.  We're fat.  we ordered 2 dozen to start, ate them in five seconds, and ordered another two dozen.  Whatever, we're hungry

2. Linguine with clam sauce.  I kid you not, this was the best linguine I've ever had in my entire life, topped with the best clam sauce I've ever had in my entire life, that had big hunks of clams swimming in it and floating on giant cloves of roasted garlic

3. Veal Don Pep - If you're with people that don't like veal, order it anyway and let them try it.  You'll convert them.  One of my friends isn't a big veal eater, so we ordered it with chicken and they brought out veal accidentally...and it was tender and juicy and fried perfectly with this delicious, bright bruschetta on top

4. Tartufo and Cannoli - and espresso's.  When in Rome!

We also ordered the Shrimp Luchiana and a stuffed artichoke - which were both phenom, but the baked clams and the linguine were literally so good, we couldn't think of anything else.  I would have happily eaten another plate of pasta...and I'm not really a big pasta eater.

We had their house wines (bottle o red, bottle o white) and they were both good.  The bill?  Completely completely fair - especially considering nearly half of it was spent on clams.  I didn't think it was over priced at all, we had a great time, and a delicious meal.  Cash only, as you can see from everyone else's reviews. 

Oh - friendly tip - if you're coming here, wear something with a little give.  Sure, you can pretend you're going to be a "lady" or a "gentleman" but once you get a load of the smells and the food in here, all those manners go out the window.  I was drinking the left over baked clam sauce with the serving spoon.  And I don't care who knows.

I come here a lot with my family. The food is fantastic and always consistent. I love the fact that half the room is always filled with wise-guys, it adds to the authenticity of the meal. 

Highly recommend the shrimp Luciano over liguini, the lemon chicken and the veal/chicken don't Pepe. 

When you are done order a canoli its better than any bakery can offer. Also, was fortunate to try a tiramasu that they rarely have and is not on the menu. Best damn tiramasu!

This place is one of the best Italian restaurants in New York. I have been coming here for years and can't even think of one bad experience. Everything from here is awesome. The baked clams and veal don pepe is a must. CASH ONLY. Maybe my only beef with the place and that's not even really a big deal. Don't even think about it if you haven't been here, this place can't be beat.

I think this place is a solid a 4.5. Went here on mothers day 2014 and the wait was short and they seem to be efficient on rotating tables. The place is relaxed and a little tired looking. They did have an ample waiting room.

We tried the house wine which was ok. I heard it might of been homemade but I couldn't tell or it could of been box. Downside here is there is no bar and no liquor. I like a drink when out and so a half point deduction.

 But drinks aside we are here for the food. Starting with the clams they were good but nothing more at $ 21 for an order of is 12 kind of a rip off at almost 2 dollars each for a small tiny clam. I could of had oysters at that price duh! Then we had the shrimp Luciano on a bed of linguni. It was  OK but it didn't come off as an Italian dish to me. That onion sauce could of went well with German food like a breaded cutlet or sausage.  Don't get me wrong it was good but seemed out of place when I wanted Italian. Then we had the chicken scap.  This was excellent and done perfect. I was impressed that the chicken was crispy and moist. It included sausage peppers onions and potatoes. Very well executed.

I will definitely return to try other menu items.

Amazing!!!! Must try the shrimp Luciano ! I'm not a fan of shrimp but at don peps it's hard not to love it.  Overall my experience here has been great.  Food is consistently tasty and amazing. They have large family style portions and many options to choose from. Aside from the shrimp Luciano being my absolute favorite, I also enjoy the chicken parmigiana, baked clams, and linguine with white clam sauce.  The wait staff and hostess are always welcoming. Keep up the good work!

Wow.   It's as good as it gets....From Ronkonkoma L. I.    I Love the Baked Clams, and the Linguine with clam sauce.   you never tasted anything so good.   Being brought up in an old fashioned Italian Family from Italy..... mom cooked close to this...but wow, progress has made it even better.   Don't waste your money in other restaurants....here's where its at....it don't get no better than this.    I can t wait to go back.

Yep, this is the place you're looking for if you want the quintessential NYC Italian American dinner experience.  The menu is unique, the veal don peppe is a true original.  They took extra good care of my father who doesn't walk well.  Service was great, no complaints.  It's cash only, it's not cheap, but it's worth the price on all levels.

My husband has been coming here with his family since he was a little boy in the '60s - the food is home cooking at its best and the portions are abodanza!!!  We went there on our first date and we had zuppa de mussels and steak pizziola.  I was hooked right then ;)  There's home-made house wines red or white. No other alcohol is served there. I've had so many things off of that chalkboard menu since that first date and every dish outdoes the one before it.  My favs are the baked clams, linguine w/clam sauce, chicken/veal Don Pepe, Suffed Artichoke and cold tomato/greenbean salad.  Who am I kidding I can't even name favs because I'd have to keep writing all day!  Just go.  If you have a craving for grandma's old world cooking and can't make it yourself, then take your family over for the best meal served family style.  If you're lucky enough to be there on a night when the cheesecake is ready, OMG is all I can say.

This place is the best family style Italian restaurant in NY.  When I lived in NY we always went here but now that I live in Florida I could only go here when I'm visiting. It's to bad I can't find any Italian restaurant that even comes close to Don Pepe. Love, love this place the service is great and food amazing. I promise you, you won't be disappointed. If you go once you'll want to return again and again. The only downside is they only take cash.

My boss Jack can't stop raving about this place like it was the best Italian restaurant in the whole of New York & I remember stopping here once,  years ago but didn't quite leave an imprint on me... I guess it all depends upon the kind of food you order. Don Peppe is located at 135-58 Leffert's Blvd, South Ozone Park, between 135 & 149th Ave, 11420.

Well, last Friday my boss took us all to Don Peppe's  & specially ordered his favorite dishes.   It was also to celebrate one of our lawyers ....Pat's birthday. We all crammed up in his small car, 5 of us in the back seat, and 2 in the front seat, we were lucky we didn't bump into a cop otherwise we could have been flagged down.  As soon as we we were seated.......

He started his litany of orders starting from the 4 bottles of wine...Bread in Baskets & butter. then came the Baked Clams, Don Peppe Special Salad, Pimento & Anchovies for appetizers..We didn't even wait for the celebrant as he was tide up in court with a client.

Then came the Pasta, Two kinds of Linguini, One with White Clam Sauce & with the other with Red Clam Sauce, It was delicious. (my favorite so far)  The celebrant arrived at this point.

Then came the Veal Parmagiana, Breast of Chicken Marsala with Peppers, Mushrooms & Sausages, & the Lobster Fra Diavolo with Clams, Mussels & Calamari . It was awesome!!

The Desserts  were equally appetizing too. Freshly made  Cannoli, Cheesecake &, Lemonchelo. It was glutony at its best!!! We can't hardly move after that..
The waiters were all so attentive & on the go, Very pleasant bunch....BTW, No cards please Just Bring your cash!!!....

If you want good Italian food in NY, you gotta go to Don Peppe. While it's not the most amazing Italian food I've ever had, its authenticity brings the customers classic Italian fare.

First of all, Don Peppe does not take reservations. Get there early. If not, expect a wait. 

Second, go with friends. Lots of them. So you can try everything.

Third, bring cash. Plenty of it. 

Lastly, save the bread for dipping.

My friends and I were well prepared. We arrived for an early dinner and were seated immediately. There are no menus. All the items are listed on a chalkboard. We followed the 3 aforementioned rules up until we asked for Penne Alla Vodka. it's akin to asking for a California Roll at an authentic Japanese restaurant. We made that mistake. It's the type of embarrassment only a foodie would endure.

We ended up sharing:
Baked Clams
Linguini with White Clam Sauce
Veal Parm 
Shrimp Luciano
Cannolis

Every single bite was cooked faultlessly with the perfect complement of sauces. The Veal Parm, especially, was melt-in-your-mouth tender. 

The cannolis are not to be missed. They are enormous and can easily be split between 2 people (if you're willing to share).

This is a classic and is still amazing after all these years.  The salad Don Pepe and Baked Clams, followed by Linguine with clam sauce and the Veal Don Pepe is a can't miss meal.  Depending on how many people are dining you can add the stuffed articoke as a starter and a number of other dishes will not disappoint.  Great capuccino and fruit sorbets, spumoni, tartufo, cannolis and Tortoni!
Simply the best Italian food I have had, i've been here numerous times and cannot say 1 negative thing.

Unusually there was no "but" at the end of my wife's "I really like this place". I followed previous Yelp reviews and would just add that the pasta sauces are excellent and the house red is fine (no label)

Simply stated, Don Peppe is king! There are italian restaurants and then theres Don Peppe. Unmatched in nearly every menu item. Been coming here since I was a baby (24 years old now) and it has tasted the same exact way every time. Best baked clams, linguini and clams, veal Milanese (named veal don peppe) and shrimp Luciano on the face of this earth! Do yourself a favor and get here immediately!

This place isn't good at all, it sucks. First off, they made me take off my beanie when i walked in the door, I understand if you're my mother and it was a old school familly dinner but this is a shitty itialian place in the middle of nowhere with old itialian guys wearing shitty mechanic shirts. Second, we ordered the fettuccine prosciutto, I love prosciutto. There was one major problem: there was basically no prosciutto. If you're going to put it in the name I had better be seeing it on the plate or tasting it when i eat, i got neither. Also- the bill was $45 cash only (nothing wrong there) I put $60 on the table and asked for change when the waiter came by...I waited for atleast 20 minutes and no one ever came back to the table. At this point I was fed up and just left. I would definitely not recommend coming here at all, I will never go back and make sure that everyone knows how bad this place is at the hotels in the area.

PS: the sauce literally tastes like they got some Ragu from the store (the pasta was cooked properly though). My family makes homemade sauce all the time and you can taste the difference, this is totally canned junk.

DO NOT GO HERE

Came back.  Great place to eat a great dinner before dropping someone off at the airport (or eat here before you fly away).

For the same price you'd pay for airport fare, why not come here and have a great meal?  Go.  

Also, more Italian people were here yet again.  Great sight.

Just went to this place a  few days ago 
. I went their cause my girl firmed and I were watching entourage and we heard Don Peppes and needed see if this place was for real so we went and the food was amazing. It was pretty cool going to a place that was in my very TV show for some time.

Don Peppe is legitimately authentic. Just go - the staff, ambience and food is great. Be mindful, food is served family style, which allows me to enjoy multiple items. So eager to eat, no time to photograph.

For a group of 5, here's what we ordered: Hold off on the bread (wait for it). We got 2 orders of baked clams, so delicious and not overly salty. After clams have been dispersed, this is when you take the bread and dip it in the remaining sauce from the baked clams. Clam linguine lots of garlic. Shrimp linguine w pink clear sauce and onions. Chicken don Peppe, pounded breaded chicken w 'pico de gallo' atop.

I never give 5 stars, to anything, ever. 
I have lived in NY for more years than I like to say and I don't know how I missed this. 
If you want perfect pasta, perfect old school Italian in NY. Skip everywhere else, Mulberry St., Arthur Ave, etc. go here. 
Shrimp Luciano, wow. I want that as my breakfast every day. I hear it's named after  "Lucky" which just adds to the mysterious deliciousness of gossip of this place. 
Baked clams are also promoted on t shirts, and they were, of course, magical. 
I wanted other things, but it was two of us and a baby (btw they were sweet and welcoming to her.)
Atmosphere and ambiance? Come on....If you want dim lights, mixed cocktails and tuna carpaccio go elsewhere. But for fantastic and memorable pasta and lovable servers, come here. 
All cash. No reservations.  It is what it is, which is kind of great.

I won't lie, we probably would not have known about Don Peppe Vesuvio if it weren't for another crew. Vince, Drama, E and Turtle. Yes..HBO 30-minute comedy show runner brought us to this New York staple. 

First off, it's in the middle of Ozone Park which was formerly an Italian neighborhood like much of Queens. No reservations and no plastic accepted. You have to love the drab appearance of it inside, it's like a restaurant set from a soap opera. If you've been here, you know what I'm talking about. Don't bother asking for a menu, it's on the wall and it looks like it could also be used interchangeable to tell you who won bingo night too.

While this may not be my favorite Italian I've ever eaten, it's certainly up there. The waiters here are old school no-nonsense standup guys. My first time dining here I was told, "No alfredo or vodka sauce, guy". Gotta love it.

Baked clams is a must and I will say that that is the best I will ever have. I'm all for "one shots" but these babies are HOT. The bread crumbs are so light and the juice/sauce is just fantastic. Now the rule for everyone is to use the bread to mop that good stuff up. I'm a sick puppy, I take spoonfuls. Yes, spoonfuls!

We typically get two pastas when we go there. Linguini with white clam sauce and the spaghetti with shrimp sauce. The linguini is done very well, lots of garlic as is appropriate and cooked flawlessly. Great clam flavor. The spaghetti with shrimp sauce may actually be in my top five pastas. A simple pomodoro sauce with red pepper and shrimp. This is how good pasta should taste though, simple good old home cooking. 

Prepare yourself for the veal don peppe. Fred Flintstone style veal cutlets topped with a catering size portion of bruschetta. This veal is so tender that they serve it to you with spoons! If that's not comfort food, I don't know what is. 

Aside from the food, it really is a fun experience between the characters you see in here and all the history if you ask around. While this may not be the same Vesuvio from The Sopranos, it's not far off. 

Take the trip out there, you won't be disappointed.

Looking for real Italian food here's the place to visit. This is no olive garden :-D and not located in little Italy but in Queens!

Make sure you leave home those plastics, cash only!!

Fat Peter rating system. 
as follows: 
STARS- standard yelp
CHANCE I WILL BE BACK- YES
Why I went  - its Don Peppe

Wasn't that good.. I was expecting more WOW all i got was a ok pat on back.  I never tried cocaine or meth either but imagine day you try and its like smoking a cigarette.  what do you want me to say??

Great restaurant and service. Food came out a bit slow but it was very busy. They did dishes one at a time and the in between times were kind of long. Otherwise food is amazing. Baked clams were great, linguini with white clam sauce was one of the best I've had, the veal don pepe was also one of the best I've had. Bit pricey but dishes are big. Would definitely recommend and eat at again.

I drove over 1.5 hours and $23 in tolls from New Jersey only to learn that the restaurant was closed for vacation from 8/4 - 9/1/14 .  It would have been nice if this was noted on their website and Yelps site.

Went to Don Pepe to try and have some great Italian while on a layover at JFK.  This really is the first time I have been disappointed with such a highly ranked yelped restaurant.  

We tried the Shrimp Pasta and their famous clam linguini.  The Linguini was so disappointing especially since they are known for this dish.  Extremely  greasy and very underwhelming flavor.  

The shrimp pasta was ok.  Something I would expect at a buco de peppo chain.   The biggest disappointment was the pasta.  Thats what makes a great italian dish.  The pasta was certainly not fresh nor handmade.  I literally could have  made the above meal at home and kept my $100.  

And to top the experience off they didn't have the cheesecake or tiramisu for desert.

Wah---wah.  For the price and quality...high disappointing.  

I would not recommend making the trip from JFK for this lackluster experience. Go to terminal 4 and get a shake shack burger. 10X the value and taste.

Come with a group and be prepared to take home a "doggie bag"  but you'd have to be crazy to give this food to the dogs. The chicken parm is great and the pasta is very authentic. Avoid the steak, it's overpriced but the stuffed peppers are worth it.  Beware this place is CASH ONLY.

Quite possibly the best italian food we've tasted. Not sure of the location since we don't usually go to ozone park... but what a gem.

the veal was excellent and the eggplant and baked clams. wow . so glad i have a new spot now

Don Peppe...  the food is 5 stars...  however, if you take no offense to the rudeness of the staff, the management.  If you take no offense to being handed the check and literally asked to leave just as your dessert is being served..  the reason,  "They need the table"     what can I say..   except ..  never again!    
if in Queens, I'd go with Vetro or Matteo's..  at least they are civil!

Wow!   Everything everyone wrote about!  A MUST show if you are in NYC Queens!

There is nothing I can add it except it was as good as advertised.

I ordered the eggplant parm. The food was good but on par with other places I've tried. I wasn't a big fan of the service or should I say lack of it. My server only came by 3x. I did not even have my drink filled once. Maybe I should come with my Italian friends and then maybe I will get better service.

The classic, and maybe the best Italian baked clams in Howard Beach, head to head with Lenny's. And this place has got so much history too. You can see why it got hype from "Entourage" and why the mob and Fat Tony made this place famous. A true old-time original "only-in-NY" type of restaurant. Of course order the white linguine with clam sauce, and also veal with eggplant or veal with peppers and mushrooms. A little expensive, but worth it. Cash only!

If you have ridiculously horrible vision such as I do , you'll most likely go blind attempting to read the menu ( which is on the wall) Not crazy about ordering family style and definitely not crazy about the food. Luckily I eat like a bird , but for those who actually spend money to eat like a king ,prepare for the food poisoning of a lifetime . Don't say I didn't warn you!

I cannot believe that I have waited this long to write a review for Don Pepe. The food here is the most authentic Italian food I have ever ate in my entire life.

Don't pepe it is a hidden gem, hidden in a residential neighborhood, the restaurant itself is covered in black tint windows, it always looks closed, Almost as if they want to keep the secret that the best Italian food in New York City exists inside those walls.

The food here at don't Pepe is beyond anything I can describe, the best to describe the food here don't Pepe is large and delicious, a must try for all.

The garlic bread is a must, spaghetti with meat sauce Is a must, Linguine with clam sauce is a must and you must go with an empty stomach.

Get your ass to Don Pepe ASAP.

To start off: you know you're at a great place when you have to travel into the heart of Queens to find the restaurant and there is still a long wait for a table. The food did not disappoint. Spaghetti in Clam Sauce and Chicken Cutlet Parmigiana were fantastic. 

The atmosphere is a fun one, but don't expect something super classy. There are no menus, just a big board at the back of the restaurant (though the menu is online if you're really opposed to walking over to the board). The dining room is one big space decorated with equestrian themed pictures. The staff is nice, though can be a bit inattentive with the amount of diners eating there. The only reason I gave this four and not five stars was because we were given our silverware one piece at a time, because they had to wait for other diners to finish eating, clean them, and then send them over, because they had a shortage. It was the same while trying to get a glass of water, which a bit frustrating. All that aside though, the food is worth it.

Family style ONLY. Very bright. Awkwardly bright. They don't give you menus. There is one big menu on the wall (like at Burger King) and you order from that. Baked clams tasted like any other so nothing amazing here. Wait staff is attentive. They do not stray from the family style rule at all though. They are very precise about what the menu says and they will not change anything for you.
best itialian food in the whole entire world. I would keep writing here for days if my hands didn't get tired

If you want really authentic, home cooked italian food then Don Peppe is the place. Yea its far and not easy to get to, but the food is worth it. 

I was lucky to snag my brothers car. Came out here with my girlfriend and tried a few of the pasta plates and the chicken parmagiana. 

Everything was delicious! Service was spot on too.

food is to die for. 

Cash only and no reservations but when it's this good they can do that

This place is a gem! The Italian food here is one of the best around. Every dish you order is so authentic. The baked clams are the best id ever had. The spaghetti with white clam sauce is out of this world. The veal don Pepe is a must along with the shrimp louciano. If ur in the neighborhood it's truly a must go!
No words necessary. It is the go to place for authentic Italian food.

We have never had a meal here that is not absolutely delicious.  I have only one complaint, Mr. Mike, the owner: the waiter started to set the table for the next party even before we had put our coats on!  And the restaurant wasn't even full yet!  Not nice.  However, we are still coming back, of course.
Really good Italian food.  They have a pasta dish with shrimp and some kind of butter sauce that's to die for. You won't be disappointed.

Went to Don Peppe's last Saturday. The wait was more than 1/2 hour. We finally got seated. The food was very good, tho I've had better Italian food in Forest Hills and the city. House wine was surprisingly good too. Portions were generous, true family style fashion. 

So why am I only giving them one star you ask. Well, after we were "prompted" to pay we settled the bill...we lingered at our table for a few more minutes. I was finishing my wine. A guy (owner or manager?) came to our table and asked us to leave as there were people waiting to be seated. We waited to be seated too! Okay, we want to be considerate, we get that. But, he could've told us in a nicer way. He was RUDE and we felt that he didn't care about us, as customers. It was like, you paid, now get out! No class at all. We will never go back there again!!

I went to Don Peppes with my boyfriend who lives in Ozone Park. He'd never been there before either, but had read about the place in Entourage (on HBO), and then read somewhere that mafia guys frequent the place. I love mafia movies so we went there one afternoon for lunch. The one complaint I have is that our white table cloth was stained with red sauce. Otherwise the place was cool. There was a couple of wiseguys sitting a couple of tables away from us, everytime they spoke they would whisper in each other's ears and cover their mouths. Just like in the movies. No idea if these were "connected" guys (lol) but it sure seemed like it. Then the food came. The clams were out of control..the best I ever had in my life.. we had I think 3 orders of baked clams. The prices were kind of high, I think we spent over $200 on just myself and my boyfriend for just lunch. Well, we do eat a lot, but still... that's kind of pricey. I still recommend it.

I have been going to don peeps s
 For 49 years.  My dad would take us once a week. I loved it. At 8 I was hooked!!  During the last year I have noticed changes.  The bread is stale. They skimp on lemons. They don't give u new plates or silver wear.   We had to ask for lemons,Plates and cheese.  The owner screams at employees. He actually asked us to leave after spending $250.00 Because he needed the table.  After eating there last night and seeing the to go food we ordered. I'm done!! I will never eat there again,  it's a shame. When dad owned it it was wonderful,nowu. Have a hard headed son. Who is NOT a people person in. Control
Ciao Bella!!!

The food here is fresh ,simple ,unfussy,authentic Italian, and absolutely delicious ! You may like me be a little intimidated when going in an old school Italian  spot and getting a quick once over but believe  me the food here is worth any initial feelings of hmmmm do I belong here ! My friend and I were greeted by a very handsome man the host maybe , who  saw us and motioned the number  2 and waved us right inside the dining area I  was like how  you doin when he placed a hand on my shoulder and welcomed us in .It definitely feels like a scene straight out of good fellas or the sopranos,  it's an old fashioned Italian restaurant filled with lots of old fashioned Italian people  . We decided on the chicken don pepe tender chicken pan-fried to crisp perfection with a juicy tomato chopped tomato ,onion and garlic sauce on top, baked zitti, and broccoli with garlic and olive oil all super fresh and delicious ! I would definitely come back especially since it's less than ten minutes from my home .

This is Better than Carmines in the City! (IMO)
Friendly Staff, Huge portions (family style).

2 adults and 2 kids, ordered:

Apptetizer
-Baked Clam -  RECOMMENDED (So far my favorites!)
-Stuffed Mushrooms
and 2 main dishes
- Spaguetti with Garlic and Oil (Simple but delicious).
- Baked Ziti (for the kids).  They enjoyed it, Cheesy (kept pulling / breaking the cheese).  

It was soo much food, that we only shared one dessert
Tartuffo. 

Food comes pretty quick. 
Always busy, expect noises because is more of a family style.
Staffs were very attentive.

****************************CASH ONLY************************
Food is amazing. Better come hungry and with big company. No reservations and cash only. Looks like nothing from inside or outside but the food is truly authentic, huge family style.

Had a great & Marco provided us with excellent service.  The veal piccata is outstanding, but only enough for 2 people, unlike every other dish which is enough for 4 people if you're going to eat a few items.  Whether you're passing through, live in the neighborhood, or have time to burn while waiting for someone arriving at JFK, try Don Peppe's.

food is as good as it gets and so is the service! they go above and beyond here to serve you!

 first time here so didnt know what to expect but ive heard rave reviews from friends so i decided to take my buddy and a few friends here last night for his birthday..they dont take reservations which i thought was a bit odd these days but once everybody in my party was there they got us seated right away..

we asked the waiter what was good so we took his advice and got served a new dish every 15 mins not only that but he also cut the food into portions so we didnt over order. i also brought a cake with me for my friends bday and they had it prepared and walked it out with the candles on it with out me even having to ask them!!! excellent job don peps!
Nice family style southern Italian food. Cash only. good food. Enjoyed the shrimp Luciano,pasta marinara, linguine with white clam sauce, artichoke

Been here a few times in the past and decided to come here last week. 
Food remains the same, same menus on wall, same plating, same service, same MSG coma after eating. 
Same, same, shame.....

Adios, Don peppe.

Old school family style place. If you are from the area this is probably the bees knees. But those us from the west coast are not impressed.  Average food, average wine, decent service, high priced for what it is. The cafeteria style room is slightly unsettling to most since it is one large strip mall type room (no separate bar, greeting/host area, etc) with obtuse lighting. And heed everyone else's warning, cash only which I probably should have read. Luckily I had enough cash, but what type of restaurant has probably a $50 per person average tab and doesn't take major credit cards?

Freaking AMAZING. Perfect family style NYC Queens Italian. You're not going to find better. Bring a pile of cash. It's worth every bit of it. You'll be treated like ... family. If you want to be treated better than that, go somewhere else. If you want it quiet, go somewhere else. If you want cheap, go somewhere else.

This place is possibly the best Italian food in New York. Been here many times. Always a fantastic meal. If you have not been here you need to check it out. Ok, so a year and a half later, back again for the 4th or 5th time since I wrote this review. Never mind possibly. This IS the best Italian food you are gonna get. Period.

Three of us came here on a Saturday in January after my beloved dog Hannibal passed.  Parking is a hassle.  We parked on a street.  We were seated immediately for 7:00 dinner.  It's not a fancy place...homestyle.  Service is excellent...very quick!  All male wait staff.  We ordered the baked clames, linguini with white clam sauce and the chicken with peppers and mushrooms.  Everything tasted like home cooking...smthg my grandpa would make.  Excellent but no finesse if you could understand what I mean.  The baked clams I would not order again.  They leave the clam whole and add some breadcrumb mixture to the top.  Definitely not over the top.  The linguine w white clam was delish.  The chicken w peppers was aight.  Peppers were excellent but again the chicken mixture was smthg grandpa could make.  I would definitely come back but I was not overly impressed, but then again not everyone has Italian family that cooks better.  The house wine, however, I was really digging. The place is really loud so I don't think bringing kids would be problematic even thought I only saw one kid around the age of 3 there.

Came here on a Saturday evening and was very crowded.  This place is very loud, and very cramped for space.  We ordered eggplant rollintini which was blah, needed salt and so did their Chicken Marsala.  We ordered a side order of broccoli in olive oil and garlic which the garlic was burnt.  Over all I don't know what the hype is.  I don't think I would return,  it's over rated.  I've tried better Italian food from a pizzeria.

My favorite Italian restaurant. Always will dine here with the family in a large group for special occasions. Love the clams and calamari.  Family style entrees always good for pasta and meatballs. Fun, lively ambiance with good service.  Keep up the good work!!!
