It lived up to the hype. Killer linguine n clam sauce. House wine was really good. Cash only sucked and was embarrassing.

This place is by far the BEST Italian establishment I've ever been to. I first heard of this place on HBO's Entourage a few years back. I recently did some research for a good Italian restaurant in my area and this name was at the top of the list. It was literally 5 minutes from home! I decided to take my fiancé here as soon as I looked at the menu. He absolutely loved it. As soon as I walked in, I felt as if I were in Italy. The staff is really nice and courteous. The cooks were having some wine and playing spades. You felt as if you have entered someone's home. 
      The most popular dish on their menu is the Veal Don Peppe. It is quite a pricey dish at $42.00 but worth every penny. The meat is of a great quality. It is topped of with diced tomatoes and onions. It was a great tasting dish. When you come here you must order a bottle of red wine. It is made in house and tastes divine. Pairs well with any of their dishes. 
       Another great dish is the Linguine in Garlic & OIl. The portion in this dish is rather large. 2 or more can easily share this plate and be satisfied. It is a simple dish, the garlic and oil used for it gives it a rich and interesting flavor. Definitely recommend this option. 
        Lastly, for dessert you need to try a cannoli. It was really the best cannoli I've tried. The blows the ones from Fortunato's in Little Italy out of the water. You can tell how fresh they are and it definitely leaves you wanting seconds. 
         The one thing I would add is that by no means is this a cheap eatery. The menu is a bit pricey but you are paying for the quality. You can sense the high grade quality of their food from the first bite. Believe me on this one, if you enjoy Italian food you will love Don Peppe's. Plenty of celebrities and athletes have come from all over the world to try this amazing place. Check it out for yourself. It'll change your perception on Italian food forever!

Food was very impressive. Service, less so. Allow me to expound.

Food: the broccoli rabe with sausage was too salty. The pastas were phenomenal! We had the pasta with shrimp and pasta with clam sauce. Our party of ten also had an order of mussels, clams and salad for appetizer. Clams were great, but mussels and salad were not impressive - totally not worth the money. Most hings appeared to have been drowned in garlic, olive oil and/or butter. Yes! Tip: ORDER THE TABLE WINE! AMAZING! Made on the premises, too.

Service: this is where it loses one star. Our party's intention was to order multiple pastas to share, but our server advised against it for whatever reason. He also took the liberty of ordering multiple portions of things we distinctly ordered only one of... What...? Not sure what he was thinking but yeah... not really acceptable. 

The above would not have mattered as much, but there is more. I overheard a server describing a "Chinese guy" as an "*expletive deleted* *rear-end anus*." To this server's credit, I do not believe that he was mentioning ethnicity in a derogatory way. He was merely describing the customer who had a bad attitude or asked for something that the customer should not have. But still, I have sensitive ears, I am seated but am 6 feet 2 inches tall, so I hear you man. Do you think my table of ten Chinese people are coming back? Maybe not...

Decor: everything here is super cramped, excluding the restroom, which was large and clean.

I live in Manhattan and have eaten at so many Italian places. This one takes the cake.  You can not go wrong with anything on the menu. The linguini and clam sauce and don Pepe veal special are my favorites. It makes the trip out to queens worth it every time!

The best Italian food ever!!! Been coming here for years. You must try the Don Peppe Veal and the Linguini with Garlic and Oil or Clams. Theres not a dish they make that doesn't taste good. Fresh simple but so good. The baked clams and burnt broccoli are also favorites. They have no menu. The menu is on the wall and served family style. Cash only and not so cheap. Try a bottle of their house made wine...so good youll want to take a bottle home.

Worse restaurant ever
No service - after half an hour of sitting down. Only 3 tables had people too. Shaking my head at management. 
Menu on a board
Dirty filthy

The last couple of times I've been here i have been overcharged for pasta. a couple of weeks ago I got baked zit which is the best I ever had and thought I would try the shrimp luciano which everybody raves about. So I placed a to go order in the restaurant and was given a total of 62 dollars for both meals so I said wait a minute the baked ziti is 17 the shrimp luciano is 24 dollars The waiter tells me the shrimp Luciano on the menu is a appetizer you wanted the meal with the linguine: I did not feel like putting up a big stink so I just ordered it but their prices are ridiculous  and other time I got baked ziti and spaghetti with garlic and oil and it came out to 48 dollars??? I am ordering pasta not 3 streaks from a steakhouse absurd prices for Italian food and here is the kicker they claim to be family style and yet I can eat both meals in one sitting no way is this family style. I am done with this place the food is good but not worth the aggravation of Different prices every time you go their

First off I just wanna say that I don't really like the Menu on the wall. I can't see too good and ended up ordering the wrong thing. It was still bomb though. This place is deff not family style because it was just enough food for 1 person. The baked clams were easily 10/10 could eat them every day. Mad crunchy. Not too clammy and the breadcrumbs were fuego. Bomb 10/10. 

After the baked clams I ordered Spagetti with White Clam Sauce. Next level macaroni kid. Just the wright amount of White Clam Sauce. Perfect blend of garlic too. I never thought I'd come to say this, but it was much better than my Mama's Linguine I grew up on. I told my mom she's gotta step her game up. Big Tom was right. Breadsticks on point too bro. Can't believe how crispy they were. 10/10 for the dinner. 

For dessert I had like 6 or 7 cannolis, all fuego, but I kinda lost count. Cream was through the roof. Shell had perfect crunch and a few of them even had chocolate chips on them which I never seen before. Prob coulda ate more. 

My 1 complaint was that it is cash only so I had to run to an ATM down the block which was kinda annoying to be honest. Paid the bill and left pretty happy.

Driving to Don Peppes on Lefferts Blvd through four ethnic neighborhood changes, further exemplifies why NYC is so unique, all of the diversitys, all within a few blocks. 

Arriving at Don 'effin' Pep's, as my gombatachich affectionately refers to it as, on the Tuesday after Easter I realized, that this was my first meal here in a decade. 

Ambiance and decour remains the same as it was back was a kid, circa 1970's, simple trattoria style. After reaching Hollywood like popularity with the advent of Entourage, popularized to the whole common and free world, I was a bit hesitant to return.

Don Pepps as anticipated, keeps the good food rolling out decade after decade and fickle ownership remains, in that, opening and closing can occur at any time without rhyme or reason. Legend has it that a few early closings on Friday and Saturday night's have even occurred, early closings.

With never more than two specials, likely only one, the food is not current traditional American Italian. Certain items are not available, meatballs and garlic bread for example, but both seem to be available on every Italian food menu across the country.

Why is the lasagna that's available only a few times a year so incredibly delicious? The best friggin' ricotta cheese is used. Not typical in look nor composition, the noodles of the lasagna are bigger and thicker, making the dish densely filling.

Luck struck again as the veal chop was available. When I used to order it years back, it was either unavailable or sold out. Super meaty, super tender the chop appears boiled, top it with their secret wet glazy seasoning, bam! Sorry, I don't know the ingredients of the glaze.

The Chicken and Veal Parmesan are so tasty, its hard to not inhale the food quickly, and no matter how full you are when you leave, somehow you still want more, at least I do. Typically when I consume food to that uber level, I pay for it the next day, which never happens after a Don Pep face stuffing.

In short, there's no fancy food here, nothing exotic. It's plain and simple Italian ingredient arithmetic. Sauce, cheese, meat and nobody does it better.

It's ok, not A-OK, just ok. which is why I am giving it two stars.

I am actually surprised by the 4/5 star reviews.  My friend has been coming here for a while and raves about it (she is not Italian) so she invited me and my bf, we went with 2 other couples.  


First off, I hate that it is so bright in this place, can't you dim the lights a little for dinner service?  I hate that I have to read a menu off the wall, it's only on 1 section of the wall and if I was sitting further away I wouldn't be able to read it.  There is a table in front of the wall menu and when people are sitting there you can't read the bottom.  We all left it to my friend to order since she has been there many times and I straining my neck to read the menu.

Our food was average, to me at least.  We ordered mozz and tomato salad, ok, baked clams were good but small.  We had pasta with plain marinara sauce, again just ok, basic.  I do admit that the chicken we ordered was good, I forgot what they called it but  basically it was chicken Milanese.  Also some type of shrimp, which was ok, it needed more flavor, garlic, salt something.

The wine is terrible,  it tastes like watered down grape juice and is served in small soda jug type of thing, not even a carafe, what the heck? I swear she said they only had one kind of wine which was red wine.  If I come back I am bringing a flask.  


The service was pretty bad, no one asked how we were doing, all the waiters were gruff and looked pissed off.  

I am 1/2 Italian and everything I make is better.  This food is just basic.  The pizzeria near my job is better.

The only way I would go back is if my friend invited me again, then again I may try and convince her to go elsewhere.

I had a situation recently when a delivery truck leaving a nearby Key Food dock hit my son's car and took off his rear view mirror. The Key Food manager was no help and the employees who told my son that they saw the accident..turned around and told me they didn't see anything. Unbelievable! 

Now I will talk about a restaurant on the same block where the accident had occurred..Don Peppe's. I have to make everyone aware that Mike Deluca there at Don Peppe's is a stand up man. He had witnessed the accident and confirmed this with me and my son. We have never met Mike before. The insurance company who represents the truck driver who hit my son's car called me and said how Mike Deluca was very descriptive as to what happened and this insurance company is going to mail me a check to cover the damages. They said Mike Deluca's report helped to clarify what happened that day. If an employee there at Don Peppe's acts in this honorable way..then this restaurant is worth anyone going to. I am going to bring the family to Don Peppe's soon to have dinner there and will thank Mr. Deluca personally for helping us out.

It pains me to give this place anything but 5 stars. I LOVE this place but I had an experience yesterday that turned everything sour. This is my go-to place to take people who have yet to experience the incredible food....and the no frills, family style of it all only adds to what makes it great. I've been talking Don Peppe's up to my mom for quite awhile now so we decided to go there for her birthday yesterday. As each dish hit the table, she was wowed by the quality of everything, made to perfection. Our waiter was the perfect balance of great service and slight sarcastic banter for a bit of comic relief. Everything was so wonderful, I left the waiter a generous 30% tip. We were not there very long and were just finishing up coffee and a birthday dessert when one of the bussers came over to clear some glasses. He took my mothers drink and she politely told him she was still drinking that and he refused to give it back barking at us that there were people that wanted our table and we needed to get up. Who does that? Takes someone's drink that they paid for and refuses to give it back?!? He had a strong accent and we were in disbelief that he actually said that and brushed it off as a misunderstanding. A minute later he returned with a clean table cloth and hung it over the empty chair next to my mother. (Our coffees were still full at this point.) Again, a minute or two later a second busser came over and said "come on, let's go, people want this table! You must go!" I looked around to see other tables who were there longer than we were and couldn't understand why only the bussers were angrily pushing us out the door. Even if the need was so great, perhaps the manager or even the waiter who we had just heftily tipped could have kindly explained that it was a busy time and they needed the table. Our whole dining experience totaled 1hr 20 min and imo we ate rather quickly, only waiting for each course to come out. I am truly saddened because this is a place i was proud to take others to, but my mother was left with such a bad taste after those final moments in the restaurant, and on her birthday no less. I can only hope that had the waiter or manager known about this behavior from the bussing staff they would not have approved. :-(

I love this place. Anytime i am on Long Island heading home to Westchester, I'll eat here. 
Linguine with clam sauce is my crack.
I love this place, as others already stated "best baked clams east of the mississippi".

What a day!!! We went to aqueduct to bet on the Preakness and met someone there who suggested we come here for dinner. My parents lived here over 30 years and we've never come to this place. I loved it. We had baked clams, veal, mozzarella salad and pasta with marinara. I thought everything was on point! It's a cash only place. Will definitely come back.

Baked Clams are to die for. I don't know how they do it! Billowy and balanced. Not a hint of rubberiness. Tender sweet and savory. Don Peppe Salad: THROWBACK classic simple tasty. Linguine with white clam: NOBODY DOES IT BETTER. Veal Don Peppe is a tender veal cutlet expertly pan fried in olive oil and coated with bruschetta that tastes like it just can off of a farm in Tuscany. Chicken Scarp is a winner. Wish I had 3 stomachs and I would have ordered even more dishes. Place is an homage to the good ol'days of Howard Beach and Ozone Park before each of those areas turned into a more diverse (less Italian) neighborhood. Run to the Don. Waddle home!

Not the fanciest joint. Not the friendliest. No reservations accepted and cash only. But hands down the best Italian food on the planet!

I can eat the shrimp Luciano over linguine for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

I think it's overpriced. This is a place built on   a image of those who go just to say they did. Way too much garlic, which leads some to believe it delicious, not me. Many other place have much better food for money. No atmosphere but it is well lit. Not a place I will return to.

We went there as a kid when I lived in queens in the early 70's and went back a couple of times in the early 90's. Last night we had to go to JFK and decided to take our group there. Was not disappointed. The food was the best.  Great to go with a group ( we were7) so you can shar the family style menu items. 

We had baked clams, luigini with white clam sauce, baked ziti, eggplant rollintini, veal parmigiana and chicken in lemon wine sauce and everything was super delicious. 

We asked the server for help with ordering and he was great.
The baked clams are out of this world! I heard about this place from Entourage and I have to say they did not disappoint!!!!

I was excited to try this because of the rave reviews, however I was thoroughly disappointed with the service.  I should've known with the grade pending sign on the door that the evening wouldn't end well. The food was a solid 3 stars but averages out to a 2 with the lousy service.  The baked clams were good; the linguini was too buttery for my taste, and the veal Marsala was nothing special. As for the service, waiters were anemic when asked for their recommendations. No one even bothered to take our drink orders. Instead they were playing on their cellphones while others played cards. The food took forever to arrive; each entree arrived separately with 30 minutes in between even though the restaurant was half empty. When the check finally arrived, I wanted to tip less except I was not in the mood to wait another 30 minutes for my change. Last time I will come here.

I  was taken there when I was about 15. My father and I were at Aqueduct and his exact words were " you want to have the best baked clams in the world. So we go around 4pm and sit right down, My father orders clams, spaghetti marinara, and the chicken dish. Ok now one of my fondest memories of the day, besides the great food and being with my dad. A short fellow walks in and is getting take out. My dad tells the waiter I will pay for that. Me wondering if he knows him, I say hey dad you know that guy. His reply was sort of, he was the Jockey at aqueduct that made me win the late double, and that's why you and I are here now eating. A GREAT DAY

Been coming here for years, best Italian food in Queens. Nothing fancy, rustic, family style. Yeah the waiters may be either too aggressive or too passive, but hey, you're in NY. People need to calm down, real Don Peppe clients come strictly for the food. Do yourself a favor and just order the baked clams (OMG the best in any restaurant, soooo gooood!), linguine in clam sauce, veal Don Peppe and the lemon chicken and you will leave so happy. Sure you feel like a fat, chubby kid when you leave, but again like a happy fat, chubby kid lol. Red house wine and tartufo can also be added to your meal for the ultimate satisfaction. Take the trip and just try it!

I'll be honest.  The hype of this restaurant from the show and movie "Entourage" convinced us to check this place out.  They weren't just hyping it up.  This was some of the most delicious Italian food your mouth could ever come across.  

When you walk in to this brightly (maybe overly bright) lit room, the guy in his deep accent asked "How many?" followed by telling you to "Sit wherever you like".  Across the room I see a bunch of the staff/management playing cards on one of the tables.  No shits given.  One guy, who looked like he might be the one running the joint, while playing cards, managed to keep his eye on the entire restaurant.  Without even looking away from his cards he would yell out "Antonio!  Those customers over there need you" or  "Tell that group that just walked in the door they could only order to-go now." (They stop serving after 930pm)

The menu was on the wall.   After much deliberation, we decided to go with the linguini and clams in a white wine sauce and the Veal Don Peppe.  Our server Antonio took our order and it didn't take long for our food to come.   Prior to this we were served some rolls of bread.

The linguini came out first, still piping hot and boy did it look awesome.  The amazing aroma of the pasta and sauce hits you right in the face and you know you're about to eat something really special.   I was impressed as our server took our empty plates in front of us and transferred the pasta to each of our plates, lady first.  It was so good and there was so much left over.  In fact this one dish, ordered by the Asian family next to us fed that group of five.

We ordered the Veal Don Peppe out of recommendation by much Yelpers.  A lightly breaded large piece of veal with chopped fresh tomatoes and red onions in an oil and vinegar sauce.   Again, HUGE portions.  Serves many.  I happily brought this home and continued to eat this for the next day.  Highly recommend this as well.

Great service throughout.  Great food.   Lots of leftovers. 
I already told my wife.  Every time we visit NYC, we go to Don Peppe's.

So much hype about this place from friends and yelp, yet it was so disappointing.  The decor and exterior are not welcoming at all.  The staff is quite nice and quick on their feet, so first impression was mixed for our party of 4.  Keep in mind that this is cash only and no reservations whatsoever, so be prepared and come early.

We ordered linguine with white clam, veal, and baked clams.  The clams came out first, being small and flavorful.  Then we sat and waited about 10 minutes for the linguine, which was nicely served to us by our waiter.  THEN the veal came after, so we had it by itself.  I would've preferred to have the veal along with the pasta, but that's just me.  Thought the place is packed with a high turnover rate, we weren't too overly impressed with the food.  

To be honest, we thought the portions were small and flavors weren't as hearty.  We have had many other family style Italian restaurants in Queens, Long Island, and Manhattan and we'd prefer certain ones in Manhattan over this Queens spot.
Their linguine and white clam sauce is seriously out of this world! Also their baked clams are delicious, I love the smaller clams and don pepe's never dissapoints!

After visiting here a half dozen times, this is my favorite Italian restaurant in the area.

First time I came here several years ago or perhaps more, I was very confused about family style dining. The server kindly explained how it works. 

Every time I came I start with baked clams appetizer. I ordered other appetizer before but my favorite is still the baked clams. Always enjoy this garlicky flavor. 

For pasta, I think my favorite is linguini with white clams sauce. Great flavor. My complaint is pasta texture. It's not al dente. I like my pasta with firm texture. Every time, I think of it after they bring the pasta, I should have asked when I ordered it. I forget. 

For the main dish, I had different one each time. Everything I had was good, trying to think what was my favorite... I think chicken with lemon and butter. Chicken is cooked to the perfect texture and lemon and garlic butter sauce nicely blend well with the chicken.

For desert, my ultimate favorite desert tiramisu is always good and consistent but cannoli here is very good too. 

No reservations. Just come early. 
No credit cards. Bring plenty of cash.

buon appetito!

The atmosphere is old school Italian all the way and I love that. I've been here before and had a great time but this time around was a car crash. 
Here's how it went wrong: 

Service: It took 20 minutes to take our entire order which came out wrong anyway, Our waiter didn't serve us our baked clams and Chicken Don Peppe which they always did before and they did for other tables around us, they forgot our spoons to serve ourselves the clams, they also forgot our utensils twice and we had to flag down a server to bring us new ones-At one point we just grabbed a set from the table next to us. 

Food: 
My biggest complain was about their signature dish, the baked clams. They packed too much breadcrumbs in each clam. The clam became a needle in a haystack. The linguine with white clam sauce was too oily for my liking.

Brew:
House red wine which is great with veal or any red meat. I love it with the Veal a la Don Pepe
House White. Great with seafood, which I pair with the linguini with white clam sauce and the baked clams. The alcohol was the best part of the meal. 

Giving them benefit of the doubt, I've had much better experiences here before in the past and I hope this was just an off night for them but I may be fooling my self since it was a packed restaurant and it didn't seem other tables were having the same problems as mine.

Good Luck!

The baked clams were great and so was the linguine with white clam sauce. Veal parm was typical. Would def recommend for a pasta dish but our waiter was not very helpful or nice. Go for the food, not the service.

Electric atmosphere, great service, incredible food. 
This was our first visit. On the recommendation of a friend we stopped on our way back home from the NY Aquarium.  Good to note that it is cash only and family style servings.
Bring plenty of cash and a big appetite!

Old School Italian favorites done  well. Family style portions of pasta, veal and chicken dishes that will please most anybody. This is a casual dining experience !! no fancy wine just bulk wine served in unmarked bottles...but it's really not too bad !! We always enjoy our meals and have been coming back for many years.
Great place if you're anywhere near by.  Will be back many times.
Little pricey but veal or chicken don peppe is amazing!! Waiters are welcoming wine is made in house.

The place is a joke.  Read every review.  The service sucks.  The place is rundown. People say the food is great.  Really.  How sad.  The food is like an average Italian meal at any restaurant.  Limited menu. Twice the price with oblivious waiters who snub their guest.  It's an Overprice tourist traps for wanna pretend I'm hanging with the mob.  Give me a break.  Waste of time and money. And way overpriced for average food.

definition of old school Italian restaurant. Walk in and are told to seat yourself. No menus here, you read the wall to pick your poison. It's all family style, and they recommend portion size depending on how many you have with you. We ended up getting the pasta with shrimp don Pepe chicken, veal parmigiana for entrees and calamari for appetizer. The calamari was not fried like most places make it, so it gave off a very fishy taste which we weren't big fans of. The rest of the food though was spectacular. definitely try the house special wine. For dessert we all got cappuccinos which were good, but the cannolis which they fill in house were very good. The service was decent, we had a character for a waiter very nice funny guy. I would recommend this place for sure, just make sure you wear stretchy pants.

This place was a joke. The first waiter was obnoxious. The food is mediocre at best. The portions are for big fat slobs!!!  NEVER set foot in this dump. Unless of course you enjoy getting ripped off. Very disappointed.  Awful experience.

A friend recommended this place to me, speaking very highly of it. We told the waiter upon being seated that this was our first time here (he asked). About 15 minutes later he asked what we wanted and we asked for menus. He then told us it was on the wall on the other side of the restaurant (THANKS FOR MAKING US WAIT 15 MINUTES TO TELL US THAT).

After we ordered, we were practically ignored for another half hour. Then the food came out. The food was decent, but nothing to brag about. I grew up in NYC frequenting the most talked about Italian eateries, I've had better.

We were then ignored for another 45 minutes until we approached our waiter and asked for the check. 

Overall, the food wasn't worth the customer service; or lack thereof. A meal for two people shouldn't take 2 1/2 hours; and no it wasn't because it took that long to prepare the food, we saw tables near us come and go before we could even pay. This place is al hype and not worth the trip. 

FYI this outdated dinosaur of an establishment doesn't take cash, but they do have an ATM that will include a wonderful surcharge.


If you want good food with great service try Spumoni Gardens in Brooklyn. Otherwise if you want to waste your night going blind staring at a wall menu and being ignored go here.

Good ole Don P's! Need I say more? Came here for a friends graduation party. We had a party of about 10, I recommend with bigger parties coming earlier due to their no reservation policy.
We were seated immediately and served by their whole staff constantly replacing our drinks supplying us more bread and cleaning our table. They paid attention to detail. When the food came everyone's eyes widened and a team of waiters served us. We had the baked clams, the burnt broccoli, the lemon chicken, and the chicken francaise. These were all delicious and I will be coming back soon.

Now this is Italian! Family style, unpretentious atmosphere and plain good well made fresh food. I love the salad of lettuce, tomatoes and onions with a red wine vinegar dressing, it is always  cool and fresh, I could go to Peppe's just for the salad. 
My favorite above all are their mussels marinara, to die for, absolutely the best I ever had, the mussels are plump and fresh, and the sauce is sweet with the nectar from the mussels, I could sit there with a loaf of bread and eat the mussels and sauce all day long!
I have had their linguine and shrimp, which was fantastic, chicken Parmesan, equally wonderful. Baked clams are great, as is their linguine with clam sauce. 
A little on the expensive side, but it is family style, you share everything.
Plain decor, very colorful patrons, you need reservations at night and weekends. Don't expect warm fuzzy waiters, this is old school and all about the food.
The problem is everything is so good you order too much!

Yummy Italian food, taste authentic and worth every penny! 
There are no menu's given, the only one exist on the wall. The decor is very old school NY Italian style, but the food definitely makes up for it .

I really enjoyed dinner here! The linguini with clam sauce was delicious. The eggplant and chicken dishes we had were great as well. It was my first time here and my family and I will definitely be back. I would recommend going at around 8 when the wait is not as long. If you're a bigger group, they might make the portions bigger for an extra charge, so just be prepared. The menu is on the wall--it's pretty intuitive to just look up and choose your food!
I am a big Fan - Only wish there was in NJ too! Great-freshly prepared good and hearty Italian food. Just the way it should always be!

This was a place my friend's family took me to when we were kids. Ever since I remembered it as having the best Italian food I ever had. Leaving Aqueduct and hungry we yelped and found this place and sure enough it still exists, with the same chef that was there since the 80s! The food is still spectacular! I ordered the stuffed artichoke that I've dreamed of for almost thirty years, it did not disappoint. We also had fried eggplant, cold antipasto, eggplant parm and chicken with mushroom and peppers. We even got a side of "gravy" for the fried eggplant. It was all delicious and ample portions. I can't wait to return and order more and different food...plan on taking a while and bring some friends, there is a lot of food that's meant to be enjoyed. Oh and their house wine is one of my favorite red wines ever, their own blend. It's smooth and pleasing, and that's after having tried twenty wines at the LI vineyards this week.  
We are headed back when we come to town and I highly recommend you try it too.
The food is good but pricy and the waiter is not that nice :( they need to work on their hospitality management

Went tonight with 10 of my friends ,just amazing we got the baked Clams, roasted peppers and of course stuffed artichoke, also linguine with Clams, steak,veal Don peppes,lemon chicken dessert and the homemade wine was great there's nothing bad to say everything we ordered was delicious I highly recommend this place,ignore the bad reviews on the decor it's not that bad just remember your going for the food !!!!!
Italian food family style that taste amazing.  I have been coming here for a long time and it is always a great time with great food! The baked clams have to be one of my favorite things to order!

Many people gave  it a 4 star. Funny thing it is all compliments that they write. So why did they ny give it a 5 star?

Okay.  I went to culinary school.  My x-BF is a james beard chef de cuisine and is from Italy. The food does not get better. It says 3 $$$.  OMG... U know him much quantity and quality of food you get?

I am a sommelier.  They homemade wine is wonderful. 

Service is beyond 5 star. So why do others not give it a 5 start rating?

I travel the world. I am in Italy at least 2x a month. There is not a tougher customer than people from the boroughs. Italians, Jewish,bAsian. Whatever. We complain about everything. Shut up and enjoy ur food. The food is amazing. 

If it was not good. It would not be be packed at 6:30 pm. This is the real thing. Taste, quality, and the flavor of the boroughs. 

Compliments to the Chef and the staff.

I've been coming here for years and never been disappointed. This family style Italian food. Our regular is their house wine baked clams veal al don Pepe chicken lemon butter and clams in linguine!! To die for! My favorite Italian restaurant.

I really liked this place for my Italian food craving! The clam pasta was awesome! The taste was great and on point. This place serves family portions so keep in mind that one order of pasta can satisfy the tummies of at least three big guys!

Great place.  Old school, cash NYC Italian.  Family style, most very reasonable prices in the $20s. Some of the best Veal (veal Don Peppe) ever.  Linguine clam sauce best I've had. Excellent fried eggplant and a really good son Peppe salad with excellent dressing and cheese/meat. Stuffed artichoke also great. House wine was very good too.  For 5 hungry guys with desserts, coffee and all that and more...$375 with tax and tip.  Nice waiter too. Had some conversations with neighboring tables also.  Great spot.  Wish they had one in Nassau.

I cannot give a bad or five star review since I did not end up eating there. Just too hungry and do not want to wait. The restaurant is really unique in many ways. All food are meant to share, family style; Cash only, no credit cards; No paper menu, only a menu on the wall~ The service is good once they start noticing you are there. Might come there again another time.

Food was alright. Waiter was rude. He messed up the order and then put the food in our plates. Later, when we told him that they forgot the shrimp, he told us to "Put the food back in the plate" so that he can bring it back. My mother had asked if they had chicken salads and he said yes he will bring chicken with salad. My mother's boyfriend had been here a few times and went up to the host in the front and told him about it. His response was "have you been here before, we don't serve chicken salads". If they don't serve chicken salads, then he could have simply told us they didn't serve that instead of bringing out a whole fucking plate of chicken! I personally don't like going to small family own restaurants and expected those type of attitudes anyway. When we first walked in, they told us there's no wait so the rest of us walked over. Then he gave the table away... and we waited.

Wow. Thanks to my brother for the recommendation. Italian family styled entrees, which I prefer. Got a chance to try the white clam sauce linguine and the shrimp luciano linguine.  The white clam sauce was very fresh as the only problem was the waiting time. 

They do not accept reservations nor do they accept credit cards! I would recommend this restaurant and would come back!

Expensive Italian food done very averagely with downright rude and incompetent service. 

Our waiter barely spoke to us and when he did he mumbled as if he was pissed to wait on us. The Chicken Marsala came with no pasta (chicken breasts only) and our Baked Ziti was on par with Olive Garden. Most of us did enjoy the Eggplant Parmesan.

On top of all of that we were told to leave. Yes, we got kicked out. They needed to turn the table minutes after we paid. Sorry but the "fuggedaboutit" attitude you either like us or you don't wasn't charming.

I am an Italian Restaurant nutcase. I have eaten at no less than 50 different Italian places all over CT, NJ and New York City looking for the ultimate. This is it! This place is the greatest ! Veal Parm, Veal Don Pepe, Linguine with white clam sauce,spaghetti with garlic and oil,baked clams, whatever. Its all the absolute bomb. Across the street from JFK. Fly in, have dinner and go home happy!

Finally made it out to this place that has a reputation for serving up some of the best Italian food in New York.

Reservations are not taken.  Getting a seat for a party of five for Sunday 5:30pm did not involve a wait.  Courteous service.  The portions are huge (served family style).  Everything was fabulous - without a doubt some of the best Italian food I have ever eaten:

- Baked clams: an absolute MUST here
- Cocktail shrimp: their seafood is fresh and it tastes great

- Shrimp Luciano: very flavorful and freshly baked bread comes to the table to mop up that wonderful sauce
- Broiled steak (I know...dont ask)
- Chicken Marsala: to die for

Eating at this place would be far from a mistake.  Cash only.  Definitely will return.
Family style Italian restaurant made famous by the mafia. The food is still as good as it was in the 80's. Order more than you need and take it home you won't be disappointed

I think I'm in love. 

The two best things to come out of Entourage 
Is Sloan and the discovery of Don Peppe's.

I have wanted to try this place since I first heard of baked clams. I was at JFK and decided to finally the stop for lunch. 

The baked clams are a must. I could've eaten 2-3 plates of this alone. 

The linguine with clam sauce is simple yet deliciously flavored with roasted garlic, and a balance of butter and olive oil. 

The staff are friendly and the Chef has been here since the restaurant first opened so he knows what he's doing. To be honest the portions are enough for 3-4 people so it's actually not as expensive as you'd think. (except the clams because they're all mine!)
way too pricey for the food..the pasta was mediocre.  the sauce tasted like something out of a jar. not worth the experience.

No better Italian on the planet - period. Since I was a teen, my father (a real "Brooklyn-ite" transplanted to LA) has made us stop every time we came to NY. I now do the same EVERY TIME. Even brought my kids when we came here. 

Every request for great food in NY from my friends allows me to surprise the heck out of them a with this recommendation. 

Baked clams are to die for....as is lobster fra Diavlo. Nothing bad on the menu...ever.

If I had to choose between this and Peter Lugers..... Well as long as I had cash in my pocket Don Pepe Wins!

Folks....it doesn't get better than this....

while on the road yesterday with some down time at JFK and starving, my buddy and I by chance found this GREAT  Italian restaurant in South Ozone Park. BOOM! GREAT!
We split the family potion size of the Chicken Marsala (perfectly done) and the cappellini and marina. can say enough and we're going back soon

This is my favorite spot in town the owner is very friendly and I've eaten here about a dozen times the good is absolutely phenomenal you have to order the shrimp Luciano over pasta and chicken don peppe only orders these 2 dishes and you'll be amazed mmmmm hands down best Italian joint in town close to Bklyn

Been going to Don Peppe's for years.  I love everything about it! Never do I regret the 45 minute or so commute to the restaurant from my house. Highly recommend the baked clams and the veal don peppe. The food is really on another level. Also enjoy the house red and white wines. 

On the weekends it can get busy, so make sure to arrive early. Everything is reasonably priced but remember that it is cash only. Great for a date or a large party.
Place is excellent. The pasta quality is of a high grade. The sauce is exceedingly fresh. Waiters could be rude but who cares - I'm eating.

This place is family style large dish entrees. We ordered baked clams, calamari, stuffed mushrooms, broccoli, sausage with ziti, linguine with clams in white sauce, eggplant parm and the chicken de peppe. Enough for 10 adults and 2 kids. The service was great  table side when serving the main dishes but our waiter seemed a bit overwhelmed since the restaurant was so busy. Overall an enjoyable meal and the staff is friendly.

5 STARS! 

My friends were raving about this place, claiming it was, "the best italian food ever." I had my doubts, but Don Peppe completely exceeded my expectations. This place gives off an old school italian vibe. The food here is amazing. Everything is served family style, which I love because I can eat a little bit (or a lot) of everything. 

The baked clams are the best! You must get them! They are cooked perfectly. The clams are tender and the bread crumbs are toasty. I usually get two orders for the table when I visit. After you devour the clams be sure to dip your bread in the sauce. The mussels are really good as well! They give a pretty big portion for one order. 

As for the pasta, the linguine in white clam sauce is delicious! It's exactly how it should taste. The pasta is cooked perfectly al dente. There are nice chunks of big chunks of clam and lots of garlic. The sauce is buttery a buttery bliss.

My favorite pasta dish here is the Shrimp Luciano. I can't rave enough about this dish. The sauce consists of onions simmered in a buttery sauce cooked to perfection and then topped with tender shrimp! 

The Veal/Chicken Parm, Veal Don Peppe, and Chicken Marsala were all good as well. You basically can't go wrong with anything you order here. However, if you're currently in love with other Italian restaurants be prepared to fall out of love because Don Peppe will cast a shadow on them. After eating here, I compare everything to this place and nothing else has won me over. There's nothing wrong with high standards though. Enjoy :)
Was only in town for the night and wanted Italian, and could not have made a better choice.  Everything was absolutely fantastic.

Been here a few times with my parents and we are the only asians in the restaurant every time, which there is no problem with. But, personally i felt like some of the waiters were racist towards us. Keep in mind my mom speaks english well and so does my dad. Every time they came to take our order it was as if they were rushing us and couldn't wait to leave our table. My mom was saying something and the waiter said "i don't understand what you're saying hahaha" and he started laughing. My parents didn't hear him well because he mumbled it as he was picking up our dishes, so they laughed along. I am 17 I was born in NYC and have lived in Queens all my life, so yes I understood him clearly. The food is great, but I don't know why they treated us like that because we are able to pay the same amount as everyone else. My parents gave a big tip, which I was not happy about, because they enjoyed the food. Every time they ask me if I want to go now, I say no.

I am really shocked with my experience last Saturday night at Don Peppe's. I first walked in and the gentlemen greeting us at the door, he pointed to were we would be sitting which I understand because it was pretty packed. However, the utensils were visibly dirty and my date did not have a napkin when we sat and had to flag down a waiter twice. The waiter was very rude in the beginning and impatient with us because we didn't know that there were no menus... you have to walk to the other side of the restaurant and its printed on a wall in which even that didn't bother me.  We order the food in this family style restaurant right??? The baked clams came in sets of twelve which were absolutely wonderful btw!! The baked shells which are served at a family style restaurant came with  whopping three baked shells. We also ordered chicken parmigiana which I am pissed about because it was far from amazing and my mom makes it sooo much better. To top it off the bill comes including my 12 clams, 3 baked shells and less than mediocre chicken parm was $76. To top it off we were till hungry and FYI there is nothing spectacular about there bread.  I gave two starts for your baked clams because they were delicious but definitely not worth $20.  Truthfully I have been dying to try this restaurant for years and I am really displeased with the service and food.  I find that other Italian restaurants in Howard beach are better than this place. I will not be returning.

Anyone who complains about this place is a real whiner. The food is so good. Don't complain about the sometimes brusque service or the décor. It is part of the charm. If the food takes a long time to come, it is well worth the wait. I rarely if ever have service problems. Even if I do, the place is fun to hang out in and watch the other diners. If you want white glove service, go elsewhere. The quality of the food can vary - from extremely good to utterly fantastic. You will notice how excited people are once they are seated and about to order. Ive been eating at Don Peppe for over 50 years. Now living in Florida. When I land at La Guardia or Kennedy it is usually my first stop before going into the city. No matter where I eat in Manhattan, Don Peppe is always the most enjoyable meal. Oh, and if you want to drink wine, they only have two kinds - red or white. No label, no cork. Both served cold and both delicious. Enjoy!!

The reviews on the linguine in clam sauce are so on point because this dish is a MUST when you go here! The clams are fresh with the white sauce lacing all over the pasta, which is bombarded with whole garlic cloves...which is never a bad thing. The attentive waiter made my first experience more pleasing and cannot wait to come back to satisfy my linguine in clam sauce craving!

Their menu is a bit slim and the restaurant slightly resembles a nursing home cafeteria, but their linguine and clams are so good that nothing else matters!!!

Born and raised in NYC, I've eaten my fair share of Italian cuisine and Don Peppe's linguine and clams is the best the city's got to offer. The clam sauce is so flavorful and every bite of the linguine is bursting with the right amount of garlic, herbs, and all sorts of goodness. 

The restaurant gets soo busy, but the waiters so super attentive. 

Their red table wine is really good also. We(4 people) went through a bottle each.

The problem with most people is they are so accustomed to eating Italian food with a ton of spices. I am Italian and this is the purest Italian food there is. Basic recipes, which is exactly how great old time Italian food is made. 

A world traveler I dined with there recently told me at age 70 he has virtually been to every place on the planet, and said "this is the best Italian food in the world".

I agree.

Authentic, delicious Italian food in a relaxed environment and a server (Ditri) who knows his recipes and makes the evening fun.

Out of the way for some (near jfk) but well worth the trip. Waited for the jammy amarone to fade before writing this. We will go back with a posse of friends

SHB

Love it here! Good quality italian food. Theres always a little downfall to family-style dining, and things get a little harder with there only being one menu for the whole restaurant, but everything here is so worth it. Will be returning.

AMAZING food! Have been going here for years, and I always leave very happy! This is like your Nona's cooking - no fancy Italian food, just really great, well made Italian simple classics done right. Have never had anything I didn't love. Highly reccommend.
Nice restaurant. Very popular amongst the people I associate with. Friendly staff very family oriented. Makes a nice plate of pasta. Definitely would never mind coming here for a nice meal

the owner is super cool and friendly, i come here with my famiy all the time, this place has the best clams in the world.  I would highly order the below dishes when coming to Don Peppe's for lunch or dinner  

-Baked Clams  (Out of this world) 
-Chicken Don Peppe  (Chicken cutlet w tomatoes ) 
-Chicken Scaripirello   Amazing takes 30 minutes but worth it.   

This place puts all the local eateries to shame.  Save your money and come to Don Peppe for the best dinner in queens close to Bklyn :)

my wife and i loved this place. truly authentic Italian cuisine. if you love italian food, Don Peppes is the place.for you. cash only. linguini white clam sauce is amazing. baked clams fantastic. the wine was not so great. in house. not very good. overall great time.
This is one of the best old world Italian restaurants.  The linguini and clam sauce is amazing. It is family style and only took cash when I went.
Great food, cash only, family style serving, generous portions, be prepared to wait for seating.  I love the seafood salad.  If you are flying to or from JFK, leave some time to check it out.

Based on the reviews we just had to give this a try. The ordering process was kind of unique. They don't give you menus. The menu is on the wall and you have to order from there. Luckily, I had yelp's menu pulled up and we just passed my phone around to order lol. It's family style portions. We ordered linguini with clam sauce, veal Marsala, spaghetti with meat sauce for the kids, and baked ziti. The linguini was the best! Good place to go if you with your fam or that special someone. The cappuccino at the end was one of the best I ever had!!

A must if you've never been, absolutely no doubt the best Italian food in NYC!! And it's on Lefferts Blvd in Queens just a stones throw from JFK long term parking!! Start with Baked clams and the fried peppers! Then the shrimp Luciano over linguini (my going to the electric chair last meal) is a must!! The Chicken parm is awesome as is the T-bone with mushrooms and onions OMG, OMG!!!!!

Awesome spot for family or friends dinner, portions are massive so don't go alone lol....classic home style Italian delicious dishes with a great homey vibe and great service....definitely will be coming here a lot!!
This is the best place in NY for Italian food. The baked clams is to die for and the home made wine is super delicious.
Don Peppe... still going strong (and with good reason),  after 40 years.  Put it on your list.

As far as Queens Italian eateries go, Don Peppe's (aka Don Peps) is as good as it gets. 

The first time I went to Don Peppe was on my 16th birthday. My best friend was dating one of the waiters and he comped us the meal. After that first meal, I was sold!

Many moons later, my family and I still come to this Queens Italian staple when we want a taste of the (Americanized) old country! Some of our favorites:

- Stuffed Artichoke - terrific

- Special Salad - with cheese and salami - tasty

- Baked clams - good if a bit overcooked

- Spaghetti with garlic and oil - top notch

- Filet de Pomodoro - tomato sauce with prosciutto and tomatoes over rigatoni - delicious 

- Filet of Sole - with lemon and breadcrumbs - delish

- Veal Parmigiana - I don't eat veal but the family enjoys

- Broccoli with garlic and oil - delicious and black around the edges

- Cannoli - delicious with chocolate chips

- Red Wine - very good and homemade

- Cappuccino  - very good

The service is very good but relaxed. Don't come here and except to be in and out in 90 minutes. The courses are spaced fairly far apart.  The wait staff treats you like family - especially Benny. He is a joy!

We will always come back to Don Peps.
My favorite place the fried peppers are awesome just like everything else on the menu 6* i give this place.

The best clams in the world. 
We tried the stuffed peppers and chicken scarpirelello it was absolutely worth every dollar.  We also ordered the Don Peppe Salad best salad I've ever had.  Is iukd highly recommend this joint for someone who likes good Italian cooking. 


Pros:   Xmas eve to go orders are great . Easy access near Belt Pkwy


Cons:  closed Monday's and on vacation

The hype is true, the food is outstanding.. The decor is less than desirable, but it's not terrible.. The waiters were all very friends and attentive, surprised to see any reviews saying they aren't.. I went with my friend on a Saturday who had been there many times prior, and surprisingly we were sat right away at 7:30.. By 8 the place filled up though.. To start we had baked clams, as other reviewers have written, they are a must-get item.. We also had the fresh mozzarella which was good but nothing extraordinary, it wasn't burrata which is the only mozz I feel anyone should write home about... We shared the shrimp Luciano over pasta, it was phenomenal to say the least... Between the two of us we didn't have that much to take home, and I don't eat THAT much, so this was a preferable amount of food for two hungry people.. We finished up with the peach and coconut sorbets, good, but I have had similar.. The baked clams and shrimp were the best part and I would definitely go back for that alone

Go to order: peppers and onions, baked clams, veal don peppe, linguini in white clam sauce, chicken scarpiello and cannolis for dessert. Trust me, you will not be disappointed.
There's so much hype about the clam sauce, veal, and baked clams but it really is true. It's unreal. The linguini is super oily, but it's worth it. And there is SO Much garlic. And the veal is so crispy and the actual meat is so tender. The chicken is also very good, along with the potatoes and peppers it comes with. It's very moist, which is what you're always worried about with roasted chicken. 
This place is a must try and great for big parties because it's family style. 
I can't give this place 5 stars because of the service, which was decent. After about an hour and 15 minutes, they actually asked us to leave because they needed the table. This place is never not packed, it's like a factory the way they flip the tables. But the food is superb!
The food was delicious and I had my very first experience with seafood here. Their baked clams are SO delicious and I can't wait to be back!

Went there for my sons birthday dinner and left hungry after paying two hundred and forty bucks with the tip. Have heard about this place for years and decided to give it a try. The food was delicious but very small portions for so called family style. Thank god the waiter recomended one and half orders only giving four people a small dish. Having eaten at many family style Italian restaurants I know what it should be. A single order at la Parma in Oceanside was bigger than the one we got here. We also got the shrimp Luciano which was a dozen shrimp floating in the sauce . Our waiter was boggled after taking a table of five behind us or maybe he would of suggested having the shrimp over linguine which would of helped fill us up.dont get me wrong the food was delicious but the portions were fit for a person with bulemia.

Heard all about the famous Don Pepe restaurant to finally go and experience it was an OK experience .I will not be able to brag about it to people or tell people to go because I was not fully satisfied up all the commotion about this place .for a family-style restaurant the portions were way too small and was not what I expected. Another disappointment was the waiter who was not being attentive to my family .he was unable to wait more than three tables at one time. I tried to get a drink mid -dinner and I could not find him for at least 25 minutes. Plus it was scorching hot inside the restaurant I was sweating the whole time.

My husband and I love to eat here. 
Pasta is perfect. I like the atomospher, too. It's a kid's friendly restaurant. You can go with kids, and thay have a changing table in the bath room.

The food are just ok. The dish portion is kind of small for family style. The internet prices is different than the store price
Shrimp Luciano over lingerie is 40.00. I didn't know lingerie would cost extra. The place look like a dump! You are paying Manhattan price in queens. I had better Italian food and half of it cost in a better atmosphere!! They should give $$$$ for this place not 3. NOT going back this over price dump..

Don't come for the decor, come for the family style old school Italian dishes.
Want a menu? Look on the wall, that's the only place where you'll  find it.
Came alone on a busy Saturday night around 8ish, got seated relatively fast, 10 mins or so.
Started my meal with Stuffed mushroom, and Galamah with marinara sauce.
The mushroom cooked perfectly, still holding it's shape with a good bite. Stuffed high and swimming in the delicious mushroom sauce. Galamah or calamari was cooked perfectly, no hint of rubber texture, each bite was a perfect morsel of squid.
For the entree, I went the classic route by ordering Linguine with white clam sauce.
Cooked  al dente, with lots of plump clam pieces, whole garlic and sauce. This dish is as delicious as it gets, perfectly cooked and assembled, the flavors meld in a perfect symphony. This might be by far the best Linguine with white clam sauce I have ever had.
Ended my meal with a single cannoli, creamy but not too sweet, a good ending to my meal. I will definitely be back, there are other menu items I need to try. Be forewarned though, it's cash only.

BTW, from the poster below, I tried to look for the $40 lingerie, but did not find any. Why the hell are you eating lingerie when you can have some linguine in white clams sauce is beyond me. Keep the kinky stuff behind closed doors.

Ever been to an Italian that won't serve olive oil at the table with the bread? Well I've found one for you. This place SUCKS. The only thing worse than the food is the service. Do yourself a favor stay away.
$$$ Though worth it. Know the Menu before you go  Preview the photos of the food on YelpCash only  Bona Fortuna
The food is great, the history and experience of eating in this old school restaurant is even better. Shrimp Luciano served over linguine and veal Don Peppe are must haves.

Walked in Saturday night 715 with a 10 minute wait for a party of 4 plus high hair. 

Host was friendly and accommodating. Waiter was professional and patient (we had a two year old)

Scungilli marinara , braciole, and linguine clams were stellar. They will all make you a better person 

Chicken scarpiello was good but minus one star for mostly overlooked / dried meat. The accompanying sausage/potato/pepper were all perfectly cooked 

Side of broccoli / string beans (one plate) extremely overpriced at $35. 

Overall very good experience .

Baked clams were awesome. The kiddos liked the chicken parm (it was enough to share between them, even without pasta) and the shrimp luciano with angel hair was amazing. House red was good, on the dry side, and they make it in house. It's family style dining AND it's a large dining room. Be ready to feel like you're sitting at a huge Italian family dinner. It's great!

We went there the other evening, four ladies.  We had been there before.  We ordered the cold antipasto.  It consisted of four slices of salami, four slices of cheese, some red peppers and olives and a couple of anchovies.  The rest was ALL LETTUCE and onions.    Not a cold antipasto at all.  The pasta was good, but the veal, although tender was just covered with tomatoes and again, onions.  Not the best meal for the price which with the tip cost us $55.00 each.  The wine was pretty bad.  Don't think we will be going there anytime soon.
Rude waiter, subpar seasoning. Seems like they became complacent with their food. Again the waiter was very rude and the food was not seasoned well.

There is no better family-style Italian restaurant in NYC. There is no such thing as a bad meal here. The food is super fresh and consistent. The service is efficient and friendly. This was the only restaurant that my "off the boat" Italian parents ever looked forward to going to when I was a kid and I'm definitely addicted. Its a special place for me.
Amazing Italian food...A must try! The waiter was on point. He took care of us and the order arrived in time.

There is nothing bad that can be said about Don Pepes! I live around the corner and the lines for this place are real for a reason! I recommend- linguine with clam sauce because obvi! Lemon butter chicken or chicken don Pepe is AMAZING!!!! Their homemade wine is superb! The garlic bread, veal Marsala, I can go on because I've tasted the ENTIRE menu just go now, stop reading and go!

Good place to eat! Servers are super nice. Its bit crowded and don't really have private space between the tables. Its fresh, and their clam linguini pasta was really good. Shrimp is fat and yummy. Portions are really big so make sure to order less then other regular restaurant. One pasta can serve three people easily. And they do not accept card, only cash.

Just great and always great as a standard. 7 of us agree on the zuppa de mussels,seafood marinara,DON PEPE Salad,mozzarella and tomato,linguini with garlic and oil,spaghetti with meat sauce,veal parmagiana with eggplant parmagiana. Simply heaven Discussing coffee and dessert now.
Hidden gem, my all time favorite Italian restaurant. Must try baked clams and white clam pasta. Family style restaurant with great service!

We were staying at the nearby JFK Marriot Courtyard and craving Italian. Using our handy dandy Yelp guide, we spied this place a few miles away. 

Upon entering, at an early 5pm, and the place is mostly empty - but I must admit it was not what we expected. No red and white checked table cloths. No ornate old world paintings hanging on the wall. No chandeliers or sconce lighting. 

Drop ceiling. One big room. Black and white. Nothing but photos of horses and jockeys on the walls. A group of six men sitting at a table playing cards. A waiter is watching the races at Belmont on a small TV in the entrance. We suspect this is a scene from Good Fellas.

One of the men at the card table looks up (turns out this is the owners son and current man in charge) and calls out "sit anywhere!"

There are only two other men sitting at a table along the side wall. One is large and white, the other short and dark skinned. Turns out the shorter gentleman is the famous Edgar Prado (won more than 500 races in 1997). Apparently this is a real horse loving group. 

There is one menu - on a chalkboard at the rear of the room. It offers a handful of appetizers, pasta, shrimp, chicken or veal in one of a variety of sauces, or steak. Short and Simple. Prices are high-ish per dish but we guess this is a family style big portion deal (we are correct). 

Our waiter, terrific all the way, offers to snap a photo and bring it back. We think our best strategy is to ask his opinion - "what should we have?" This turns out to be a good strategy.

We ask for the wine list. He comes back with four bottles. We can also do carafes of house wine or an Amarone in the back for $100. We go with a Nero D'Avola from Sicily. 

Back to our tour guide/waiter - He suggests the zuppa di clams as a starter, and veal in pizzaiolo Sauce (not on menu). We go with it...

The clams were absofreakinlutkey outstanding. We dunked away every last drop. A nice bottle of red paired perfectly. 

Then came the tenderest of veal lovingly covered in deliciousness. We hit food heaven somewhere in the middle of this dish. 

The service was excellent, the food outstanding, the experience priceless. Don't miss this if you are nearby.
Don't go. It's closed. We went just last week hoping for a nice NYC Italian meal and the place was closed
Shit is legit. Nothing else to say. But it is on the pricey side. But one of my favorite places to eat.

Tasty, old school Italian fare, down to the basket of warm homemade bread.  Think the real version of what Olive Garden tries to be.  Do mot look for fanciness, it is very basic.  Black and white, clean decor.  The house wines are MUCH better that what most folks pay a pretty penny for in a chain restaurant. We tried the linguini in clam sauce (white) and I will say it was ridiculously good.  Everything is served family style, and one player was enough for two of us had some to take home.  One thing that was a no go was the house salad made with iceberg lettuce (a little overpriced for a salad, about $20).  Will definitely go back.

Best Linguine w/ white clam sauce hands down! Nice no nonsense old school Italian restaurant. 

Start off with nice Scungilli Salad Or Baked clams, both were delicious. The linguine w/ white clam sauce is a must, for those on a low carb diet, try the Veal Don Peppe with salad on top. Be sure to try the homemade Vino, served cold.

If you still have room, try the Pistachio Tartufo or Tiramisu.  Bring cash, No credit cards.

Always on point.
I have to say that this is one of the very few places that I have eaten at that have always delivered.  
The food is always amazing, the service is always great.
Baked Clams are always a MUST!!!

We only make it here about 3-4 times a year but I would go everyday if I could.

Can't wait for my next visit!!!
I been around the world, this includes Italy this place defiantly is the best.

I Was Able To Find This Place On Someone Instgram Post! && Me Being A Major Italian Fan AUTHENTIC ITALIAN FAN! Ran Too Yelp Read The Reviews, Bookmarked It Then Know I Had To Try It!

So I Was Out Of Church Alil Before 7, && Myself && My Sister Were Very Hungry! So I Said Let's Try This Place I Just Read About...Call The Place They Said Come In Before 8:30. Made It Alil Past Had My Sis Run In Too Make Sure We Can Still Come In! I Was Anxiously Waiting In The Car. Called Me && Said We Has Fun 5 Minutes Too Park && Come In Because They Were Closing. Lucky Me I Found A Spot Right In Front! Came In Said My Thank You's && My Experience Began!

We Came In Was Sat Right Down && We Met Marco! Who Was A Great Waiter! Allowed Myself && Sister Too Enjoy The Atmosphere! Good Environment ,  Even The Food && The House Made Wine Was Also Good. Family Style Dining, Not Too Pricey && One Menu Too Choose From. It's Authentic! We Enjoyed Can't Wait Too Go Back! Thanks Again Marco NO Polo

Well I finally figured out how Turtle from Entourage lost all his weight, he attempts to eat all his meals at Don Peppes. He realizes how bad the food is and vomits up all he has eaten! The originator of old school, Neopolitan family style has gone down the drain. Maybe I'm just spoiled by Peppe's successors on Long Island but a rececnt visit with my son after deplaning at Kennedy was horrible. It was downhill after the excellent salad. Cappelini with meat sauce arrived as spaghetti with ketchup sauce. Chicken Scarp with all the trimmings had inedible sausage (raw inside) and fatty chicken. Save yourself approx. $75. Per person (no alcohol)  and dine elsewhere.

Went here as a large group and it took some time to get a table since they don't take reservations. 
I am a frequent patron of Carmines over the years bc they are always consistent as well as very good value. I am a lover of spaghetti clam sauce and this place really hit the spot. Their portions are by no means as large as Carmines. In fact they are considerably smaller to the point where I may not consider this as much of a family style. I could finish an order of pasta here whereas at Carmines, one order can feed 3. Bringing the price to double. 
Their veal entree can easily feed 2-3 (6 pcs per order). We had the chicken scarpiello, pretty good, it was chicken with bone roasted with sausages peppers , onion, potatoes. It may have been sautéed first to get all the Flavors to seep and then roasted so it tasted a bit dry even though it was flavorful. The roasted potatoes in it was the highlight of the dish since it absorbed all the delicious Flavors while roasting in the oven. The highlights: baked clams. Very delicious, breadcrumbs were full of brine , garlic and oily deliciousness. Veal Marsala was good. They didn't pound it super thin so each mouthful was substantial. Their calamari wasn't fried and would highly recommend. This dish was very generously sized. the red sauce was full of chunky garlic and tomato. The squid was extremely tender (must try). The veal lemon wasn't anything special. Overall yummy but not that cheap. However I'll definitely return just for the clam sauce, baked clams, calamari and try some of the other dishes next time. This is a true old school Italian American joint.

This place is definitely worth the wait. I would recommend this place to anyone who loves real authentic Italian taste and flavor. The house red is exceptional and has such a great aroma to it. Their family style serving is great portion size is great but their in house clams are delicious. Their in house sausages are delicious as well, their sauces and dressings are to die for. Very unique look and a great staff.

The best....hands down. 

Anything on the menu. 

Personal faves are baked clams, linguini w/white clam sauce, veal don peppe

Bring your appetite and don't you dare try and eat "just a little"
Excelnt food, service a nice family style service.   But be aware, cash only.   Street parking.   Not quiet place, it's family style

I don't often praise restaurants I frequent or write reviews but this was delicious! Fried peppers were fantastic, the stuffed mushrooms were to die for and I had the chicken breast and pepper platter which melted in my mouth. This is a great Italian restaurant in Queens. I can't stop thinking about the food and I definitely want to go back soon! I will say the scenery could use an upgrade. I did feel like i was eating at A race track but the food is so good I didn't care. Don Pepe's is fantastic!
Oh my God the very best in authentic Italian food take it from a sicilian. Family style dishes that you will enjoy and please try the baked clams you will never taste anything like this anywhere.

My First night there and I fell in love with the food it was so amazing. Especially the baked clams and the stuffed mushrooms. They were so delicious, I will come back again. Great food and great service.
EXCELLENT!! Shrimp Luciano (not on board), but Oh So Good! Baked clams, veal don peppe.....ANYTHING here is most likely delectable!!!

If you go here and do not get the Linguine with White Clam sauce you're doing it wrong. PHENOMENAL!!!!! Perfect al dente pasta. This is real authentic Italian food. I can taste the tradition in each dish. The baked clams are also fantastic. Everything that I have tried on my couple of trips to Don Peppe's has been a hit.

As a heads up it is CASH ONLY. I would say it is on the pricey side but its all family style food, so you're getting big quantities. Service is outstanding, very professional. I will be back, no doubts about that.
Outstanding food and service. Family style meals with generous portions. Absolutely delicious!
the best ever nothing beats it.. Stop complaining about prices you are paying for quality not quantity

This is not a restaurant. It is an institution. What makes this place as great as it is goes far beyond just he taste of the food. I don't know why I waited so long to write the review but you're gonna thank me!
It offers a meal that is always prepared with the best of ingredients by people that understand what make food great. You can have a dish here and live it and if you come back next month and have it again it's the same. The consistency here is one that is rarely equaled. The food is always the same. Unbeatable. The staff knows how to take care of its customers both the loyal and new. 
Don Peppe puts every restaurant around little Italy look like they are practicing. 
Seriously you should go here and keep going back until you've tried the menu.  But if you're looking for suggestions the stuffed artichoke, chicken scarprielo, linguine with  clam sauce and shrimp Luciano are the best you will ever eat. 
If Thats not the absolute truth find me at my own restaurant Nana's Breakfast Nook, in Howard Beach, and I'll pay your bill. 
Buon Appetito!

Some of their dishes are not family style portions. I do not know where people get this idea how don peps is the best Italian place in New York because it is not. They are ok nothing everyone makes it out to be. I have had better else where for a lot cheaper if you want family style then carmines is the place to be their portions are huge the same goes for Caio baby not family style but their portions are huge for only one person. Some dishes at don peps like linguine and clam sauce is 25.00 and I could not believe how small the portion was also the waiters like serving the food here I'm not use to that so my reaction every time the waiter placed the food down was to help my self and the waiter got mad lol sorry I am paying to eat. I am not paying to be served like a 4 year old child.

What a great italain gem. The real deal! Had chicken parmigiana. Excellent! Chicken Marsala. Excellent!  Broccoli rabe. Excellent!  They make you feel like part of the family. A must if  your in New York!

I came here on a Sunday afternoon with 2 great friends, one of which is Italian like myself so we grew up with and know good Italian food.  We sat down or tried to and noticed the chairs were greasy and filthy so one of our friends gave us wipes to clean our chairs.  I'm already turned off.  But I said let's give it a chance.  The waiter came over, didn't introduce himself, didn't smile etc.  I wasn't getting that warm and fuzzy feeling.  The bread was brought over and when we asked for olive oil they said "we don't do that".  Seriously, what kind of an Italian restaurant is this?  So I overlooked that.  We ordered red wine in a carafe which came out cold.  Everybody knows that red wine should be served room temperature. They gave us plates for our entrees and all 3 of them were filthy.  We asked the waiter for new plates!   We shared the Don Peppe salad special which had olives, peppers and salami.  It was good, but nothing spectacular.   We shared the linguini pomodoro which again was good but nothing to write home about.  Then we shared a chicken francese dish which came out with an orange tint to the sauce which I've never seen before.  It was bland and hard to cut even with a knife.  When I make it, I can cut it with a fork.  We decided we've seen and ate enough and wanted to leave asap only to be told they don't take credit cards so beware to bring cash with you.  In closing, I was extremely disappointed.  I've heard about this place for years and read the good reviews so I'm asking myself what kind of people are leaving these reviews.  Certainly not Italian people who know good food and I've eaten in some of the best Italian restaurants in Queens (L' Incontro, Tazzina, Park Side) so I know good food....unfortunately this is not one of them.  Oh and they have no Wifi either or at least when I was there.  People have said to me, maybe you didn't order the right dish.  It shouldn't matter - with a good restaurant, everything should be good.  I won't be returning.

The food was pretty good. We started with the linguine with clams. A garlic and oil base with clams. It was tasty. Wasnt "the best in the city" but real good. 

Then 3 of us shared the veal with peppers and onions,  and the chicken with butter and lemon. Both dishes were delicious. 

Here's the thing. Considering the dishes are pushed as "family style", we were all craving more. For 25 to 30 a pop for a dish, they weren't "Carmines Size". The pasta dish could have been more. One person could easily finish it.  The chicken and veal each had 3 average size pieces in each. We wished it was larger. 

25 for apps,  25 to 40 for entrees, you can easily spend 225 for 4 people here. 

Its expensive but good. And cash only.
If you love pasta this is the place to visit and my drink was delicious lol  very nice place and they have a happy hour

I've been hearing about Don Pepps for 13 years. my husband and I finally went there for dinner.
 it's family-style so we didn't order a lot because I'm a vegetarian and there's really not much we could share.
We got a delicious salad of Caprese and a bowl of spaghetti and my husband had some calamari.
I Loved Loved Loved the ambience!
a lot of Italian people there from the neighborhood in Howard beach.
 it was great I felt like I was at a party because we all seem to recognize each other or know each other.
 we sat next to two fellows and they were regulars so they told us about the menu.
 the food was pretty good and the decor was old-school its what you don't see anymore.
I miss the old days so it was refreshing to see here.
 We will definitely be back.

Been coming here for years.  The food is absolutely the best. Sometimes the service is questionable? But it depends. The food is always delicious and on point. The wine is delicious. Highly recommend this place if your looking for real Italian food. Love this place.

I don't care what anyone says...this place is Amazing!!!!! this linguine with clams to die for the Veal scallopini was soooo buttery and lemony is the most amazing way. The decor is plain nothing out of this world but its so you can focus on the food!!! it steals the show anyway. Priced just right - family style - you need a seat get there early no reservations CASH ONLY. But me and my Boyfriend enjoyed it so much (he's a Marine and loved the fact that as soon you walk in there are photos of marines on the wall - made him feel right at home) Owner/Manager was so welcoming -- so old school went around to all table talk to everyone like he knew them like you were at his house. My and my BF we're like we should come back every month forever- it could be our place- and when we're old we can talk about how we had been coming there since we first started dating,.. lol. It's that kind of place. A gem in Queens...but then again are you really surprised???  
Honestly I can't say enough good things...my only concern is when am I going back???

My friends have been telling me about how good this place was for a while now. I haven't gotten a chance to go but I am happy I finally did. The food and wine is AMAZING. If I could give this place six stars.....I absolutely would. The food was the best Italian food I have ever had. You HAVE to get the linguini white clam sauce. It was beyond delicious. I would recommend going with a bigger group of people because everything is served family style. I went with three of my friends, we ordered the baked clams, stuffed artichoke, linguini white clam sauce, veal don Pepe, and the chicken in lemon butter sauce. The baked clams were perfect, so delicious. Make sure you dip the bread in the clam sauce. You'll thank me later. Then the stuffed artichoke was huge and also really really good! The linguini white clam sauce as I said before was incredible. The pasta was cooked perfectly and there were a ton of clams on the plate. I am not a fan of veal but was told to try the veal don Pepe. I am SO happy I did! It was amazing. You HAVE to try it! I could've eaten probably 5 pieces by myself. The chicken in lemon butter sauce was also very good. The chicken was cooked perfectly and very tender. We also got three bottles of the white wine which was one of the best Italians wines I've ever had. It was more on the sweeter side. Overall I had a great experience here. I can't wait to go back and try more things on the menu!

Mybe we ordered the wrong items of the menu, but we felt that the food was 
We had great expectation when we sought out Don Pepe because of his histor of being a great family style Italian cusine, but it was horrible. The pasta with meat sauce was a convination of undercooked meat and sauce over what appeared to be an attempt at Al dente spaghetti.
