I can only imagine that the chef is taken his cue from other famous pasta chef- Mr. Chef Boyardee

Too Far from manhattan. But the pasta dishes are second to none. Perhaps the best in New York. What is exhilarating are the wide choices. You can order most Italian meats, cooked in any variation to go. Pasta dishes are also diverse, as the Vongole contains come of the best garlic flavors in NYC. I wish it was nearer to manhattan so it won't be such a drive.

Didn't realize it was a family style restaurant until my friends told me. The serving portions are pretty big for their pastas but when we ordered appetizers, they gave us so little. Our waiter was kinda rude and acted as if he didn't really want to serve us. Maybe because we were there late up until they closed... the baked ziti was okay, the most popular linguine in white clam sauce was hyped up too much. From my understanding Italian food has many amounts of olive oil but some of them were so oily the sauce didn't even really stand out. 
The bread was kind of stale, not that great of a quality. 
Food was filling though. For a party of 13 we ordered 5 pasta dishes and 3 appetizers

The waiter was rude and unhelpful. You have to order everything you want at once. He could've said this more nicely instead he said that we can't order again and mumbled that he is going home and won't put in another order, especially since it was 5pm. Very crowded seating. Portions are supposed to be big but not for 30-40 bucks. Food was not horrible. We did go there with a big group but did not hassle him. Also the bill was very unclear as only numbers were written out. Very unprofessional place but decent food.
Best family style Italian food around.  Baked clams, shrimp marinara, linguine white clam, the veal don Peppe and chicken and eggplant are amazing.  Been coming here for 20 years and has not changed.

On the basis that this is for many a destination Italian family style restaurant the meal did not disappoint.  Possibly giving the visit second thought because of Turtle's endorsement and the "hype" discount - I don't regret getting a friend to convince me to go.

Homemade wine like from my father-in-law's garage, killer OG style Italian salad, stuffed mushrooms that were the perfect appetizer, rock-solid-butter-oil-garlic pasta and a killer breaded veal we all great start to finish in a spot that is all about food and no pretension.  Baked clams were also solid, I don't have the clam-expertise so I cannot comment but my companions gave it a big thumbs up.

Don't believe the hype but do believe your tastebuds, buds!

I'll see you soon again Don Peppe!
Absolutely love their food! But, always double check your receipt as they tend to make mistakes...

Tip #1: Since your wait may be long and there is no bar to order a libation while you wait, take a bottle of wine or a couple beers to enjoy on the porch! Several regulars had this figured out and I'll know better next time.
Tip #2: Bring lots of cash. Don Peppe's does not take plastic and I'd hate to end up unable to pay!

We had the baked clams - OMG they were so good! The Shrimp Luciano - delicious! And the Veal Don Peppe is breaded/fried veal topped with a fresh tomato and onion bruschetta-type sauce - an excellent combination of heavy and light. 

Some reviewers have not appreciated the quality of the food at Don Peppe's. I am not sure what planet they are from but this is the real deal! And remember - No Reservations, No Plastic, No Frills. Just garlicky, buttery goodness dripping down your chin.

My favorite place for great Italian food with a big group.
It's family style with big portions so I advise a big group where you can order more items and have a little bit of everything.
It's an old school place which I love.
Never can wait to go back.

This is as good as it gets! Being southern Italian we know good fresh food-and Don Pepe is the place for it!Some reviewers dont understand that southern italian cuisine uses a LOT of extra virgin olive oil-non-italians may say the food is greasy-but it really is not-olive oil is a
condiment in southern italy. My family have been comming to Don Pepe for over 50 years-when they were in east NY brooklyn.
The linguine and white clam sauce is the best I have ever had(yes-better than my wife's)
baked clams the best in the world-perfectly done-their red sauce is excellent-chicken and eggplant a very good and different dish.-never had a bad meal here-not fancy or stuffy-just neighborhood people enjoying good food

Dear Yelp, just writing to say hello and that the Russians have probably hacked your server, too. How do I know? Well, it's because Don Peppe's has 371 reviews and four stars, and that's totally unbelievable! First of all, the dining room smelled faintly of urine and cigarettes. Secondly, the carpet and bathrooms were absolutely filthy. Then the food must be really good. It had to be, right? Nope. The food was just barely OK and certainly not worthy of South Ozone Park! And to add insult to injury everything cost twice as much as it should have. Don Peppe's...one star!

Best Italian food I tried. I went in with my girlfriend for her birthday celebration. The staff is nice, and the manger is very social. They are very friendly, and I will bring my other friends to try them out next time stop by JFK airport!

Don Peppe's has bad ambiance.  The restaurant is loud and ugly and the waiter was curt and lacked any grace whatsoever.  I asked the difference between spaghetti marinara and spaghetti pomodoro and he gave some incomprehensible, self-contradictory answer.  I find stupid, rude waiters to be intolerable.  

BUT

The food was just outrageously good, so after much thought I had to give this restaurant 5 stars despite everything else that I normally care about being typical low-class Queens crap.

I never thought that spaghetti marinara (basically pasta with tomato sauce- the plainest and least interesting Italian dish there is) could elicit a "wow" from me.   Well, it did.  And so did the chicken with lemon and butter (rich, sweet, complex citrus flavor) and the artichoke.
Yea so there's Italian food. It's nice with the sauce (and of course bread and of course wine).

You want overpriced Italian food then this is the place for you. Placed a take out order today.  got spaghetti marinara 21.00, baked ziti 20.00 shrimp Luciano 26.00 and chicken don peppe which is not listed on the menu but veal don peppe is 45.00 and veal is more expensive then chicken but I will still include the veal in my total which should of been 112.00 before tax. However the waiter gave me a total of 135.00 how in the world can this be??? This place has you by the balls. And if it wasn't for my family wanting it I would of walked out. And if the prices are not on your board he is a solution get menus!!!!!!!

I've been here multiple times with my family (usually to celebrate someone's birthday). The #1st best thing about this place is that it accomodates large groups. We're talking 10 or more people. #2nd best thing is that the food is goddamn delicious: linguine white clam sauce is my family's favorite dish to order, and I highly recommend you order it as well. Fried calamari, and baked clams are go-to appetizers. Tomahawk steak might be the most expensive dish to order, but we get it anyways. It feeds everyone, the steaks are huge and cooked perfectly how we like it (medium-rare). Other dishes we order are the Baked Ziti, Chicken Don Peppe, Chicken Marsala, Shrimp Marinara, etc... #3rd best thing about this place is that service is always wonderful, even when it's very busy. Decor/ambience is old-school Italian, menu on the wall, Mafia looking people all around, and cash only. 

I highly recommend this place! One of the best Italian restaurants there is in NYC.

Been coming here for many years and it seems to get better every time. If I was asked what my last meal would be there is no question it's Don Peppe. I'm not a fan of linguine in white clam sauce but I would bathe in theirs. The veal don peppe is so simple but so amazing. All the dishes are insane. One of if not my favorite restaurant. Just do yourself a favor and get here.

OMG this is hands down the best Italian food I've ever had the veal was so tender & tasty & the portion sizes are enough for 3 people to share. It's huge guys. My boyfriend and I probably ate it like 2-3 times. The only thing I hated the most was the menu. It's on the wall & if you're seated at the front of the restaurant & blind like me you won't be able to read the menu  it's family friendly & simple but yet have a welcoming feeling. Will be back

Wait staff is old school..... Family style servings and the portions are large. House wine!!!! The food is phenomenal!!

A must try!
One of the best restaurants I been to.  The waiters are very nice.  Food is excellent. I look forward to going back

A-OK! This place definitely serves family style! I was with one other person and we only had to order 1 dish because it was enough for the both us, plus one other person. I expected the venue to be on the higher end of pricing because it had three $ signs but, if you and at least one other person don't mind sharing the same dish, you can actually eat hardily for a reasonable price, especially if you're the one that's "footing the bill".  Pete is a professional waiter who's about his business. After the meal, we were both ready to just relax and watch a movie so, that means the food was filling.

It is very hard to find a good Italian restaurant, especially if you're Italian like myself. This is one of the only places that meets my family's expectations time and time again. I've never had a bad experience at this restaurant in the 10 years I've been eating at "Don Peps". Be prepared it's family style, cash only, no reservations, and you must put your whole order in at once. On weekends during peak hours there will definitely be a wait and there is no parking lot, just street parking.

I like everything at Don Peps for the most part, I'll tell you about their best dishes, in my opinion. First off if you're a wine drinker I recommend getting the house wine, red or white they are both exceptional. I can polish a bottle of either by myself with no problem, it's that good. 

Antipasto-- the baked clams are by far the best in Queens, I dare say NYC, but that is how I feel, they are lightly breaded, fresh, and have the best juice, we usually use a loaf of bread or two just soaking up the juice. The fresh mozzarella and tomato, and the Don Peppe special salad are the go to. The don't have fried calamari so don't go there expecting that. 

Pasta-- Linguine white clam sauce is unreal, it is so consistent, it tastes exactly the same each and every time I go. It is a packed with clams and the sauce is light and filled with flavor; lots of garlic! The spaghetti meat sauce, ziti with broccoli, and the fettuccine al prosciutto are dishes we usually get; we usually order two pasta dishes. The white clam sauce is always number one, number two vaires. 

Beef & Chicken-- Veal Don Peppe is fried to perfection, topped with chopped red onions and  tomatoes. I'm not a huge veal fan, but I can't get enough of this dish. The veal is not tough at all, it is delish! The breast of chicken peppers and mushrooms, the chicken scarpariello, and the chicken marsala are always the go to dishes. The steak pizziola is also another low-key fav, but not always a staple. 

Fish-- The calamari marinara, the seafood marinara, and Lobster Fra Diavolo all excellent in a red sauce. I get the calamari the most, it's usually a bit on the hot side, not gummy. I haven't had the other two dishes in a while, but I've never had any complaints in the past. 

Desserts-- Tartufo; it's an ice cream ball with a chocolate shell and the sorbetto usually comes in the fruit of the flavor you order it in (orange, lemon, coconut) both are delish and very cool! 

A family favorite; molto, molto bene!!

Don Pepes been here 3 or 4 times past 3 or 4 years . Very good Linguine with white clam sauce. Delicious baked clams. Baked ziti good not great but good. Got Veal dish also very good. Might've gotten Fried Calamari. Every dish I've gotten was good to most being very good. 

Might be best Italian food I've ever had come to think of it. Next time I go will take pictures. 
Nice wait staff. Sometimes a long wait. And outdated decor. Cash only is annoying but it is what it is. 

Lastly I have talked Parents out of going here for family dinners more than twice. Reason the cost . While it is very good. And family style it is also over priced. Pasta is inexpensive.

This place gets packed really fast. There's an enclosed outdoor area where you can wait until your table is ready. Street parking is available but ... good luck! 
My family and I (party of 6) came here on a Friday night at around 7:40 and were seated immediately. The staff was extremely welcoming and friendly. The waiter offered suggestions and did not rush us! I hate that they only serve wine by the bottle or half a bottle but not by glass. However, my sister and my mom shared half a bottle and the white wine was dry and strong. By the way.. there's only wine and beer!
Food: 
We tried the garlic pasta and shrimp pasta .. both omg. . Delicious. There was also some sort of shrimp with breadcrumbs (amazing). The lemon chicken was also good and didn't have an overwhelming taste to it. The veal was very tender and flavorful. I enjoyed everything ! The linguini was boiled to perfection and wasn't hard or clumpy.. mmmm delicious. 
I'd highly recommend the tiramisu for dessert, tasted homemade and delish! 
If you're looking for a quiet dinner, don't come here. Everything is family style and it is LOUD. The tables are placed a bit close together so it may seem a bit claustrophobic. I also really did not like the whole cash-only thing. I loved that the serves literally serve your food for you at your table --- from the family sized dishes onto smaller plates. 
Also: there are no menus. The menu is placed on the wall, I wish there would put more than one of those (maybe on another wall too) ?  
Overall: highly recommended for family/group dinners. Total for a party of 6: $266 (tip included)
The best baked clams in Queens :)  And my favorite dinner dish, Veal Don Peppe's.  Enjoy the family style setting, every menu item is delicious!   Cheers

Staff was very pleasant and our waiter Larry was great - served our dishes hot.  Excellent service, I was so excited to be there because I hadn't been there since I was a kid! This is a family style which I generally enjoy.  However, the food was less than mediocre .  Baked clams were boring at best, little to no flavor.  Shrimp Luciano which is a signature dish was ok.  The waiter said it was served with pasta and that we needed an order and 1/2 - well the pasta it was served with was for an additional charge of $19.  Not complaining about the charge but there was not even enough pasta for four people to share. The lemon chicken was tender but nothing to write about.  The veal dish with peppers was equally disappointing.  The Italian cheese cake was flavorless and almost as cold as the house red wine we had with dinner.   In two word - overrated and overpriced!!  Too many other great Italian places for me to ever go back.   I was very disappointed!

This is the place to go for delicious Italian food served family style. It is cash only and there is a menu on the wall, nothing fancy and it looks like it would seat many people. We had the baked clams and the shrimp luciano, mouth watering good ! They serve salad and bread beforehand. The salad dressing is on point.  It's pricey but worth it and you may have some food to take home.

My family arrived at JFK on a flight from Los Angeles. I searched Yelp for a nearby Italian restaurant. Don Peppe's lived up to its review and I would drive from long distance to dine there. The family style dishes were exquisitely prepared and beyond delectable. So much so that the pricey menu was forgotten after the first few bites. Luckily for us we had a fair amount of cash on us because it's a cash only establishment. In summary, you would be hard pressed to find a better meal in a setting that is very inviting............and a feast is being served.

Decided to try this place since it was featured on tv about their linguine with clam sauce. First off, this place doesn't do take out over the phone... odd. Their service and attitude is not so great. Pretty rude actually. Most importantly, their linguine... just ok. Definitely had a lot better with better service.  Also tried their zuppa de clams... very salty!

Im not really sure why this place gets the press it does. I have absolutely had better Italian food. I've even made better Italian, and I'm not Italian. I had the stuffed artichoke, shrimp oreganata and the penne in marinara sauce. Everything came with TONS of water. The artichoke was good, if not bland. The shrimp were pretty tasty but nowhere near the best. The pasta should have been good, but sadly, it was lacking.
A TIP: check the receipt before you pay. We did not realize until the next day that the tip was either included in the total amount of the bill or we were ripped off. We definitely overpaid or over tipped.

Best Italian food you will ever try! Can't even name you one thing that was my fav, because everything is so good ughhhhhh and the price isn't that bad! 
Got a peach sorbet and it was the cutest! They cut it so perfectly and stuffed sorbet inside.
This place is as Italian as it gets. Simple authentic tasting recipes, friendly atmosphere and excellent staff. Best linguine and clams I've ever had and the baked claims were soooooo goooood

this place is amazing , i have been going here since i was kid with my dad and my uncle my they both rest in piece. wow i love it , the food is amazing and awesome. baked claims linguine  in white claim sauce oh its awesome,shrimp luciano   at don peppe's,veal piccata,chicken special ,tartufo    dessert

The food was good -- nothing special. But the reason I'm writing this is to describe the offensive service. In fact, the service at this establishment vies for the worst restaurant service that I've ever experienced. We sat down at 5:30 this Sunday afternoon. Three minutes later a waiter approached our table and said, "What do you want to order?" Not "Hello," not "Welcome to Don Peppe..." We could have been in a fast food joint. Throughout the meal they couldn't wait to clear the plates from one course and rush the next course onto the table. The kicker came once we had finished our family style main courses and told the waiter that we wanted to order something else. He said that we couldn't. I asked about a specific dish. He again said that we couldn't order another plate of food. I thought he was putting us on. He said, no, we really couldn't, that management doesn't allow it, that they need us to leave because there were people waiting to be seated and they needed our seats for the next round of patrons. Mind you, we were eating our dinner and wanted to order more -- we weren't homesteading, we weren't taking up a table for an extended period nursing cups of coffee. As a matter of fact, we hadn't even yet been asked about dessert or coffee. The diner in our neighborhood treats the customer with far more respect than the unwelcoming, contemptuous behavior of Don Peppe's staff and management. My recommendation: Stay away. They don't deserve your patronage.

My favorite was the tomato sauce on the eggplant rollatini. Everything else was typical good Italian food. The sauce was outstanding. The service was mediocre. Nothing special. The cappuccino was not good. Starbucks is better. The coffee was weak and water, no body. My dad got a cannoli and said it was very good, one of the best cannolis in a long time.

We ended up renting a car from Manhattan to go check this place out, and it was totally worth it. The service was impeccably friendly, and this "family-style" restaurant is accurately described. The food was delicious and each course was served to us at perfect intervals. To top everything off, their house-made wine blew me away. I had rather low expectations for a house-made wine, but it was smooth and crisp, and we ended up bringing the left over bottle home! Thanks for making this mini road trip worth it!

My daughter-in-law strongly suggested we have dinner at Don Pepe.  She said it got great reviews, so we went, hunted for off-premiss parking since the restaurant does not have a parking lot.  As you approach the restaurant, numerous signs are taped to the doors and windows reminding patrons of the dress code as well as NO CREDIT CARDS ACCEPTED.   The four of us did a personal body search for cash.  After satisfying our search we had enough money, we were seated. It was suggested by the maitre D, if needed, an ATM was next door.  The dinning room is an open sparsely decorated room with one large menu adorning one wall.  Keep in mind, the portions are family style so if you're a virginal newbie to Don Pepe, like us, we relied on the waiter's guidance and suggestions. We, or at least I, expected hearty fresh Tuscan thick crusted bread.  The bread was mediocre at best, so much for expectations. We prefer olive oil to coat the bread when eating Italian food, strike two - no olive oil for the table.  I guess Don Pepe does not use olive oil in cooking the meals or in the salad dressing.  We ordered the baked clams, which were tasty, smaller than the size of a quarter and in a very delicate garlic butter sauce; read 'delicate' as BLAND.  We ordered a shrimp in garlic and butter sauce platter.  The shrimp were properly sautéed and on the sweet side.  The sauce was delicate, again read 'delicate' as BLAND.  We ordered baked ziti and the sauce had a nice flavor and not acetic; actually this dish should be called "melted ziti" since the cheese and pasta ends lacked the crunchiness and browning of being baked .  Finally a platter of chicken scarpiella with sausage and grilled vegetables arrived.  I'm not a fan of food on the bone but our waiter said being on the bone adds a rich flavor.  The chicken was dry and had a 'delicate' flavor, sort of like cardboard and filled with tiny bones.  Eating the chicken you must be overly concerned to avoid chewing then swallowing the small bones.  We asked the waiter to wrap up the balance of the chicken, about 75% was uneaten and the yet to be served broccoli in oil and garlic.  I can't comment on the latter because we did't eat or see it.  We also ordered a small bottle of house red wine.  When swirling it in my glass I saw many 'legs' running down the inside of the glass so I was expecting something really good to drink.  The wine was just ok, but a 187ml bottle of house wine for $12, I was underwhelmed.  My daughter-in-law asked if we'd be willing to come back.  Not to hurt her feelings, we said sure, but in the back of my mind and unsaid, sure I'll come back - in the next millennium.  To be fair, for a Wednesday night, the place was packed.  After reading a number of positive reviews, I guess they don't like to travel more than 10 minutes to eat at a better Italian restaurant.

Food was amazing! Took about 10 minutes for a waiter to come talk to me. They were a little to lax w customer, imo. But Sangria and my veal parm was probably the best I've ever had.

Very authentic place, classic NY eatery.

Go hungry and bring cash. 

The best classic Italian food I've ever had (outside of Sicily) and I've lived in NY my whole life, so I've eaten a LOT of Italian food.  
This place makes me volunteer to drive people to JFK!
Portions are family style, so the bigger your party the better, so you can try multiple items. 
Try the home made wine and make sure you get the baked clams!

.

The waiter was the worst !!! I mean if i have not been going here for almost 30 yrs .. it seriously was unbelievable how bad he was .. we waited 25 mins for our order .. 60 mins for pasta .. than 20 mins for the check .. 

The food is always top notch.. its THE Best there was is always perfect always delicious.. 
Best pasta and baked clams in the WORLD...
Better than italy !!!

Veal don pepe always tender and tasty .. 

Just that waiter was a disaster.. paid no attention to us at all .. 

When we go back i will never sit w him

read the  bad reviews first,they are all accurate..dumpy place, menu on the wall you could barely read from across the room.  ordered shrimp luciano as so many recommended on the higher stars of this review website.  when ordered, waiter, who had no personality, said "you want it over the linguine, right?"  not thinking it didn't come with it.  when then check came not only did we get about 12 shrimp for $26, the 1/2 lb of linguine it was over was $$$$$14.00.. insane.  $10 for a bottle of sparking water.  when asked for oil to dip bread in,which was basically a warmed up grinder roll, they told us they had no oil, just the butter..  how the hell does any good italian restaurant have no olive oil.  stay away.  $100 for lunch!!!!!
If you go here please be aware that you should go with a bunch of people!!! They serve a lot of food!!! Food is great and wine it's always packed here!! Full of families

I've been wanting to go here for so long but couldn't round up enough people to go. I suggested we take my husband's parents and they were down. First off be aware there is limited street parking so if you go during busy hours you will have trouble. Second they tell you at the door it is a CASH ONLY business. The man who greeted us, counting wads of hundred dollar bills, informed us before bringing us to the table. I was quite shocked a restaurant that must have huge tabs and expensive plates are a cash only establishment. Since we were already there we stayed. 

Our waiter was very professional and informative. We got the baked clams, baked ziti, chicken scarpariello, broccoli in garlic and oil, and shrimp luciano.  Clams were so tasty and delicious. The baked ziti was pretty good, but it literally was only enough to feed 4 people once. I think for the price we should all have some left over or at least for 2 portions. At Carmines the food portions are huge and delicious so I had them in the back of my mind the whole time. The shrimp luciano was delicious but the shrimps were small as hell and it was such a small portion. I didn't eat the chicken but everyone at the table hated it. It was dry and bland, and they asked if we wanted the "complete package" which included potatoes and sausage. What they failed to mention was that was an additional 21 dollars on top of a $61 dollar plate of badly cooked chicken. Our broccoli still hadn't come out yet so I had to ask for it go. When I got home I saw the mostly burned pieces of vegetable and it tasted as bad as it looked. I threw it out and took most of the night as a loss. 

P.S House wine is basically just regular wine. Go to Carmines!

This place is definitely a haul to make it out to by mass transit if you are coming from Manhattan but it's worth it. There is a dress code but it's not crazy strict. No jerseys or ball caps but T-shirt and jeans is fine. Its cash only so keep that in mind when planing your night. It gets busy so expect to wait a little but not crazy long. the wait time was a little over an hour on a Saturday night at around 7:00 when we were there. 

There is a large separate waiting room at the entrance with some seating but most people were standing. When you arrive go in through to the restaurant and put your name on the list with the host. Then hang out in the waiting room until your name is called. 

PRO TIP: Ask to use the restroom while you are waiting. Take your time as you walk through and get an idea of what you want to order.

The restaurant consists of one large bustling room with loud conversation being had all around. It very much adds to the ambiance of a family style Italian restaurant. The menu is only on the wall so don't expect a personal menu. All dishes are served family style on all large platters and the wine comes by the carafe. 

For drinks we ordered a carafe of the house red which we thought was a great complement to the mean. The food here is excellent. We started with an order of the fried peppers. It comes as a platter of charged peppers and onions that is nicely seasoned and coated in olive oil. This was a nice vegetarian option as a starter for the table and paired nicely with the bread provided. For Entrees we ordered the Shrimp Luciano over linguine and an order of the stuffed shells. The platter of linguine was very large and can easily feed three or more people depending on your appetite. I thought this dish was amazing and the highlight of the mean for me. The stuff shells came as a much smaller order. Its reflected in the price but its about enough for a single serving if that is all you are eating. Also very good but did not stand out as much as the shrimp over linguine. For desert we shared a piece of the ricotta cheesecake, by this point we were all pretty full but the cheesecake provided a nice end to the meal. Along with this I ordered a single shot which was a little small and I would go with a double if I had to do it again. 

Overall an excellent experience that would recommend to everyone.

Simply The Best! 
Nobody makes baked clams better than Don Peps
Nobody makes a veal better than Veal Don PePe
Nobody makes a better Linguine with White Clam Sauce

One of the great advantages of having great New York (family) is that they introduce you to some of the best out of the way places imaginable. Don Peppe lives up to that description. Great old style family style Italian, served by a crew that has worked here forever and accepts cash only. My personal favorites, linguini clam sauce, spaghetti filletto, baked clams and their veal milanese

We were so lucky to have Marco help us. Shrimp Luciana over linguine was great, Naples (or Sicily ?) style. One tad bit salty for my taste but the flavor was so delicious!! The veal with chopped tomatoes and onions was also a perfected recipe. The appetizer baked clams was a little too oily for my taste,  but everything else made up for it. Keep in mind that between the linguine and veal dishes we could've fed five people, and we were a party of two. So I know what I'm having for breakfast!  A unique and unforgettable total experience and over everything thanks to Marco who we loved talking to!

I have been wanting to try this place out for a while. My husband and I went for my birthday and it was pretty quiet around 4:30ish pm. We walked in to a group of men playing cards and horse racing memorabilia all over the walls. Only a few tables were occupied. They told us to sit anywhere. We had the most attentive waiter, Harry. We told him it was our first time here and he was more than happy to suggest dishes for us. For appetizer we had the baked clams. They were absolutely delicious. The topping and the sauce they came with was garlicky and buttery and we mopped it up with the amazing bread that came with the meal. Next was the linguine with clams. I was impressed at how perfectly the pasta was cooked. It still had a bite to it and it was so addicting. The sauce was perfect and I couldn't stop eating it. We also had the chicken special which was thin fried chicken with a tomato sauce on top. I was full at this point but couldn't help tasting. It was so moist and the tomatoes on top made it even more delicious. Our waiter kept checking in on us at the perfect times and we even made small talk with him. We will definitely be back. It was such a pleasant experience.

P.S. CASH ONLY!

Very good food & enormous portions. Nothing is ordinary , everything is delicious!!
5 Stars - Anything with shrimp - Especially shrimp luciano & the linguini in clam suace

My husband and I went there for dinner last night (for about the 500th time in our lives).  The place has become absolutely filthy!!!  The walls are encrusted with food debris, the ceiling has huge dirty water stains (from roof leaks), the carpet has not been vacuumed/shampooed in ages.  One of my forks had dried tomato sauce on it and I had to polish our knives to get rid of the unappealing water stains on them.  We won't even discuss the condition of the restrooms!!!

Our waiter was seated at a table on the extreme side of the restaurant reading a newspaper.  There was the usual table of men playing cards, totally oblivious to what was going on around them.  This is especially notable because two of the men were the chef and the "manager", who clearly couldn't be bothered paying any attention to the business they are supposed to be running.  Our waiter forgot to bring our order of broccoli rabe with our chicken and we had to ask one of the busboys to get him from where he was reading the paper to remind him that we hadn't gotten our full order.  He was extremely apologetic and went  to get our broccoli rabe (which took about 10 minutes) and treated us to a half bottle of wine on him.  

With all these complaints you might wonder why we have been there so many times.  Well, the food is still butt-kicking good but I'm starting to wonder if it's worth it with the ever-increasing prices, yucky surroundings and slap-dash service.
Excellent food & service. They really accommodate their guests. Go early because parking can be difficult

We went this past Sat night (9/23/17) for my husband's birthday. We were 5 ppl total.
After being in Manhattan for the San Gennaro Feast, we were all hungry and couldn't 
wait to eat at Don Peppe's. Well to our surprise... their portions are definitely NOT 
"Family Style". We ordered the baked clams, which for $26 a dozen were the size of a walnut.
Mozzarella & Tomato w- roasted peppers (4 pieces each) Family style?? Think Again...
We also ordered the linguine & white clam sauce and veal marsala and chicken scarparello which was basically, little pieces of cut up roasted chicken $21 a 1/2 order and the kicker was the potatoes, sausage & pepper weren't included but at an EXTRA cost you could order separately. Why call this dish Chicken Scarparello then ???? The service was no better.
The waiter told us we couldn't order anything else once our order was placed??? So if you wanted another appetizer - well FORGET ABOUT IT !!! Never have we heard of such a thing.
Lastly, The Italian bread you could have gotten better from your local grocery store &
$10 a pitcher for soda filled with ice was in my opinion ABSURD.... Thumbs Down Don Peppe
Totally disappointed and would never go again or recommend to anyone.

Loved it! The service was top-notch, waiter was a gentleman. The clams lived up to their reputation - amazing. The veal was perfect. Linguine was a little more firm than what you would expect al dente to be, as lately everyone's al dente is too soft. This linguine was old-school perfect. House wine tasted home made and charming. Can't wait to go back.
This place was terrible. The food was eh but there was nasty in our water. Family style? It was awkward as hecking heck. Also it's cash only. And 2017. Just a bunch of locals go there. Whatever!

This rating is from an Italian who grew up in Brooklyn with a large family. None of my family who went with my family to try it out enjoyed the experience.1st off bread served on table was hard and stale couldn't butter it without it breaking apart. Food was not bad but way way over priced for what you received. Wine served in used open bottles was cheap swill. At end of meal when asked if we wanted dessert most of us asked for coffee, guess what no coffee served here only higher priced cappuccino or expresso, ordered cappuccino asked for whipped cream on top, no whip cream, i ordered a canoli looked old and tasted old. Bottom line place is old and rundown, bathrooms are filthy, service is by men who look like there doing you a favor by there presence. This place is for people who go there because of the name it cannot be for the food  the look of the place or service, do yourself a favor spend your money some place else. ** After spending almost a small fortune with my group when I got home i made a prosciutto sandwich I was still hungry

Love this place. Old school chalkboard menu on the wall and you just order.  That's it!  The portions are incredibly large, so if you walk in this place hungry... you are exiting in the most satisfying pain ever!

Just got back from peppes a little while ago. First time there and I've lived so close to it for a hundred years. It was amazing. We started with the baked clams which my mother in law recommended. They were amazing. After that we ordered the linguine pomodoro. I was upset with this selection because I wanted garlic and oil but when it came holy crap was it good!! The sauce is amazing and pasta cooked just right. I want some more right now. Then we got the chicken scarpariello and veal Marsala. Both amazing as well, I especially loved the chicken in the scarpariello. Can't wait to go back. Only downfall is the very much outdated decor and the dust just hanging off of the vents of the AC. Still not enough to lose a star the food is too good, but it definitely needs an upgrade inside

Had the opportunity to come back a couple of more times and I am definitely still a fan.  Not gonna lie, this is not a cheap dinner, but if you are willing to accept that you will have a great meal.  The place seems to shine when you are with a group, but we were also perfectly happy when there were 2 of us.  Our waiter was wonderful and had no issues in talking through how much of each item we'd need for the group and who would be eating what.  He even made sure our pregnant diner with a fish allergy was well fed.

On a Sunday afternoons before 3 we had no problem getting a table for 9.  The house red is awesome, is it Opus One?  No, but this is good table wine that goes down way too easy.  Whatever you do come prepared to eat, I mean really eat.  We started out with baked clams (yum), seafood salad (the most tender calamari and octopus I have ever had, really perfect) and a Don Pepe Special Salad (wonderful).  From there we went on to the pasta course which was the Shrimp Luciano with Linguine.  I've had a lot of shrimp and linguine dishes, but this one is on another level.  Perfectly cooked shrimp in a light tomato cream sauce with maybe some brandy(?) and tons of shallots; it's amazing.

Next was the meat course; the chicken parmigiana is a great version, but the chicken scarparello with sausage and peppers was excellent.  We were stuffed, but how about some dessert...sure OK.  The waiter brought a platter filled with tartufo (ice cream), cannoli and tiramisu and of course we dug in to the decadent sweets.

It's super casual place with excellent food; remember to bring lots of cash and mangia!

Good food and environment. I've lived in Ozone Park for over 20 years and have always heard about Don Peppe. I went with a group of 10 people to this "family style" restaurant, which was a different concept for all of us. The family style concept gives you a feeling as if you're having Sunday dinner at home with your family. (I think 10 people was too much for this experience. I feel 6 people would've been better.) Because of the large portions of food we were able to share and try a variety of what Don Peppe has to offer. I tried baked clams, mozzarella and tomatoes, anti pasto, spaghetti pomodoro w/ prosciutto and chicken marsala. Everything was good. My favorite was the mozzarella and tomatoes, my least favorite was the chicken. I had high expectations for this restaurant having heard repeated great reviews. The food was good but I was not impressed.

Everytime I visit NY I have to go to Queens and have dinner at Don Peppes! They have amazing Baked Clams and their Linguini & Clams are the BEST on the planet!  
Their House Red Wine is fantastic as well! 
Great service and Delicious food!

Family style......almost like Carmines in NYC.  Carmines is better in my opinion.
Sauce is good.  Linguine and clams seems like they used the canned chopped clams rather than fresh......not a fan of that.  Might have to give the place another shot
This place is like a hidden gem. Staff is attentive and friendly. The food was great. The house wine was a bit strong too. Overall great experience.

Hands down - this is my favorite restaurant of all time. If I had to have one last meal, shrimp Luciano, baked clams, and a cannoli from Don Peppe's would be it. The food is unbelievable here! The house wine is also delicious. Believe the hype - this place is incredible.

We chose this place because it had relatively good reviews, when we arrived the "host" pointed at 2 tables and said "you guys can sit there or over there" we walked over ourselves and sat down, we waited for at least 10 minutes for a waiter to come around and at least offer us water but that didn't happen none of the waiters came over so we simply got back up and left. Worst service ever!

Extremely overrated. I ordered stuff shells to go, when I get home I opened the container only to be disappointed. I paid $13.00 dollars for three stuffed shells! Eat at Lenny's clam bar in Howard beach you will never be disappointed!

I had a wonderful experience at Don Peppes. Feels like a throwback in time while part of family you're not part of. Very comforting place with staff that are hilarious and know the place better than they probably know themselves. 

The wine was great, appetizers were big. I must add all the plates are family style - very big portions. The food was wonderful, it very home style. By that i mean it tastes like your grandmother cooked it if you're into that. It's not exactly my taste which is why i'm giving them 4 stars. 

I would come back but i wouldn't go out of my way. Parking might be an issue also.

Don Peppe is hands down my favorite Italian restaurant in NY.  The food is absolutely amazing and of the highest quality.  Everything on the menu is phenomenal.  Shrimp Luciano is to die for.  Service is good, menu is literally on the wall for you to read and they only serve wine.  The prices are a little high but well worth it for the best high-end Italian restaurant in the state.

It's really too bad that the waiters who "work" here have ruined this place for me (for the 3rd time in a row). Because the food is truly amazing, but the service is awful and waitstaff are extremely rude.  You will wait forever for your food and it's impossible to get their attention to bring the dish they forgot 39 mins ago because they are too busy staring at their reflection off of the glass meat counter.  These guys think they are somebody, wanna-be gangstas out of a Godfather movie.  Disrespecting and mocking customers as if they were a group of high-school cheerleaders.  Seriously, you're over 40, borderline obese, all male team of waitresses who cant even master a task as simple as bringing the correct food to a table.  It wouldn't take 8 requests to get the check from a a monkey.  These guys are the perfect example of a "public service ad" telling kids to stay in school.  
I would never expect this type unprofessional, immature, ignorant behavior from a gas station attendant, let alone a reputable restaurant.  They should be embarrassed to call themselves "Italians".

Came here for an early dinner with a friend. Just a heads up everything here is served family style and is cash only. We had the mussels in red sauce, the linguine in white clam sauce, and cannolis for dessert. Everything was so delicious. I couldn't get enough of the red sauce from the mussels. I think I ate an entire loaf of bread dipping it in the red sauce. I will definitely be returning here for dinner

Let me tell you .... I'm from Staten Island & it's worth the trip on the belt !!!! Make sure you go w/ a few friends ( at least 6-8 ppl )  cause then you get a full variety of there food & make sure your hungry cause you will eat .... linguini & clams  Bam !!!   mussels in red sauce pow !!!!   ( I think I ate a loaf of bread support in the sauce 's. ).  I would never order chicken parm.  Right ?  Chicken parm. Is chicken parm ,  but not here !!!! It was the best I ever had ever !!!!!!  The veal don Pepe. Banging just banging !!!!!   The menu is on the wall 6-8 apps 8-9 Dinner item 2-3 dessert  no specials cause the food here is special. & I laughed when  I was told that but I will tell everyone the same now.  It is that good !!!!
Came here before a flight based on reviews. Just ok. No better than your average Italian restaurant. Family style was a plus. Charged $9 for a Peroni! Will try somewhere else next time.

I have been to hundreds of Italian restaurants but not one comes close to Don Peppe. The food is absolutely amazing specially the veal Don Peppe. The spaghetti in clam sauce is to die for. The waiters are so authentic and always know what to suggest. The home made wine is superb. I have been coming here for over ten years and will continue to do so. Definitely a must try!!

We came here on a Tuesday night at 8:00.  Place was busy.  We had baked clams linguine and white clam sauce Chicken Son Pepe and escarole.  Everything was delicious.  Service was excellent.  Love the old world Italian fell here.  Brings me back to an early day Little Italy.

Italian Family Style Dining. 

What we ordered :
1.5x Baked Clams 
2x Linguine White clam
2x Shrimp Luciano 
1 Stuffed Mushroom
1 Tomahawk Steak (Not shown on Menu)

Definitely get the white clam pasta and baked clams. The tomahawk was amazing, but when the bill came, it looks like it was more than everything else combined. We should've asked for the price first, but aside from the price the steak was cooked perfectly. 

Not accepted here :
No hats
No credit cards
No tanktops 
No baby carriages/strollers

The wait here can get pretty long, they do have a pretty big waiting area though with benches that stretch really long. The staff was ok, we had to remind them a few times about our sodas which came an hour later. Overall satisfied, but I think they miscalculated our bill by adding a mysterious $28 charge on the bill. 

Note their posted 2018 VACATION schedule:
They will be closed January 29th - March 1st 2018. We heard from the waiter that they usually close in August too. Looks like they do pretty well for themselves to close business for 2 months.

Words cannot describe this utterly fantastic restaurant.  the staff is very friendly the food is absolutely delicious I've never ever had a bad meal there in all the years I've been going there and I have tried almost everything on the menu if you want a place to eat out this is the place to do it.. But just remember it's CASH ONLY....

As usual...fantastic meal.  Late lunch today after picking up my better half from Kennedy.  Shrimp Luciano, some house wine.....so good.  Love this place....looks and feels like an old time cafeteria but with great food. No reservations and no credit cards.

I will make this review easy to read. Food is way over priced for what you receive, don't ask for anything extra like maybe a little olive oil to go on the hard Italian bread they serve you, and dont ask for a cup of coffee after a meal because they don't serve any, decor is outdated, waiters act like they are doing you a favor by your eating there. And make sure you ask for a fresh piece of pastry if you order any but don't ask for whip cream on the side because you won't get any. If you don't care about spending money give the restaurant a try, your experience might be better

This place isn't what is used to be.  Been going here for years.  The food is SO good but this isn't where you want to go if you're looking to stay, relax and enjoy your meal.  We had a party of 10 and they rushed us out of there with the quickness.  They were actually ripping the table cloth off to change it from underneath the coffee we were still drinking.  Also depends on the server you receive as some are clearly not happy to be there.

Came here for a family birthday dinner. It was the birthday boy's favorite restaurant...... WAS. He was so disappointed with the experience that he was apologizing to ME for hyping the place up so much. 

I had heard such rave reviews about this place from these people, that I was pretty damn excited. Fanciful tales of bountiful, orgasmic food and service in a family style, old-fashioned Italian way.

Meh.

Apparently, family style means that the rude waiter barks at you for your order and drops a couple platters of food on the table 20 mins later before wandering off. Then the maitre de comes over and cuts your giant veal cutlet for you with a spoon while pontificating and expounding on random nonsense at the top of his lungs. I've never experienced service quite like this. I've been to other family style places and this is not how it's supposed to be done. 

The food is..... okay. Nothing to rave about, but nothing to complain about either. Our party was bragging about the portion sizes beforehand. Bunch of Italians saying things like "hope you're hungry" etc. etc.... they weren't scaring this Viking. I crushed the last of the food after they had all quit and was still hungry when I left. 

This place is expensive. Which would be fine, if it was a really nice place with great service..... it's not. 

This place is LOUD. You have to shout to your waiter, or the person across the table. 

This place is cramped. They pack you in like sardines. 

The best beer they have is Peroni in a bottle. Basically, Italian Budweiser. And you have to beg to get even that. So, tough luck beer lover.

Now, my main problem with this place..... they rush you. Like ridiculous. They want to turn the table over and get fresh asses in the seats. I get it. But, they literally run over with the check and demand you pay the second you are done eating. 

This place must make a fortune from all the local goombas that flock there. But, they've seen the last of me. More importantly, they've seen the last of my entire party... Who were all disappointed in the experience and were fairly regular customers.

Seriously you will never go wrong here , the best family style restaurant around the good is amazing the atmosphere is amazing and the staff are beyond impeccable, so happy they are in my neck of the woods , I go at least once a month with my family , bring cash tho they do not take credit cards but that's just fine with me .

So in 2012 I left a negative review. I just happen to check Yelp and for some reason Don Peps review had a new heading. It was changed to Downtown Pizza. I did not change it !! So here my my review again.
400 bucks and the worst service and dinner of my life. I will never eat here again. Eggplant that was under cooked. Braciola that was dry, unseasoned and flavorless. The pasta was good, wow they didn't mess up the pasta. But the sauce tasted like it came from a jar. The manager never once came over to ask how dinner was. They were all too busy watching TV. This place is living off its reputation from 30 years ago. Soup to nuts we were done in 50 minutes. They put nascar pit crews to shame. Take my advice try another restaurant this place isn't worth it.

I have only came once, but I loved it! The wait was horrendous, I waited an hour and a half, but once we got to the table, the food was amazing. I loved their baked clams and pasta. Big portions!!! Can't wait to come again! 
I could only find a photo of the cowboy steak we ordered.
Beware: menu on the wall so don't be mad if you don't get a physical one :) 
We ordered: baked clams, garlic and clam pasta, veal with butter and lemon, white wine, and fetticine al proscuitto.
One of the best Italian places I've ever been to. Highly recommend the chicken Don Pepe
I love this place this place is amazing the food is authentic I recommend going there every day and of story just go there
One of my fav place to go! They have the best don peppe chicken, backed clams, linguine with clam sauce, and stuffed shells!

I love the vibe of Don Pepe's. We felt like we were in a true Italian neighborhood, old school. It was Christmas Eve, the place was packed, Huge dishes were being brought out and put on tables all around us, the waiter walked out from the kitchen holding a 6 pound lobster with it's tails and claws flying to show to a potential customer. The menu was written on a short board on the wall and the place was generally louder and happy. We enjoyed every minute. By the Way, the food was fabulous. Don't miss!

On March 23, 2018, my wife arranged a surprise birthday party for me with 21 family members attending.  I was surprised!  Don Peppe's Restaurant made the night very special.  The anti pasta, the baked clams and the two pasta dishes that started the meal were nothing less than excellent and I was amazed I could still eat after the sumptuous portions.  The main courses consisting of veal cutlet, chicken cutlet and shrimp were all to die for!!!  Capping the night with an terrific assortment of deserts and Italian coffees made most of us to agree to go on diets for the next week.  The restaurant waiter service were polite, professional and anticipated and satisfied all of our needs.  I can't believe it took me 70 years to find the best restaurant in town.  Bravo, Bravo, Bravo!!!

I've been coming here since my parents took me to eat when their flight to Israel was delayed in the the 1970's (when they had a partition separating the eating areas and the maitre di smoked a big cigar ). I moved away from New York in 1985 and now I visit twice a year. I eat at Don Pepe each time with a bunch of old friends. The more people the better because then you can taste a bunch of good stuff.  The food is the best. I love the atmosphere and anyone who complains about the waiters should be banned. They are friendly, knowledgeable and alot of fun. All the food is great but my dinner most times start with the Fried Sweet Red Peppers (which are to die for) and Baked Clams. Then Linguini with White Clam Sauce and Linguini with Red Sauce (for those who don't like white clam sauce ). And then Chicken Scarpariello, Veal Picata, A Shrimp Dish, lots of wine and finished off with a cappuccino, tartufo, tortoni and the best canolli I have ever eaten anywhere. After all these years I have never been disappointed with anything and either has anyone I brought there except  one of my friends who doesn't like lot of garlic in his food.

Best baked clams and linguini with white clam sauce on the planet. Old school feel to this place and my favorite Italian restaurant in a city loaded with Italian food. You just can't go wrong here. Going early isn't an issue but know that if you go late you will have a long wait........that is well worth it. Enjoy!

I was going to give this place 4 stars, due to the excessive wait for a table, but because the food made up for the wait, I had to give it 5.  Aside from our hour-long wait and lack of taking reservations, the experience was great!  First thing you need to know is that they only take cash, and there is no menu, just a blackboard listing the choices (there is a wide variety to choose from).  Our waiter, Harry, was efficient and friendly.  He answered all of our questions with a smile.  The next thing you need to know is that this restaurant is family-style, meaning that the portions are huge!  We started out with the baked clams, which were perfect.  Next we tried the stuffed mushrooms, the shrimp cocktail, both of which were very good.  The bread is flavorful and they are generous with the refills. The wine, which appears to be homemade, was so good.  I am not a huge wine fan (they do not serve hard liquor and there is no bar), nor is my husband, and we both had two glasses.  Our company, who knows a lot about wines, loved it as well.  For the entrees, we ordered the linguine with white clam sauce; their signature dish, which was fantastic! The portion easily could feed four people!  We also ordered the linguine with marinara sauce (delish) and the chicken cutlet parm.  Everything was extremely good, and despite the probable wait, I will definitely go back.

Came here for dinner. Ordered the baked clams and mussels. Not clean, mouthful of sand. For entree, we ordered the spaghetti marinara, sauce was salty with a few pieces of garlic for $24! Worst recommendation of 2018. For sure, we're not coming back.
No good not coming back here to eat sands , I'm definitely not gonna take anymore recommendations from that same person who've recommended me this place

One of the best or the best Italian food I've ever had. The baked clam, linguini with white clam sauce and baked portobello. OMG, I am drooling just thinking of them. And don't forget to order their house white, goes super well with the food, I can probably have two bottle of those by myself. Most of the servers been there for a long time, and it's kind of hit or miss with their service. But it's the food that keeps on bringing us back.

This was an unexpected great while staying overnight at a hotel by JFK airport. My wife and I went there on a Saturday night around 7:00, but we were lucky to get seemed immediately even though the place was packed and larger parties were waiting. We both said this was one of the best meals we've had in quite some time and we eat out often. The veal with peppers and mushrooms had a red sauce that was awesome. The waiter was great. Not one thing I can say that's negative. Just know that it's a cash only place.

I can't begin to explain how disappointed I am from my experience on a Saturday night. My family used to always look forward to coming here- from the wine, to baked clams, and shrimp luciano- it all used to be delicious. If you wanted to come here on a Saturday a year ago, you'd be waiting hours. Let's just say we waited 5 minutes on a Saturday night at 7:30 and that's not a good sign. My boyfriend and I called about 7 other restaurants before we decided to come here and no one had reservations until 9:30 that night. 
We started off with white wine, antipasto salad, baked clams, and stuffed mushrooms. The sauce on the clams and mushrooms had absolutely no taste and the amount of oil was insane. We then got the shrimp luciano and that was good, however also extremely oily. For our main course, we decided on the porter house and we completely regret the decision. Not only did it take long to come out, it seems as though they completely forgot about it because the dryness of the steak was unreal. Not even edible. When we asked for the check, the waiter asked if the steak was ok. We told him it was very dry and he asked if we wanted him to talk to the chefs. Quite honestly, it was already 9:30 at this point so it wasn't worth it. However, if you see your customers didn't even touch their $90 steak, how do you not comp them some how? A few dollars off the bill.. a free dessert. Well, nothing. $273 later and we left extremely disappointed and told ourselves we'll never be back. 
I have no idea what happened to this place, but they had a really great thing going for them and it completely went down the drain.

I've been here three times to date. The first time I came here, I was definitely more than surprised to see that the menu was painted on the wall.
We always start with baked clams.  They're probably my favorite thing on the menu and are always cooked perfectly.  The sauce that is used on the clams is perfect when you dip the Italian bread in it.  I always try so hard not to fill up on this.
Last time I was there, we had the chicken scarparello.  I really wasn't sure what it was before ordering it, but I am really glad that we got it (chicken with sausage and peppers).  The veal Don Peppe is another favorite of mine.
I have never been disappointed by the food and service. I always leave stuffed.  I enjoy family style meals because it means you can try a few different dishes all in the same night!

PS.  The wait can be long.  It is cash only.  Waits tend to be long.

My son had eaten here a couple of months ago and wanted to take the rest of the family to celebrate my wife and my anniversary.  I read all the reviews and checked out all the photos.  

Yes, the food was pretty darn good.  Really good.

Yes, the service was pleasant but not great.

And yes, the prices are too high.

For example, a double order of tomatoes and mozzarella, which is six slices of tomato with six slices of mozzarella and a sprinkling of olive oil and basil...$48.  I mean it was good quality and pretty tasty but that price is ridiculously high.

Everything else we had was priced better but still overpriced in my opinion.

Aside from the above, we had the baked clams.  They were pretty good but I've had better.  We then had the Shrimp Luciano with pasta.  1.5x portion for four of us.  It was great.  Really great.  What we didn't know is that on the menu, the $27 is for the Shrimp ONLY.  The pasta is separate.  So 1.5x of the shrimp was $42 and 1.5x for the pasta was $21.  So that means it cost $63 for the pasta course for four of us.  However, there were plenty of delicious shrimps (5 or 6) apiece with a good amount of pasta.  The sauce was fabulous.

We then had an order of chicken parmagiana and an order of veal with lemon and butter.  This was accompanied by an order of escarole.  All three dishes were fantastic.  There was just enough for the five of us.

Finally, we had three cannolis, one tiramisu, an espresso, and a cappuccino.  They were reasonably priced and delicious.

We had three sodas.

So for the five of us, it cost $325.  I think that's too much but the food was all so good...and my son paid!  I think it's good to experience the Italian family style meal that I grew up with but I still think it's overpriced

This place has been a staple for the boys for years now.

Went during the week so no issues waiting for a table. 

Tom mozz  huge portion...       perfect
Broccoli  in olice oil n garlic...   perfect
Baked clams...                         perfect
The other 4 went with Italian dishes, which were served family style and again perfect ( chicken and veal)
I went with the cowboy ribeye, and I'll tell yea, it can easily take the Pespi challenge to meat staples such as Lugers, Chris, and Morton.
Med rare, was in fact med rear, and huge.

If you can find a parking spot, it's well worth the trip

Wow, an amazing family style Italian restaurant. Sauce is right and the favors are booming. Be ready to spend money here for sure. Not really a dinner  for two because you're guarantee leftover. The service is friendly. The only thing was the chicken was a bit dry.

I've been there 3 or 4 times now and am always so happy with the food and the service. I go there whenever I can but sometimes it's logistically impossible. I haven't taken any pictures up until now but this time I got one of the linguini and clams in white sauce and the escarole. This was the first time I've ever had linguini and clams so I wasn't quite sure what to expect. The white sauce was more of a clam broth, which I found to be much better for me health-wise. Just keep your leftovers level or they'll leak!

I'll try a different entree next time because it's my goal to try everything they have but I'll be getting the escarole every single time I go there from now on. I can't even describe how delicious the browned, whole garlic cloves they toss in there are.

The only thing that perplexes me is that they don't appear to have chicken parmigiana as a standalone entree. Is that akin to ordering "a side of queso" at a Mexican restaurant?

This is fantastic a classic Italian restaurant. I had the linguini and white clam sauce, which was among the best I've personally ever had. The lemon and garlic chicken is fantastically done, with an array of flavors. The desert is great, in particular the canolies. 10/10 would recommend.
Amazing Italian food had shrimp Luciano with house made butter sauce creamy beige truly amazing, also had thee steak, also an incredible dish.. extremely happy worth every penny..

Yo!! Whats really good good wit that Buttah sauce!!!!! Seriously, props to my boss for hoking dinner!!! #EyeSeeyou  Anyways, my roomate and myself ate like royalty....we drank some wines and ate some foodz and laughed some laughs sat down on the seatz and talk some talks. #CreeeEamyBeige

We have been going to Don Peppe's for more than 30 years.  Living out of the area now, we are only able to eat here every year or two.  The food is still outstanding.  Love the Zuppa di Clams, with garlicky red sauce.  Their pasta with marinara sauce is also delicious, as is the chicken parm.  Everything is served family style, and the waiters know just how much to bring based on who's eating what dish.  Cash only, with fair prices for a large, full course meal.  Great place, with fine service!

Cash only place! Make sure you bring enough. Your credit cards are not worthy here! LOL! The restaurant is huge, especially the waiting area at the front. We came here during lunch time. I'm sure it's always packed at dinner time.

They don't give out olive oil for the table, only butter is served with the bread. It's a family style restaurant, so one plate looks enough for two. We ordered chicken scarpariello and seafood marinara. Both dishes come as is, just the way it's described, meaning the seafood marinara has only the seafood and marinara sauce without the pasta and chicken scarpariello comes only with the chicken. Hubby orders the sides of potato and sausage for the chicken but I really didn't care for the pasta so I liked mine as is. One great thing about my seafood marinara is the tenderness of the seafood. Nothing too chewy from this seafood. I really liked munching on it. Seriously, so tender! I wonder what they did prior to serving the seafood. I'd like that secret. As for the sauce, the homemade marinara sauce was quite delicious. Hubby's chicken dish was all right but I didn't think it's the best chicken scarpariello I've ever had but Hubby liked it. To be honest, we're happy campers that day because we enjoyed our meals. 

We thought the prices for entrees were a bit higher than most family style restaurants but I guess since most people know the name, it's worth the try. Check your piggy bank, I'm sure you could spend for at least one nice meal at Don Peppe!
I can't say how great this place is, it's hard. I gave it a 4 star because it's pricey, but the food is fresh and delicious.

Good. Basic good Italian food. The food is served family style. We ordered linguini with white clam sauce and another with meat sauce (all beef), eggplant parmesan and chicken with lemon and pepper. We did not have dessert, but did have 2 appetizers; cold antipasto and tomato/mozarella. I liked the latter the least of everything. The meal was relatively quick. I would return. Beware...cash only.

Best Italian food I've had in NYC. You'll walk into a lot of old school Italians eating traditional NY Italian food at its best.

- Baked clams are the best in the world. Especially when they are baked with all the clam juice poured all over it. 
- Veal Don Pepe was the best veal I've ever had anywhere. Chopped tomatoes and onion with a touch of balsamic over a nice piece of fried veal
- White clam sauce over linguine. I love Carmine's version. Love it. My friend kept hyping this one up as a far better version. It's better but not far better. If Carmine's is the 9 of white clam linguine, Don Peppe is a 10. Tons of clams, tons of garlic and sauce is insanely good. 
- Chicken Marsala. Eh I would pass on this. Not particularly my favorite dish in general anywhere but it was decent. 

If you're gonna go, go on a weekday late after work to avoid the massive crowds on the weekends.

2 stars  cause the clams and the shrimp oregnata are really good.  The homemade wine was good.  Bread with butter. No oil ! Pomodoro sauce, I think Ragu is better no joke.  Ambience none.  90 dollar steak pizziola.  I don't think so. Cash only no menus.  Come on people. Get over it.  Save your money there are plenty of great Italian restaurants without the attitude

Maybe I was disappointed because I read so many rave reviews.  The food wasn't bad but it wasn't great either. Asked for some extra sauce and was told "sorry can't give you any."  Had much better food at much better prices other places. No need to ever go back.

My wife and I ate at Don Peppe for the first time last night to celebrate our anniversary. We arrived about 6:00 on a Friday evening and found a parking spot right in front of the place. We were seated right away with no wait whatsoever. The waiter was happy to advise us about the different dishes and the size of the portions, which are quite large. All through the meal the service was friendly and thoroughly professional. 
We started with the baked clams, nice, fresh, little necks with delicious garlicky bread crumbs. Then we had the stuffed artichoke, about the best I've ever had.
For our pasta course we ordered the spaghetti marinara. The pasta was cooked perfectly and the sauce was delicious. The portion was huge, more than enough for two.
For our main course we split one order of Shrimp Luciano and an order of sauteed broccoli. The shrimp was fresh and perfectly done and reminded us of Shrimp Scampi with a tasty pink sauce. The broccoli was well done and cooked with an abundance of garlic. Actually all the dishes we ordered involved garlic which we enjoy.
For dessert we had cannolis  and I had an espresso.
This place is on the expensive side and dinner for two ran us $150 before the tip. Considering the special occasion and the quality of the food it was money well spent. We'll be back.

I'd admit that Don Peppes Baked Clams are the best. Just wish the clams were bigger in size . The linguini with white clam sauce is my favorite pasta dish!!! It's a must! I can never seem to order any other pasta dish.  I've noticed though that the amount of clams inside that dish have been downsized. SMH! 
The service is better on certain days But the food is worth the visit.  Delicious and No Matter how full I am; I always end up ordering their nice strong and hot cappuccino ! Oh, and How can I forget? Dessert!!!!

A must when you are in New York. Have been coming here since I was literally born. So grateful for their amazing staff both FOH and BOH. Baked clams. Veal Don Peppe. Lemon chicken butter. Linguine and clams. Shrimp fra diablo. Delicous.

We went out for dinner, 3 couples. The linguine with clams were out of this world. The shrimp luciano and baked clams a hit as usual. But shame on me and the other 2 couples why we didn't question the bill about the $130.00 tomahawk ribeye we ordered. $130.00 for 8 pieces of sliced meat with a big bone. Highway robbery. I'm upset because every time i go there the bill is written on a piece of paper with no rhyme or reason. I gave it 3 stars for the food. Always great! But i feel like they size you up and make whatever price they want to. It's always at least $100 a person when we go and for the life of me i don't know why. Tonight's bill was $270 per couple. Must have been a slow night so they needed to hit us up. Sorry. Just the bad taste i get in my mouth when i leave there although I'm in paradise when I'm eating the linguine and clams.  Go figure. I'm not a cheap person. I love eating food and don't mind paying but i get this feeling the last couple of times going there that they rack up the check. For example. We ordered the branzino filet and the waiter said he was going to give us a little bit more than 1 order then on the bill it said 2 orders of branzino instead of 1 and 1/2 orders like it said on the shrimp luciano!!! When we walked in at 7:45 the place was more than half empty. The waiter pulled a fast one on us and made his slow night better. Not going to return for a long while!!!

Pretty basic old school Italian restaurant vibe. Everything is served family style which gave us (a party of 5) a great chance to try several dishes.  Here's my take on each of them. 

* House made white wine:  Some may find it a bit sweet but I loved how light it was considering how much we were about to eat!
*Bread basket:  they could make a bit more of an effort with the bread basket. It was pretty much the same bread you'd grab at stop and shop thrown in the oven for a few minutes.  Served with butter no oil.  Could be improved
*Tomato/ Mozz? /Pepper App:  Super fresh: Super delish!
*Baked Clams:  The clams themselves were  (like, really small) but were preapred perfectly and very tasty 
*Eggplant Rollatini:  Out of this world! 
*Pepe's special salad:  Passable Italian salad.  not bad/ not great 
*Linguini White Clam Sauce: Mixed reviews from the table on this one.  I loved it but the flavor was def mild.  Garlic was roasted so there wasn't much of a kick to the sauce but I like it that way.  Others at the table thought the flavor was a bit lacking.  Still the entire platter was finished in record time so I can't imagine the complaints accounted for much :) 
* Broccoli Rabe:  A bit bitter/ a bit charred as it should be. Others weren't crazy about it.  I thought it was done to perfection. 
* Veal scallopini:  I don't eat veal but the table all agreed they loved it. 
* Vanilla/ Chocolate Tartufo: Chocolate shell was really rich, ice cream was super creamy.  Perfect ending to a great meal


The added bonus of this place.....and possible the most important reason I loved this spot .....

I think it has to do with the family style dining and the larger parties that tend to gather here but several times I looked around and NO ONE (not a single person) in the place was on their phone!  Everyone was eating talking and enjoying the company of those they were dining with.  The staff interacted brilliantly with each table and this likely add to the fantastic environment.  

I only learned late in the meal that this place has a touch of fame based on HBO's show entourage.  Whether you're coming for that or based on a recommendation as I had, def a good night out especially if you have a large(ish) party.  

Expect the meal to be around $100 pp.  with drinks.  Seemed a fair price for all of the great food and excellent service
I think this restaurants should change the way they give you the checks, they should give it by machine so that way we can be sure what we really paying for .

Been to Don Peppe's quite a few times now and it's official...we love this place. I think people who are giving less than five stars are forgetting a few things...

Firstly, the decor is not representative of the food. If you're expecting a super upscale ambiance and dining experience, you're in the wrong place. The Food is so good this shouldn't matter...Close your eyes. Secondly, I read some derogatory things said about the waiters and staff...these guys are running themselves ragged, dealing with big crowds and tight spaces. Give them a break. 

When you go to Don Peppe's remember its family style, it's gonna take a while (good food usually does, Sundays are for family anyway so relax and enjoy), as others have said, they only take cash, and yes it is pricey but SO worth it.

This place reminds me of eating dinner at my Grandma's house, fresh, flavorful food, family and fun. The red house wine is so good and some standout dishes include the baked clams, shrimp luciano, veal or chicken Don Peppe, and the porterhouse! Bring your family and friends!

One Of the last of it's kind-like spotting a White Rhino on a Photo Safari- these places just don't exist anymore. The Food is Better Than Great- it's SPECTACULAR. Every bite of the stuffed clams, the chicken parm, the Linguini in clam sauce is to be cherished and remembered. Don't just bring an empty stomach- fast for a day before you go so you have enough room for the feast you are about to eat. Anyone who has anything bad to say about the Food just has ZERO taste- do not believe them.

I went to Don Peppe's for their baked clams. I was so exited that I gobbled it up before I remembered to take a picture. They were very tasty. I loved both their white and red clam sauce. Food was great! 

But their prices are extremely high and I find it ludicrous and unlawful that they only accept cash. It was interesting and slightly odd to see the cooks playing cards in the middle of the dinning room during dinner service. 

To be honest, there are many comparable restaurants in the tristate area. I went there for the experience and to check out all the hype. But I can eat locally for the same great tasting food at more reasonable prices.

Not worth your visit staff was rude very judgmental I don't know if these folks thought I couldn't afford my meal but nonetheless food wasn't that serious especially if your being watched upon while trying to enjoy it thumbs down

The Veal Don Peppe here is the best veal dish I have ever had. You can cut it with a spoon. The dining experience here is like no other. The service was very good and it provides such an authentic queens experience, you think you are in a movie. It's also somewhat close to the airport.

Not sure how this place has such high reviews.

1. About service...very rude...people saying because its busy yaddayadda. I went when they opened was empty. Still very rude.

2. Menu is on the wall... so if you're seated far from it...you'll look like a fool trying to read it. Also, price is different from online.

3. Price... I expected at most 60$ for my shrimp pasta and chicken... paid a little over 100$.

3.5. Quality.. 3/5 food was okay but the experience overall was not pleasant.

4. Took about 1hr for the food to come out... 

5. No olive oil for bread?

oh yeah... im not sure but there is a consistent loud noise/vibration...
best italian food in the planet. been going since 2000. veal don pepe's is out of this world.

I remember eating here years ago and we absolutely loved the food. This is our return trip after many years. Came here with another couple and we were very disappointed.  They are not accommodating at all. We asked for oil on the table for our bread and that was a complete no no.
We also asked for a salad with dressing on the side that was a no.  
The bread is nothing to write home about just regular old Italian bread.  
The food was just as good as any other pizzeria that we might go to.   This place is living on its reputation because there was nothing outstanding about anything that we ate.
baked clams stuffed mushrooms linguine with White clam sauce and chicken Parm all just average.
We are real foodies and eat out several times a week We like really good food. I put this on the average list
Simply put very good Italian food in a way too noisy setting for a bit more than I prefer to spend for a good meal.

It was very early, we were hours before boarding our flight. Where could we find a nice place to grab a meal? Yelp to the rescue. Did not disappoint! Wonderful Italian family style restaurant with horse racing memorabilia all around. Attentive staff. Freshly prepared and nice portions. Just the place to savor a great meal with those not traveling, before the "mall atmosphere" of a terminal in any airport in any state in the union these days. Good to experience the restful family dining atmosphere in these times. Thanks Yelp! I give a hearty recommendation! It is 4 stars since the front didn't seem inviting and they don't take plastic. I am glad we went!!

Been dinning here more than a decade. Food is the same but always good. Menu has never changed except for the price of course. I always go back because there are few dishes that are always awesome and I definitely don't mind paying high price for it. But after last Friday's lunch....... maybe that will be my last time there.
