How can you charge a bottle of beer for $10?!?!?! Seriously! I let you get away with cash only yet plus tax, waiters always round up the bill, surging dish prices because I love your food. But $10 for a bottle of peroni? You guys really disappointed me.........

I will not go back. this place is way overrated. i guess people that don't cook Italian go here since i learned from grandmothers from Italy and there food put rings around this place.  Also they charge you extra for everything, i ordered chicken scarpareillo and usually it comes with potatoes, peppers & onions. well after i ordered a double size i notice they added $21.00 to my bill. the waiter said that was for the peppers and onions. What, that makes no sense isn't that how it comes????? The wait service is not so friendly. food is over rated. i guess being Italian i know what real Italian food should taste like and it isn't like that. :(
Rude waiters food is good but overpriced not feeling this place anymore. Too many other places to be waiting for a table to be rushed and crowded. They can keep there clientele. I'll go elsewhere.

Ah the food was delicious, the menu is on the wall!

The baked clams and the red wine were by far my favorite but we also ordered an anti pasto salad, chicken marsala, shrimp marinara, chicken parm and linguine with clams. The portions are family style, great for sharing!

"Let me ask you a question. What horse do you got your money on for tomorrow?"

You're gonna hear things like that in this place. They make great food in here because its automatic to them ad they really don't care if you're dissatisfied because you must be outside your mind if have anything to complain about.

Real foodies know the deal. This place is the industry standard in this city and theres really no comparison.

Don Peppe's is on my exclusive Best Buds List for exciting my taste buds to point of unfilled consistency.

BEWARE THEY PAD THE BILL!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! RIP OFF PRICES!!!!!
Had dinner tonight and noticed a 19.00 additional charge on my bill.
Waiter said that was for chicken scarpariello which a 1/2 order is
22.00 and the 19.00 is for 1/2 sausage and some potatoes and peppers
First of all what Italian restaurant serves chicken scarpiello with out sausage, potatoes, and peppers included in the chicken scarpiello.
Google chicken scarpiello and you will see the ingredients.
The waiter lied to us and said our chcken scarpiello just is chicken
and nothing else..(wouldn't that just be chicken).
So at the end the 1/2 order of chicken scarpariello was 41.00, what a joke.
We also ordered pasta with meat sauce, tiny small portion was 18.00,
with hardly any meat in it, but at least it was on the blackboard menu
as pasta with meat sauce. We also had baked clams 12 tiny ones.27.00,
but again it is posted on the blackboard so we new the price before ordering.
Spoke with several friends who knew about this place and read lots of the
reviews and see that it is common for them to pad the bill.
Good thing it was just 2 of us and not a group of us, would never go back
to this CASH only restaurant, which we also knew about before coming. They round out the sales tax to the higher amount and still use handwritten paper receipts (guess they cheat the Sales Tax bureau.

If you go ask all questions and price first, ask for the sizes of the small portions, (its not family style unless its the full size portions which are all double the price), and read your paper bill when you get it.

Food was great, our waiter was patient! I will definitely return. I didn't get to take pictures of my food because it was so good I forgot to. This a family style restaurant. I give 4.5 stars. The only issue is all cash.

Went to this place for date night. Definitely a neighborhood classic. Everything is family style, so come with an appetite! Didn't have the signature linguine with clam sauce but will definitely be back to try it. House red wine is a must .. nothing fancy but definitely good eats.

Every dish was EXCELLENT!     We tried the baked clams, mozzarella with tomato AND roasted peppers, calamari (we had the entree as an appetizer and it was the tenderest I've ever had), baked ziti and chicken in lemon/butter sauce -- all delicious!   The water was okay, but other staff members were rude -- standing in front of the only menu in the place, a wall-board.  But the food was great.  A bit expensive, but worth it.  Cash only.
Outstanding chicken parmigiana. Great taste and service. Definitely recommend if you are in the mood for Italian.

Food is classic italian seafood, but I have to question the pricing and lack of customer service. They charge 28 dollars for shrimp luciano and don't tell you that it was an extra $14 for the noodles that the shrimp was served on top of... then they charge $10 for a pitcher of iced tea... with the baked clams at $27... our lunch bill with tax and tip came out to $100. Also it's cash only, but you wouldn't know that until the check came. I was fine with paying the bill, but the added undisclosed costs left a shady aftertaste. I guess its a place with a long history of neighborhood patronage, but it definitely didn't feel welcome to nonregulars. The dishes tasted fine but I didn't think it was worth a hundred dollars for a lunch for two.

Don Peppe - where do I even start?? Family style restaurant nestled in Ozone Park with some of the most delicious Italian food. This restaurant is always packed on the weekends for dinner. I usually come early to avoid to wait, or come during the lunch time. 
After you are seated, direct your attention to board on the wall where all the menu items are listed (there is no menu for the table, so don't wait for one!) I would recommend that you come hungry, and with a group of people so you can order several items and try it all. Be advised, their portions are quite large, so unless you're hungry (like I usually am), you might not be able to finish an order on your own - it's meant to be shared. 
For appetizer, I LOVE their baked littleneck clams. They come out piping hot with a perfect breadcrumb crunch on top (not soggy at all), and my favorite part is the drizzling a spoonful of garlic/clam juice over the top of the clams right before you eat it... SO GOOD.
For the entree, I love their linguine with white clam sauce. It is one of their most popular menu items and I can see exactly why. The linguine is perfectly cooked with lots of fresh clam meat just swimming in an abundance of their delicious white wine clam sauce. I also really like the Veal Don Peppe - a HUGEEE piece of breaded veal cutlet topped with chopped raw tomatoes, red onions and red peppers.
Earlier last month, the night before a big race, I came to Don Peppe to carb up with their spaghetti with meat sauce. I finished an entire portion by myself! Although I must say, I was a little bummed that they didn't have meatballs on their menu. 
Can't wait to come back here to try the Shrimp Luciano and their steak! Heard great things about those.
Note: this place is CASH ONLY
Second note: they are usually closed for the entire summer, I believe from July through September - and possibly other times throughout the year, so I would call to make sure they're open before making a trip over there.
Third note: their dress code - no hats, no tank tops
Quintessential Italian fare. They should adopt the Olive garden slogan because here, your really family. They will yell at you if you ask for french fries :)

This famous restaurant is overpriced, overrated and underwhelming. A $60 chicken scarparello was dry and over cooked. The service was surly, preemptive and almost intimidating. The house wine and Don Pepe salad was good. Any minor request to deviate from menu was rebuffed with a frown and a sneer. There are many wonderful Italian restaurants out there. Avoid this one

Old school at its finest.

The place has been here forever, you have to be very forgiving to give Don Peppe five stars. This is one of those red checked table cloth places that doesn't care about Yelp reviews, Food Critics or its flaws.
For example, you want wine? One White and One Red please. Both crafts of wine come out ice cold. You want menus, its all on the chalk board. Don't like it? Hit the Belt Parkway!

Listen, the owners don't give a flying F what anyone says. This is their joint, everyone heard about the baked clams. Theres a long line to try them so don't pitch a bitch. Eat and GTFO. Merry Christmas! Queens..

I put on my glasses to look at the menu board. Baked clams are a must. Linguini with clams are a must. My buddy orders Veal Parm, he doesn't know about the family style method. I'm gonna sit back and let him see how it all unfolds. 

The clams come out. They're good, a little too heavy on the bread crumbs for my taste but still rock solid. Where else are you getting baked clams half as good other than my house?! 

Next the linguini comes to our table. I was about to take a picture but the waiter starts serving us. I grab some red pepper and go to town on my linguini. Pasta from a box but damn that is pretty friggin' good! Tons of roasted garlic & oil, this is a feast in itself. It's allowing me to forget about the cold red house wine. 

I'm pretty packed but now? The Veal Parm comes to our table. The waiter starts serving it up. Pictures? Not happening here, what did they do in the 70s. If someone whipped out a camera, there would be trouble. I'm watching the kitchen staff and waiters interact from my seat. One of the cooks is vaping.. It's still an old skool joint but now with young chefs.

Anyhoo, the veal parm? Man.. that just brings me back. Old school dish still being served at Don Peps. 

If you're looking for an old school Italian joint, it doesn't get any better than Don Peppe. The customers and wait staff are far removed from Yelp. This is what they're serving and how they're serving it. Don't like it? Then don't come is the best how I can explain it.

Don Peps, I'll see you next year.

Great old school Italian spot. There will be a wait because it's a popular place but they have a nice waiting area in the front and the owner/host is friendly. 

The food is simple and delicious. I had the veal Don Peppe which was sooo crispy with a bruschetta topping - delicious. Then the rigatoni with sausage was solid. The pasta is cooked perfectly. The portions are definitely large. Baked clams are tasty and not overly breaded.

Yum!
I love Don Peppe. I have been here numerous times and it tastes better each time!! A must go place. The food is amazing and the service is even better.

Pricey, yes..
Family style food, yyyeeehhhhhh.. but on the small side....
Crowded, oooohhhhh yyeeehhhhh
Would i go back, YES lol

My recommendation... get the backed clams! lol. Get the pasta with broccoli.  skip the house wine. Small and over priced.  bread was amazing too. Honestly if i could have had just backed clams all night, i would have had that. The pasta was also amazing. Big chunks of garlic too. DELISH.  The seating is super cramped though. you and the table next to you have to take turns breathing so everyone fits hahahahaha but i would deff go back. maybe for an early dinner to avoid the crowds though.

Staff is super nice. our waiter was from Italy which made my husbands day because so is he.
Old school traditional Italian restaurant. My friend recommended this place and it did not disappoint. The food was great but the wine was even better.

If you want Italian food, this is the place to go!! My mouth is watering as I type this. The menu is in the wall which is very convenient. My best friend from South Carolina can't stop talking about it. 10's across the board!!

Best food ever! Never dissappointed when I come here. We got the chicken don pepe and linguine with white clam. Amazing. Always good and fresh. This place is old school italian. Love this place! Never leave

I have been going since I was a kid and no matter who tries to replicate it they just can't. Food is freaking amazing. Service is hit or miss however the food makes up for it every time. Baked clams and stuffed artichoke are a must

First time at Don Peppe and definitely not my last. From the moment you walk in you are treated as family with a smiling face and welcoming host. The waiters are just as friendly and helpful explaining that all the items on the menu are family style. The menu you pick from is located on the wall which is a little annoying for those who can't see but the waiters let you know what to order. 

Once the food came I was not disappointed. All the orders came in the perfect size for everyone to share and still be stuffed. The baked ziti, stuffed mushrooms, steak and cheesecake are amazing.  We even had leftovers to take home.

Tight space but we were still seated. The line through the door was frightening but it was worth the wait.  Come in earlier to avoid crowds.

Friendly staff and spacious restaurant. I hear they have lines out the door on weekends. We came on a Tuesday at 8:30pm and got seated straight away. My favorite dishes were the shrimp spaghetti (sauce was sooooo flavorful) and the lemon ice. It's a lemon sorbet served inside a hollowed lemon. It's sweet and tangy and the perfect ending to the meal.
Great,I mean really great Italian food. Everything super fresh, served family style . Very attentive staff.

Our first time here.  Food was GREAT but pretty PRICEY.  Old school Italian restaurant. Family style dishes.  Come early to avoid the wait.  Cash only.

Buyer beware.  The waiter did not mention the add-ons cost extra, like a lot extra.  So the bill come with a sticker shock.

Shrimp luciano is $28. Waiter asked if we wanted that with linguine.  That cost was another $14.  

Chicken scarpariello (1/2 order) is $22. Waiter asked if we wanted sausage with that. That cost another $19.  Mind you, I think there was one sausage in there.

The food here is good, no doubt about it and that is why I am giving it 3 stars. The dinning experience, not so good. This place is located in the middle of nowhere in South Ozone Park. I went there during the holidays and got very lucky and found a parking spot in front of the restaurant. I would think parking is a big problem here, I did not see a lot and there was no valet parking. The place was busy but I got a table for 2 immediately. There is a small cold atrium they use for a waitimg area that I would not like to spend any time in, no bar. The service was slow and the food crawled out. Nobody seems to like working there. Our waiter     was mostly unavailable. It took 2 hours to get out and both if us had the same dishes. I ordered another Diet Coke and it next came. I hear a lot if people complain about thier prices here on Yelp but they are not that expensive, the Oyster Bar in Grand Central is about 25% higher priced. I think most people I hear raving about this place just don't have access to the better places in NYC, it looks like most if them come in from Long Island. This place would not survive up on Aurther Avenue in the Bronx just based on the service and competition. To add insult to injury it is a cab only restaurant. Don't get me wrong, the food is fresh and very good but I have way too many options that include great food a friendly staff and a much better overall dinning experience. I won't return.
amazing service & amazing food, also great environment! 10/10 would for sure come back again!

If a business takes a two months long vacation and doesn't update Yelp and Google before doing so, I have to let the business know how unhappy we were to drive 30 minutes in an unfamiliar area for a wasted trip.

It isn't normal to close for two months.  When you do things that aren't normal, let the people know.  Yelp and Google make it very easy for business owners to update their hours info.

The decor isn't anything spectacular, it is very noisy, and you'll likely wait a while for a table. But that doesn't matter because the food is incredible, the staff is friendly, and did i mention the food is incredible? Been here twice and can't wait to go back again!
Great great food! It was even featured on entourage! The pasta and the veal parmigiana is great. The only downside this place has is that they do not accept food orders over the phone.

The food here is always perfect. Hot ,fresh and perfect timing for each course. Our waiter was great,we told him that we were waiting for one more person before we ordered,he was very understanding. I can't recommend anything because everything is delicious.Cash only and a little expensive,but we'll worth the price you pay.

I wanted to 100% adore this place. Felt like and looked like a place you'd see in a old movie. But some of the things we ordered were truly tasteless- specifically the $20 stuffed mushrooms. What exactly is their filling? I cannot believe they have the gall to charge such a price! It tasted like nothing. 
I will have to say the winner was the linguine with white clam sauce. That was divine. Spaghetti meat sauce, ehh okay. Chicken parm was good, not great. Stuffed clams were good. Seafood marina was borderline Terrible. The sauce lacked flavor and the seafood was a bit mushy. Spent a little over $200 for a lack luster meal. I don't get the hype. I'd go back for the linguine and nothing else.

The food was delicious! No doubt about it. Enough? Enough. However, I was seated at a table that was on the corridor of the ins and outs of the kitchen. If my chair was bumped into one more time, I was gonna scream. I don't eating like a galvone but I almost felt like i had to because once that last bite was done, my plate was whisked away. At about $100 pp, I want to be able to eat and enjoy my dinner like a lady. I didn't feel I was treated like a lady today, I felt rushed and cramped. Couldn't even enjoy a real conversation with the family. I'm glad I experienced it once. That will be it. I'm sure they could care less with the line out the door of people waiting to get in.

Dined here today with extended family and am so grateful for the warm hospitality we were shown. Food was absolutely delicious, service kind, efficient, and attentive, ambience upbeat, attractive, and comfortable. Great energy.  Thank you, all; looking forward to many returns!

This is really a neat little place with great foods and apparently grandfathered in for gambling card playing and smoking.

Be prepared to go for your lungs on price but the homemade wine is excellent the clams are great in fact any dish that you choose will be excellent

Food: 4/5
Came for my friends birthday dinner with 7 other people. We ended up ordering a bunch of dishes -linguine with white sauce, spaghetti with meat sauce, baked clams, stuffed shells, grilled calamari, veal peppe, sodas, beers and a bunch of different desserts.

Their linguine with white sauce was out of this world! It was the best clam sauce I've ever had. Their baked clams were also extremely delicious. They were perfectly baked and had the right texture with just the correct amount of bread crumbs.

The spaghetti with meat sauce wasn't that impressive. I've had better elsewhere. It was bland. The stuffed shells were just ok. I'm not a big fan of ricotta cheese but I've had better homemade shells. The grilled calamari was a big disappointment. It was way over cooked and lacked the supple texture. The veal peppe was just ok. It was fried and doused in tomato, onions and some sauce. By the time it reached our table, the fried texture was soggy and soft.

Service: 5/5
Our waiter was extremely courteous and accommodating. He made some great recommendations and he was very friendly.

Ambiance: 2/5
I was a little disappointed with the feel/vibe of this place. I've heard of Don Peppes before and was expecting more. It's very casual and laid back. No hats, tank tops (for men), baby strollers or credit cards allowed. I felt a bit overdressed. 

Overall: 4/5
This is a no frills, family style Italian restaurant with the best baked clams and linguine with white sauce! I would definitely recommend those two dishes to anyone who wants to give this place a try. I wouldn't recommend anything else. The bill was roughly $500 for our table.

Best. Linguine. With white sauce. Ever.

Totall average " Italian America " I grew up eating this style my whole life eating in the 5 Boros. Nothing was great. Had everything from baked clams over cooked stuffed artichoke no flavor just stuffed with regular bread crumbs and undercooked ( ex. No taste of cheese or even hint of anchovies ) all pastas we're average... veal parm lost in an ocean of tomato sauce.. google best Italian in Brooklyn or Manhatten for real Italian food not what I had which is totally average Americanized Italian ... disclaimers I do know this style of everything made into a parmagiana is what we all grew up on as 2nd and 3rd generation Italians but this is an average example.  Any local pizza/ or casual Italian can do the same dishes ... maybe it has a long run so that gives it nostalgia? If that's the case spend some money and at least make the bathroom look like it isn't condemned... ps never drank a whole bottle of house wine and didn't feel a buzz ( 2 options there overpriced house wine or a bottle of 110 amorone ) sorry being honest... I know it is not Marea in nyc or Lillia in Brooklyn that I should be comparing this too because that is real serious Italian ... sorry the Don is average at above average prices ...for what I ate.

What can I say, classic New York Italian restaurant. If you like great authentic Italian food This is the place. The portions are family sized but the link weenie with clam sauce was so good I ate the whole thing.

I have been dining here since I was a little girl and it will always be one of my favorites. The food is just so yummy. Their linguini with clams is my go to. I hate having to share it! It is a great place to come with your family to eat and catch up.

I have been coming to Don Peppe my whole life and have always loved the service and food. My family and I came on a Saturday night during what we thought would be prime-time dinner. We were surprised to see that the restaurant was half-empty but we didn't think twice about it.

We ordered the Veal Don Peppe, the Linguini with clams, the stuffed artichoke, and baked clams. 

The artichoke was the most successful dish of the night as it is nothing short of amazing. The stuffing is plentiful and the sauce is divine. A perfect appetizer for a large meal. The baked clams were also very good and tasty. The Linguini with clams was kind of underwhelming as it could have used a bit more seasoning and maybe a bit more flavor. Lastly, the Veal Don Peppe, (what drew us back here for 20+ years). The flavor and crust of the veal is awesome, but the veal itself was a bit tough. It use to be that you can cut the veal with a spoon and this fell far short of that. 

The reason I deducted 2 stars is because our waiter wasn't all that attentive and didn't seem like he enjoyed serving us and the food was hit or miss in some areas.

Don Peppe is a staple in Queens and it would be difficult to deter me away as I still enjoy the food and experience.

Came here Sunday, May 26th, 2019. The Sunday before Memorial Day. Was terrified, because everyone said this place has a crazy wait, which can be up to 2 hours, and they don't take reservations. Walked in the door and was seated within about 3 minutes.

As for food, went to order wine, but they only do by the bottle not by the glass, and since my friend doesn't drink wine we were able to get any. That's alright though, always next time. 

We ordered the stuffed artichoke, but unfortunately they didn't have any. So we settled for baked clams, linguini in white clam sauce, and finally chicken francese. 

The baked clams were delicious, but the sauce needed a little something. Would give them 4.5 out of 5. The linguini in white clam sauce was easily a 5, one of the best in the state. The chicken francese was in a rather pink sauce, but was very good. Came with 3 pieces. 4 out of 5. 

For dessert, we had the tartuffo and two capuccinos. Was a very good way to end the dinner. 

Only reason this place isn't 5 out of 5 is no reservations, and it was a little pricey. Paid around $150 after tip for 2 people.

This was not my first time here, but I was excited to bring my son and niece here to enjoy the food . The pasta with clam sauce was pasta with " where's the clams ? So disappointing and the artichoke had a tough burnt outside and a dab of stuffing . I just felt embarrassed for talking up the restaurant, and felt like I wasted money on not much enjoyment.

This is my go to restaurant when I am in the area. I normally have a rule not to eat at the same place twice when on work trips, but I break it every time with Don Peppe. The service is great too even on nights when they are slammed.
Delicious food. I would go back just for the food. Horrible service. Dirty. Needs to be renovated. I was so grossed out walking into the bathroom.

Not really worth it. I went because of the mention from my favorite HBO series, but the food was mediocre and the person waiting our table was a bit on the rude side. Won't be going back but it's mostly due to the food. Wasn't that tasty. And the price for a soda was insane.

Ok first, big attitude as if they bothered by being a waiter.   
Second,  bread not authentic lacked density and crust.  Had better flavors of food at local pizza joint    Will not be going back.   And worst don't think they care

If the place was 1/10th as good as the owners think it is it might be ok.  Felt like a mediocre Buca di Beppo franchise.  Let's start with the bread.  Crust too thin and flaky and served with prefab butters in little plastic containers. Next the "wine."   The white tastes like muscat.  The red tastes like grape juice.  For the salad, there is just a prefab pepper on the table.  No wanna be wise guy who pays cash only eats salad without fresh ground pepper.  The menu is pretty basic Italian fare.  Still they were out of several items when I was there.  Chicken Parmesan was decent-similar to what you can find at virtually any mom and pop Italian restaurant in the greater ny area.

This is and has been my favorite restaurant for 40 years. Nothing fancy but great food and portions. House wine works. I'm there every Sunday for dinner and it's always my way to say goodbye to the weekend.

I've been going to don Peppe my whole life except in the past 12 years since I moved to Florida. Decided to go there on my way to JFK this recent visit to NY. Food was not as good as I recalled and either was the service. We arrived on the early side for dinner so seating not a problem. However shortly after the place filled up and we were Sandwiched between two large tables . It got real noisy and I started to feel claustrophobic! Overall it was a pricey dinner for two and I can't say I would go out of my way to drop by again.

Don't understand all the great reviews. The only reviews that come close are the bad ones. Tried Don Peppe on a Friday night, first and last time ever eating there. Waiter had major attitude, Food not that good, only house wine and Extremely, EXTREMELY! Over priced.
Their food was fantastic! It's a must try, but remember to walk with cash as they don't accept cards.

Best. Baked. Clams. In. Queens. The veal dishes are tremendous as well. A spot you want to go to with a couple friends at least. The portions are substantial, you want to get a variety of plates on the table, and then be happy with a bountiful doggy bag. Probably out of the way for nearly everyone who dines here, and that's a testament to just how good the joint is. And they still don't open up on Mondays. Tip top.
Best baked clams and best linguine and clam sauce.   Their shrimp Luciano over linguine is a must.   Amazing chicken scarpiello.   All the dishes are so amazing so going more than once is a must!

This is my favorite Italian restaurant. Love the garlic infused 'real deal' Italian food. Love the local family atmosphere.  Don Pepe has given special treatment to returning Marines. As a Marine veteran I appreciate their patriotism and care for Veterans. The food is the best and reasonably priced. No credit cards so take a wad of cash. If going to JFK or Belmont, it's right next door. Don't hesitate to make a special trip. It's worth it!
Great food, old school Italian joint with family style servings, veal don pepe is great, baked clams are a must!! If you don't believe me... just ask Vincent Chase !

I came to the restaurant on Saturday night with a group of  8 friends.  The wait was long but we did not leave because we were hungry.  That was the worst mistake we ever made.  If I could give this restaurant a negative  10 rating, I would.  We were seated an hour later.  The waiter had the worst attitude I have ever experienced.  He read us that Riot Act!  He said, it is Family Style and  "CASH ONLY" and if don't like that, you can leave. Then he goes around and takes the orders.  If it is a family style restaurant and we ordered 2 salads and 6 dishes, why would he want to know how many people are going to be eating each dish???  He insisted on knowing how many people were going to be eating each dish.  When we said to him why does that matter and that we had to figure it out, he got angry and nasty. Meanwhile, he told us that under no circumstance, can we order additional food once the order is put in. FINE!!!  That would have been OK, if my husband and I, who only eat vegetarian, got a normal size family style order of Eggplant Parmigiana. But it wasn't and we were still hungry.  I called the waiter over and said that this was not a family style portion and we were still hungry. I asked him if we can order one Baked Ziti.  He screamed at me and said "ABSOLUTELY NOT!!! I TOLD YOU BEFORE THAT YOU CANNOT ORDER ANYTHING ADDITIONAL ONCE THE ORDER GOES IN!!!  Never in my life have I ever been so humiliated and angry.  WE WILL NEVER COME BACK TO THIS PLACE AND WE WILL ADVISE PEOPLE AGAINST GOING TO EAT THERE.

First time trying this place and was pleasantly surprised . Nice big family style menu. Baked clams and mixed seafood on red sauce were great appetizers. Pasta with shrimp was delicious as was the veal topped with bruschetta . Desserts were yummy also . Only con for me was it was way too bright , I like restaurants a big dimmer .
The best Italian restaurant in all of New York Best baked clams I've ever eaten  veal chop special is to die for

One of the best ever. Here's why:
1. Family style. (Everything comes out on a platter and you share it.)
2. Want wine? You've got it. Red or white. That's the only selection. They bring it out to you in an old liter Coke bottle. Not the best wine, but who cares?
3. Seafood salad -- the best ever. My dad says, "It's the best in America." And he's had a lot of them! Incredibly tender.
4. Veal marsala -- outstanding. Maybe the best ever.
5. Right next the airport. 5 minutes to the front gate.

I had dinner last night at Don Peppe, with 3 other people and a 3 year old child, and was very disappointed. The menu is on the wall. The food is served family style. We ordered one appetizer (house salad), linguine with white clam sauce, chicken parmigiana and an order of string beans. The waiter was extremely rude. The service was poor. The waiter doubled our order and we didn't know until we received the check, because he said there were 4 people and the platters only serve 2. So, when we received the check it was not what we had expected to pay. The check was hand written, with numbers crossed out. The bill was clearly inflated. It's a cash only place. I fine dine a lot but unfortunately this place was far from a fine dining experience. The bread tasted stale and the food was just "okay"at Don Peppe. There are plenty of better options in Howard Beach and Ozone Park that offer an excellent meal with much better service at affordable prices.

Often copied, never quite duplicated. Still the king with the best baked clams and linguini white clam sauce. Always enjoy the house red and salad. Only drawbacks are the cash only and tough to find street parking. Otherwise, as good in this century as it was in the last.
Amazing food however the waiter was a piece of shit. My bill was 200$ and I left him 230$, he said I was short meaning I didn't tip him enough. Pttuuuu u dirty prick, you should get fired!!

This place came highly recommended but was a total disappointment. The calamari in marinara was edible, although the sauce was bland and watery. The pasta with prosciutto was a joke. We managed to find one tiny cube of overcooked prosciutto on the platter and the sauce was the same as on the calamari - bland and watery. The desserts were straight from a warehouse store. (In all fairness, the waiter said that they didn't make them in house so we should have known better.) The cappuccino was okay but heavily covered in cinnamon. We had to ask 3 times for water and 2 times for cheese with the pasta course. The ladies room is one step up from the average bus station. The prices are ridiculous, given the quality of the food and the level of service. With all the Italian restaurants in the area, this one is a hard pass.

Oh man, I can't stop thinking about the Shrimp Luciano. It was so delicious! The shrimp was very fresh and the sauce was pure decadence - buttery and luscious with a touch of wine and a beautiful tinge of orange color. I noticed that almost every other table ordered this dish as well. Just be aware that it's pretty pricey to dine here, expect to shell out at least $50 a head (before wine).

We also tried the Eggplant Rollatini appetizer which was surprisingly savory for a vegetarian dish and came with a delicious marinara sauce. I would definitely come back here when I am in town (and on company dime) to try out the other dishes.

99% is the reviews said to order the Linguini w Clams in White Sauce. I ordered it and it was absolutely amazing. To whoever is reading this next-look no further and order the white sauce linguini. Trust the crowd! One serving is enough for two people. For app, we got the artichoke and it was quite good too.

We went Saturday 12/27 with four people. Let me say from the start, the food was very good. We ordered chicken, lemon and butter. Mike, our waiter, said , "4 pieces?" . We said yes. When the bill came the chicken was $45. We asked how many pieces was in an order.  He said, "3 pieces". 3 pieces for 1 order was $30. When we asked how is it $45 for 4 pieces Mike said "Ask the owner."
We ordered an order and a half for linguine and white clam sauce. It was more like garlic and oil. Very good but there were very little clams.
Anyway, the bill came to $205 without alcohol and we had four separate dishes.
Very pricey for italian food. Buyer beware ordering food.

All the food at Don Peppe is always delicious. The best mussels in white wine sauce ever! Get the shrimp Luciano. I can just dip my bread in the Luciano sauce and have that for dinner. The linguini with white clam sauce was also great! The veal don Peppe is veal Milanese with bruschetta on top and the veal is always perfect! For apps we had baked clams, a salad and eggplant rollatini. The chicken scarpariello comes with sausage, potatoes and peppers. I had it the next day because I was already stuffed and it was great the next day! We were there for a bday so for dessert we ordered a tiramisu, cannoli, Italian cheesecake and a pistachio tartufo. Everything we ordered was excellent. If you want delicious authentic Italian food this is definitely one of the best options in Queens. There are no mixed drinks just house wine. It's sweet and strong and perfect with their food. Make sure you bring cash they don't take credit cards.

As one of the most famous restaurants in the borough, Don Peppe has become a perennial destination for anyone who enjoys the old school Italian experience in seemingly one of the most Italian parts of NYC (#1). Not much has changed since they've opened close to 50+ years ago from Kings County; we're still quite lucky to have them.

The decor feels more random than it does antiquated. There are bright lights in all corners of the dining room, which is littered with group friendly tables covered in white tablecloths. Just outside of the door are a series of benches, presumably for people to sit on while they wait out their turn during the busy evenings and weekends. There are race car / sports memorabilia hanging all throughout the walls while waiters in white collared shirts and ties service loud groups from all walks of life.

Make no mistake, this is a place to feast. There are big plates and family style servings, this is the kind of place to celebrate food with lots of it. The menu is on the wall and people with weak eyesight might strain to see the board depending on which area of the room they're sitting in. 

Their linguini with white clam sauce ($29) might be their most famous dish and with good reason: it's very good. If one is not a fan of the white clams, then this dish might not impress. I always recommend a double order since it might be the first dish to get cleaned out.

I've enjoyed a number of other things on the menu: veal marsala, veal parm, linguini with red clam sauce, tomahawk steak, broccoli rabe with sausage, and filet of sole. I have to be honest and say their chicken dishes have almost all been a miss for me but especially the chicken with lemon & butter, chicken scarpariello, and the semi-laughable chicken chinese. The baked clams are solid, but they're a bit on the tiny side and it's hard to justify $30 for a small pile of shells.

The service is no frills and feels extremely casual. Waiters are more apt to joke around with folks rather than be stiff and professional. I've noticed mostly men making up the wait staff and I found their "rules of entry" to be quite amusing. They include: no tank tops, hats, baby strollers, or credit cards. Yes, you read that right -- this is a cash only establishment. Given the prices, bringing some serious green is definitely recommended.

We started out with red house wine, which was delicious and was constantly being refilled. Then we got salad, baked clams, a couple pastas and veal. The salad was perfectly dressed, fresh and crunchy. The baked clams are the best I've ever had; light and buttery. Pastas and veal were solid.

Where Don Peppes is special, is it's overall vibe. If you are expecting a fancy, romantic meal, go elsewhere. If you take yourself too seriously and have thin skin, go elsewhere. I got yelled at at one point because I was going to serve myself (the waiters bring out big bowls of food, then serve it to each individual person).
